# Phase E4: TypeScript nodes on the box, on MicroQuickJS - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for
> tracking.

**Goal:** A TypeScript node runs in the Pico box's plan, beside the C++ ones, on MicroQuickJS (mquickjs), and
BlipToaster's MIDI policy becomes such a node. A package's manifest marks a script pack for the device; the build
compiles its TypeScript to ES5 and to mquickjs bytecode, held by a toolchain that refuses what the engine lacks and
holds Node's output and the engine's to the same transcript; the same `defineNode` serves every pack, written in the
engine's subset. A second, small script host (`MqjsHost`) runs a device pack on the desktop and on the box, one engine
context per pack, its memory a package's own block in the plan's arena that the exporter and the loader size and place
like everything else. The box's plan becomes `rp.device.midi-in` -> `rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy` (TypeScript) ->
`rp.n8.nes`, with every behaviour and gate count E3's, and `rp-device-check` runs a script pack, a script plan and a
bench on the RP2350. Every desktop suite is bit-identical; the goldens that change on purpose are the `[packages]` golden
(`rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy` at the end of every product's row), `box-plan.hex` and two new goldens; nothing else is
re-recorded.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md), whose section 11 ("As
built") records the build and which Task 5 lands, sections 1 to 9 corrected in place. Task 1 vendors mquickjs at
`6d4d7eb` (`deps/mquickjs`, upstream's files unpatched, built by `cmake/mquickjs.cmake`), rewrites `defineNode` and its
helpers in the engine's subset with the device-pack refusals, adds the device-pack toolchain
(`packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs`) and the manifest's `retroplug.script` member, with
`packages/devtest/ts` as the seed pack; Task 2 adds the script host (`packages/graph-runtime/native/src/script/`:
`MqjsHost`, our standard library and table, the runner `retroplug-mqjs-run`) and package-level memory in the node SDK
(`rp_package`'s `memory` and `ctx`, `rp.host.packages/1`) and the loader; Task 3 adds the engine wrapper (the symbol
rename, five fixes guarded by a configure-time hash), sizing at the target's width, the device runtime bundle, `idle:
"skip"` and `forward()`, the `bliptoaster` pack, and the box running it from a 64 KiB arena with its bytecode in flash;
Task 4 runs the devtest pack through `rp-device-check` (a script plan judged by its digest, a bench, the stack in two
phases); Task 5 lands the docs.

**Tech stack:** C++20 and C (desktop GCC 13.3; the devcontainer's `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1 with newlib and its
libstdc++), MicroQuickJS at `6d4d7eb` (vendored, MIT), CMake (`file(GENERATE)` registrations, custom targets that run
the toolchain and the exporter at build time, a configure-time hash guard), Node with esbuild and the repo's pinned
TypeScript 5 for the toolchain, the Pico SDK 2.1.1 with TinyUSB 0.18.0 and Pico-PIO-USB at `5a37a66`, Catch2, the
TypeScript mock tier and `test-native`, pnpm workspaces for the one new member. No submodule moves. **No implementer
touches the hardware**: the Pico gate and the one flash of `rp-device-check` are the controller's, in Task 6.

**Spec:** [modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md). The main design's Phase E outline is
[modular-graph-design.md](modular-graph-design.md) section 8; E1's design, whose device build the host uses, is
[modular-graph-phase-e1-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e1-design.md); E3's design, whose loader, box host and gate E4
builds on and is held to, is [modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e3-design.md) (section 12.7), and
E3's plan, the previous one executed this way, is [modular-graph-phase-e3-plan.md](modular-graph-phase-e3-plan.md).

**Provenance:** every code block below was built and run before this plan was written, on the scratch branch
`proto/e4-mqjs` in this worktree, on top of the design commit cce581aa8: five commits, one per task (Task 6 is the
acceptance run and commits nothing), with GCC 13.3 on linux-x64 (a Ryzen 9 9950X, 32 threads). A block that creates a
file is that file as the prototype commit left it; one that changes it is the prototype's diff for it, so `git apply`
it from the step's text (or apply it hunk by hunk with the Edit tool). The vendored engine is the one exception: its 34
upstream files are placed by a `git archive` of the pinned upstream commit from a local checkout and proved by their
tree hash, not quoted. E4 moves and deletes no file. Each code task's verification is the stage's last full run of
`/tmp/e4pro/tip-verify.sh` with the legs its review fix passes ran again (each task's suites step says which run each
figure is from); Task 4's is the final verification (`/tmp/e4pro/s4g-*.log`), run at the prototype's code. Every
expected pass, test count and figure is quoted from the stage reports in /tmp/e4pro, those logs, the design's record or
the hardware gate's logs and record, which is what the generator checks; a figure no log records is said to be so, and
the step asks for it. When this plan was generated it was replayed in a scratch clone of cce581aa8, every block written
or applied in order, and each task committed with the command given: each commit's tree came out exactly as the
prototype's, and each commit message as its. The prototype commits, by task:

- Task 1 `51bd5a5f3`: defineNode in MicroQuickJS's subset, and the device-pack toolchain.
- Task 2 `675fb00e8`: The MicroQuickJS script host, and package memory in the SDK and the loader.
- Task 3 `d293071ed`: The bliptoaster pack and the box: the cart's MIDI policy as a TypeScript node.
- Task 4 `d17acf27a`: rp-device-check with a script pack: the devtest pack's nodes on MicroQuickJS, a script plan
  and a bench.
- Task 5 `996b9b850`: the docs. Task 6 is the acceptance run and commits nothing.

**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (cce581aa8).** The design was written before the prototype;
this plan follows what was built, and Task 5 lands the design with section 11's record and sections 1 to 9 corrected
in place. In short:

- **The user's decisions** (`.superpowers/e-pico/decisions.md`, the E4 entries; design section 2): TS nodes on the
  box are MIDI- and event-rate logic, audio DSP staying C++; a pack marked for the device runs on mquickjs on the
  desktop too, in a second, small script host beside the QuickJS one, desktop-only packs staying on QuickJS; each
  pack the box lists is compiled at the firmware's build and embedded beside the exported plan, the box registering
  its types at boot and the blob naming script types by id (no format change; trusted because only the build makes
  it); mquickjs and the bytecode run from RAM like the rest of the image, the 128 KiB arena shrinking toward the box
  plans' need, cold code back to flash only as a reserve lever; one context per pack, its heap declared in the
  manifest, sized and placed by the exporter and the loader, a heap that runs out, a throw or an overrun silencing
  only that pack's nodes; one `defineNode` in the mquickjs subset for every pack, a device pack's definitions
  refusing audio ports and anything asynchronous; and a `bliptoaster` pack holding the cart's policy in place of
  `rp.core.midi-filter` in the box's plan. At the gate the user chose **latency A**: accept the script node's cost
  on the MIDI path, the regression line moving to E4's measured figures. The user then **left every remaining
  decision to the controller overnight**, the plan's acceptance included. The controller's calls before that (stages
  1 to 3, with the user reachable) and after it (stage 4's review, overnight) are marked below.
- **`heapBytes` is the box's 32-bit context, and 3/2 is a heuristic.** The design counted one width; the 64-bit
  engine uses about twice the 32-bit one for objects, but not for payload bytes (`bliptoaster` 1.64 under full
  SysEx) and less for floats. So the manifest's `heapBytes` (a whole number from 4096 to 524288) is the box's
  context, the authority; the exporter sizes a pack at the target's width (`query_target`, `sizePlan(...,
  targetPointerBytes)`, `blob::kTargetPointerBytes` = 4); a 64-bit device build (the exporter's trial load, every
  device-mode test) gives 3/2 of it (`kDeviceHalves`), as the toolchain's check does ("the check would pass X"); the
  desktop's hosts give a context of at least 1 MiB (`desktopContextBytes()`, four times `heapBytes` past 256 KiB),
  since a desktop re-plan holds two instances of a pack for a while (the controller's call at Task 2 gave the
  desktop twice the declaration and the trial load exactly it; Task 3's width rule made those 3/2 and the floor).
  The least context is 4096 bytes at 64 bits and 2560 at 32, refused in words before the engine sees it. The box's
  boot line and the device check give the real figure.
- **Every node context runs the device runtime bundle.** The toolchain bundles a pack twice: the whole pack (64-bit
  only, the desktop's control context: registration, the descriptors, `parseSettings`, `layout_for`) and its
  **device runtime** (`RP_DEVICE_RUNTIME`: each definition kept as `{id, ports, create, layout, idle}`, the trimmed
  SDK; `bliptoaster`'s 32-bit runtime is 6,988 bytes, where the stage measured about 25.7 KB with the whole SDK), at
  64 bits and with `-m32`. Every node's context, on the desktop, in the trial load, in every device-mode test and on
  the box, loads the runtime; the runner holds both bundles to the same output digest and the same default layouts,
  which found a real difference (the runtime's layout dropped `exclusive`), now fixed. A pack that calls
  `parseSettings` or `descriptor` at module scope is refused at build.
- **The bytecode stays in flash and each context gets a private copy.** The image keeps the pack's relocatable
  bytecode in `.flashdata` (which `copy_to_ram` leaves in flash); setup copies it into the pack's block in the arena
  and relocates it there, right after `JS_NewContext` and before any atom exists in RAM, against the firmware's own
  stdlib (relocation rebinds every unique string by content, so the compile-time stdlib does not matter). Running
  writes into the bytecode (a string constant used as a key is marked unique in place), so no two contexts can share
  one copy, and the build cannot relocate it. A pack's block is `[host state, 448 reserved][its bytecode][its
  context]`, each 8-aligned; the box's pack is 32,016 bytes (448 + 6,992 + 24,576).
- **Pools at queue capacity, 64-place queues and a 64 KiB arena.** A node's input pools are made to its queue's
  capacity at its first block (the controller's call), so a pack's heap is fixed by the plan and the trial load
  measures it; the box's `rp.device.midi-in` carries **64 messages** (`RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES` 256 to 64; still
  4096 bytes, so a 4 KB SysEx is one message), since the policy's pools follow its input (42,192 bytes at 256 places
  and 19,296 at 64, at 32 bits), and the staging leaves what does not fit for the next pass, so nothing is lost. The
  arena is **65536** bytes (E3: 131072); the export's estimate for the box's plan is 57,288, and the box loads it
  into 56,632. The image takes 347.5 KiB (355,824 bytes) of the 512 KiB SRAM, the engine 98.7 KB of it at -Os.
- **`idle: "skip"` and `forward()`** (the controller's call, before the user's latency decision: both latency
  levers). A definition may declare `idle: "skip"`: the host returns before entering the context on a block with no
  message on any events or bytes input, no change on any control input or param, no hook waiting and the same
  `rp_process` as the node's last call; the first block always runs, and a definition with an audio port or nothing
  to wake it is refused. `forward(port, message)` is `send(port, message.frame, message.data, message.flags)` read
  natively for a message the running block handed out. Both hosts honour both; `bliptoaster` uses both.
- **The re-entry cap of 4, the scaled deadline and the stack guard** (the controller's calls, overnight). C calls
  back into JavaScript (`replace`, `forEach`) nest through `JS_Call` at about 290 bytes of the box's 4 KB stack a
  level, and the device check's nest at the engine's default 8 read 3320 of 4096; so a node's context is capped at
  **4** re-entries after its load (`RP_MQJS_MAX_REENTRIES`), and the box builds with `PICO_USE_STACK_GUARDS=1`. The
  deadline is the engine's interrupt against the host's clock: **10 ms a call plus 250 us for each message** a block
  hands in on the box (26 ms for a full queue of 64), the desktop with no clock timing by thread CPU time at 500 ms
  with no allowance (Windows counts thread time in 15.6 ms ticks); the pool build is outside it.
- **The engine wrapper** (`packages/graph-runtime/native/src/script/`, never an edit of `deps/mquickjs`):
  `rp_mqjs_names.h` renames the engine's 197 external names to `rp_mqjs_*`, since every desktop product now links
  mquickjs beside QuickJS and 46 names clashed (`cmake/mquickjs-names.cmake` checks the library defines no other,
  Linux and macOS); `rp_mqjs_engine.c` includes `mquickjs.c` whole and carries five fixes as wrappers: two upstream
  GC bugs (the run-time name table corrupting itself when a collection lands in its own growth, and a loaded
  bytecode's names dropping out of it at the next collection) and three swallowed exceptions
  (`String.prototype.replace`'s callback, `string_buffer_puts`' out-of-memory, `hasOwnProperty`'s key; the
  controller's call, overnight), with typed arrays made in the engine with no `JS_Call`, so `messages()` works at
  any depth. **The fixes are guarded by a configure-time hash** of each upstream span they rest on and a count of
  `js_call_rec_count`'s mentions (exactly 4), so a bump of the pin that changes one fails the configure; the first
  GC fix has no test that reaches its condition, so the hash is its only guard. `rp_mqjs_device.c` wraps `abort`
  (newlib's reaches `_malloc_r`, which the trap forbids) to the SDK's panic, a forced-include shim gives the
  `PRI*64` macros the freestanding `<stdint.h>` lacks, and `cmake/device-image/no-unwind.c` in every device image
  replaces the ARM unwinder that newlib's `setjmp.o` drags in through `.ARM.exidx` with a trapping
  `__aeabi_unwind_cpp_pr0` (3,840 bytes of the box's RAM; the controller's call, overnight). The trap still wraps 87
  symbols, and no frame passes 1 KiB with no exemption.
- **The prototype's own staging moved stage 2's review items into Task 3.** Stage 4's review placed the three
  swallowed exceptions, the re-entry cap, the per-message deadline and `messages()` without a `JS_Call` in stage 2,
  but everything they extend (the rename header, the first-argument trick, the hash guard, the host's warm path)
  first exists in stage 3, so they landed in Task 3's commit; Task 2's commit is byte-identical to its reviewed
  state. The consequence for this plan is Task 3's verification, which its suites step explains.
- **`rp-device-check` on a script pack** (Task 4). `rp.devtest.script-nest` nests `replace` callbacks to the cap,
  reads and forwards its messages there and parses JSON at the deepest level; `script-plan.json`
  (`rp.device.midi-in` -> `script-transpose` -> `script-nest` -> `rp.devtest.digest`) is exported at the image's
  arena and judged by its digest against the desktop's exactly (it hears messages alone, integers); a bench times
  the transpose with the DWT cycle counter beside the XIP cache's counters; the pack's report; and the stack is
  judged in two phases (the load, the blocks), each against 4096 bytes with 512 kept for interrupts.
  `RP_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES_<package>` gives an image its own heap for a pack (devtest 40960), refused in words where it
  would size nothing; `retroplug_product`'s `NO_SCRIPTS` is retired.
- **The gates.** The prototype's gate ran on four images. The first (8ec41346) loaded the plan and the pack on the
  device, then failed to boot three times at the menu handshake; an E3 control image failed identically and the
  video showed no signal, so it was not E4's code, and its cause is unknown (it did not recur after a clean 12 s off
  and 35 s). On ae291e38 (idle skip and `forward()` in; its upload leg was refused by `loop.sh`'s staleness guard,
  as designed, and ran on the next image) and ec6cb4c0 every leg that ran passed but the known `[stats]`-print stall
  outlier (ec6cb4c0's full `stress.sh` read 778/8110 once), with latency averages near E3's and worsts about 50 us
  higher; the user's decision A accepted that. The last full gate, on fdbce8ba (the stage 4 fix pass): the boot with
  `plan loaded: 3 nodes, 56632 of 65536 arena bytes`, `pack bliptoaster, 32016 bytes` and its heap 11,636 of 24,576
  after the first block (load 9,613 us, first block 1,016 us); `stress.sh`'s 33 functional cases ok, its latency
  runs 743/1166, 664/1124, 719/1166 and 667/1125 us, and one 901/10581 run whose outlier is the known
  `[stats]`-print stall (E3's flash image read 12.6 ms in the same window); A4 and C5 identical (440.30 and 522.16
  Hz); `faults.sh` 8 of 8 on the re-run, the first run's one stuck round the plug's short-off quirk (a 2.9 s
  effective off); the upload and pick in 4,922 and 4,926 ms. `rp-device-check` (2126adf5) flashed once: 22 types,
  the N8 protocol, the plan as E3's (54,408 arena bytes, digest `46e21691` against the desktop's `b8854b2c`), the
  bench (a first block 1.1 ms, an empty block 67 us, 65 us a note, 48 us a 64-byte SysEx, 150 MHz from flash), the
  script plan (87,416 arena bytes, digest `c7248a64d500e6d8`, the desktop's), devtest's heap 22,084 of 40,960, the
  stack 2,176 at load and 2,360 in the blocks. The final images (box `c554df45`, check `0387a668`) differ from the
  gated ones by 32 bytes of a range check and were never on the rig: **Task 6's gate is their first** (the
  controller's call, overnight: acceptance gates the final image rather than a re-gate of the prototype). The
  regression line, a worst above about 1200 us or averages above about 780 us, is the stage 5 writer's choice that
  the controller accepted overnight, beside the user's decision A, which accepted the measured figures (averages of
  550 to 743 us and worsts of 1122 to 1170 us across the images).
- **The controller's other calls** (`results.md`), beside those marked above: a `device: false` script member is
  refused as reserved (stage 1, the user reachable); the 10 ms deadline is the box's and the desktop gets its own
  default (stage 2); on the desktop a pack whose heap ran out is torn down after its last node and set up again
  (stage 2's fix review); and acceptance gates the final image rather than a re-gate in the prototype (stage 4's fix
  pass 2, overnight).
- **The plan review's fixes, and the order of execution** (the controller's calls, overnight;
  `.superpowers/e-pico/decisions.md`, "E4 plan review fixes"). The order is E3's: Tasks 1 to 5, the code reviews,
  the follow-up commits they bring, **then** Task 6's acceptance at the follow-ups' tip. The first follow-up fixes
  `mqjs-run/main.cpp:104` (above). A derived or predicted figure (the ground rules list them) that differs while the
  exit status matches the plan is reported and execution continues; a different exit status or a tree-check failure
  still stops. The 1200 / 780 us regression line is marked as the stage 5 writer's choice the controller accepted.
- **The counts, start to end:** `retroplug-device-mode-test` from the baseline's 45 cases (4649 assertions) to 45
  (Task 1), 66 (Task 2), 76 (Task 3) and 84 (1,628,820) at Task 4, 39 of them `[script-pack]`;
  `retroplug-engine-graph-test` from 333 cases to 334 at Task 3 (the QuickJS skipper); `pnpm test` from 174 files
  and 1782 cases to 175 files (Task 1's `graph/device-pack`, 7 cases, 9 from Task 3) and `define-node` from 21 cases
  to 22 at Task 3; parity, `test:native`, `test:ui`, `test:n8` and the render and kit legs unchanged;
  `device:check`'s image from 130232 / 2000 / 416830 (flash / data / bss) to 126637 at Task 2 (the loader smaller)
  and 277702 / 2004 / 421515 at Task 4 (the engine, the host and the pack); the box from 101200 / 23832 / 188020
  (PIO-USB) to 95832 / 24736 / 188020 at Task 2 and 196688 / 46056 / 120600 at Task 3, `RP_NATIVE_USB`'s from 101576
  / 9836 / 181788 to 197056 / 32020 / 114368.
- **Owed, not runnable here.** Windows, macOS and CI's arm64 Linux job have never built E4. On Windows the engine is
  clang-cl objects with a forced include of `rp_mqjs_names.h` and a `sys/time.h` shim, `MqjsHost.cpp` uses
  `GetThreadTimes`, `mquickjs.h`'s `##__VA_ARGS__` has not met `cl`, and every desktop product now links the engine,
  so the first Windows build of any product is its test. **`retroplug-mqjs-run`'s `main.cpp:104` narrows a 64-bit
  deadline into a 32-bit field in a brace initialiser**, which GCC only warns about (Task 3's build prints it) but
  Clang (`-Wc++11-narrowing`, AppleClang on CI's macOS job) and MSVC (C2397) refuse; every desktop product depends
  on the runner through its bliptoaster pack, so the default build fails on macOS and Windows. **The first follow-up
  commit after Task 5's code reviews fixes it** (the controller's call, overnight), before the acceptance and before
  any push or CI run; the runner is desktop-only, so the fix moves no image hash and no gate figure.
  `cmake/mquickjs-names.cmake`'s macOS branch has never run. `build.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch`, pull requests
  and pushes to `main` only, so a push of `feature/modularize` runs nothing: these runs are owed to a dispatched run
  or a PR the user (or their Windows agent) starts. The 32-bit bytecode runs nowhere in CI (the device check is
  built there and never run). `RP_NATIVE_USB` has never run on hardware. Task 6 states all of them.
- **What no log backs.** No E4 stage ran the `env -i` CI dry run of `device:check` and `device:box`, the Reaper
  suite, `pnpm validate`, a fresh scratch configure, or the CI views of parity alone and of `test:ui`; Task 6 runs
  them, with E3's acceptance (`.superpowers/e3exec`) as the reference where E4 changes nothing counted, and asks for
  the count where it is new. A task's intermediate state is never run: each task builds once all its files are
  placed. Task 1's legs are fix pass 1's run where fix pass 2 did not re-run them, and **its `pnpm typecheck` is
  red** (a fixture fix pass 2 added does not type-check; Task 2 fixes it), predicted from the stage 2 report. **Task
  3 was never run whole at its own tree**: the stage-4 fold into it was run for the device-mode binary and
  `device:box` alone, its other legs are the stage's earlier runs (bracketed by Task 4's final run, at the same
  counts), its sanitizer runs of the device-mode binary are counted from its tags with no assertion total, and its
  `rp-device-check` image was never built (its suites step asks for the size). The reds (each task's first step, the
  hash guard's and the heap variable's refusals) and the `-Wnarrowing` warning's significance are predicted from the
  code; the warning itself is in the stage logs but no report names it. The design's section 11, which Task 5 lands,
  carries a few figures from runs earlier than the ones this plan quotes (11.1's "84-line transcript" against 86;
  11.2's 126641 and 95836 against 126637 and 95832; 11.3's "95836 to 196688"; 11.4's owners 98,798, 18,685 and
  17,955 against 99,040, 18,485 and 18,147): Task 5 must equal the prototype, so a docs follow-up (G2) re-derives
  them, and an implementer does not report them. The gate's audio leg has no log of its own: its figures are the
  record's (`gate-commands.txt`, `results.md`). No parity baseline, kit golden, render baseline, descriptor golden
  of an existing type, `buildGraph` golden, `plan-blob.hex`, `device-check-plan.hex` or `edio-golden.json` is
  re-recorded by any task.


**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**
- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's links are relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to the worktree
  root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 6 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own). No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with" trailer. Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context lines of older code and of the specs): leave those be.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself.
- Don't `rm -rf build` to fix CMake; investigate. Never use bare `git stash`, and never switch branches with uncommitted
  work in the tree. Never touch a submodule. `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure (the two tracked
  patches): expected, leave it. `build-device/` and `build-box/` are scratch build dirs the device scripts own and
  `.gitignore` lists; removing them is fine. `pico/n8-host/build/` is the rig's build dir (ignored by
  `pico/.gitignore`); only Task 3's image step and Task 6 build there.
- **`deps/mquickjs` is upstream's, and nothing edits it.** Task 1 places it by a `git archive` of upstream's commit
  `6d4d7eb6b99011d5aab6e88a9b99e8fd4d86c6e9` from a local checkout (`/workspaces/feature4/build-portable/mquickjs` or
  `/tmp/mquickjs`; both hold it, and with neither, `git clone https://github.com/bellard/mquickjs.git /tmp/mquickjs`
  fetches it) and proves it by its tree hash; what RetroPlug needs on top is a file of its own beside it. The one step
  that changes a byte there, Task 3's red for the hash guard, applies a one-word change and reverses it at once.
- The derived files are never committed: the embedded bundle C arrays (`build/native/*bundle_data.c`), the products'
  generated registration sources and providers headers (`build/packages/products/`), the device-mode objects'
  registrations (`build/device-mode/`), the exporter's package table, the device check's `DeviceCheckCases.hpp`, the
  engine's generated tables (`build/deps/mquickjs/host/`, and from Task 2 `build/mquickjs/<stdlib>/{64,32}`), every
  script pack's outputs (`build/packages/<package>/script/`: the bundles, the bytecode, the transcript, the
  `pack64.c` / `pack32.c` sources and the registration), and the exported plans: the box's `n8_host_plan.hpp` (under
  each firmware build dir's `generated/`: `build-box/pio/`, `build-box/native/`, `pico/n8-host/build/`) and the check's
  `DeviceCheckPlan.hpp` and, from Task 4, `DeviceCheckScriptPlan.hpp` (`build/device-check/` for the test and
  `build-device/generated/` for the image).
- **Parity holds the engine's output to the bit, and no task re-records anything.** Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`,
  `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE` or
  `RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE`: a golden that moves means the step is wrong. **The goldens that change on purpose are placed

### Task 1: MicroQuickJS vendored, defineNode in its subset, and the device-pack toolchain

Design sections 4 and 6 and section 8's first commit. MicroQuickJS, Bellard's engine for microcontrollers, is vendored
at upstream's `6d4d7eb` under `deps/mquickjs` (upstream's tracked files, unpatched, LICENSE kept; vendored rather than
a submodule, so a fresh clone and CI need no fetch and the pin cannot drift), and `cmake/mquickjs.cmake` builds its two
host tools for the desktop (`mqjs_stdlib`, which writes the stdlib's C tables, and `mqjs`, the compiler and REPL),
generating the tables into the build tree. `defineNode` and its helpers are rewritten in the engine's subset (no Set,
`includes`, `find`, `Object.entries`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `Number.isInteger`), and a device pack's definitions
refuse an audio port and a settings field named like an integer, at definition. A package's manifest may now declare a
script pack (`retroplug.script`: `entry`, `device: true`, `heapBytes`), and `retroplug_script_pack` runs the device-pack
toolchain over it: bundle against an allowlist, lower to ES5, scan for library calls the engine lacks, run under Node
and on the engine, and write bytecode at 64 and 32 bits. `packages/devtest/ts` is the seed pack
(`rp.devtest.script-transpose`).

The engine comes first, by a `git archive` of its pinned commit, then `defineNode`, the toolchain, the manifest's member
with the seed pack and the refused manifests, and the toolchain's tests. Before Task 1 `build/bin` holds the prototype
tip's binaries and no test of this task's exists in the tree, so a red here would prove nothing; the tree is built once,
in Step 6: build nothing before it.

**Files:**

- Create: `cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake`, `cmake/mquickjs-win-shim/sys/time.h`, `cmake/mquickjs.cmake`, `packages/devtest/ts/index.ts`, `packages/native/test/packages/read/ScriptOnly.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/NeitherNativeNorScript.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptDeviceWithoutHeap.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptEntryMissing.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptHeapFraction.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptHeapString.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptHeapTooBig.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptHeapTooSmall.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptNotObject.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptOnDesktop.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptWithoutDevice.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/ScriptWithoutEntry.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused/scratch-pack.ts`, `packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack.test.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/async-process.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/audio-port.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/guard-else.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/host-global.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/method-calls.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/missing-call.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/outside-import.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/proto-key.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/scenario.ts`, `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/using-resource.ts`, and `deps/mquickjs/` (upstream's 34 files, by Step 1's `git archive`)
- Modify: `CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/packages.cmake`, `package.json`, `packages/devtest/package.json`, `packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake`, `packages/retroplug/src/graph/defineNode.ts`, `packages/retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema.ts`, `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.json`

- [ ] **Step 1: MicroQuickJS at `6d4d7eb`, and its host tools**

The engine's 34 files are upstream's commit `6d4d7eb6b99011d5aab6e88a9b99e8fd4d86c6e9` exactly, so they are not quoted
here: the block below writes them by a `git archive` of that commit from a local checkout of
`https://github.com/bellard/mquickjs` (`/workspaces/feature4/build-portable/mquickjs` and `/tmp/mquickjs` both hold
it; with neither, clone it to `/tmp/mquickjs` first, which needs GitHub), and the tree hash after it proves the result
is that commit's tree, byte for byte. A checkout's own build products (`*.o`, `mqjs`) are untracked there, so `git
archive` leaves them behind. Nothing ever edits these files: what RetroPlug needs on top is a file of its own.

````bash
bash -c 'set -o pipefail; M=; for d in /workspaces/feature4/build-portable/mquickjs /tmp/mquickjs; do git -C "$d" cat-file -e 6d4d7eb6b99011d5aab6e88a9b99e8fd4d86c6e9^{commit} 2>/dev/null && { M=$d; break; }; done; test -n "$M" || { echo "no local checkout holds 6d4d7eb"; exit 1; }; echo "from $M"; mkdir -p deps/mquickjs && git -C "$M" archive --format=tar 6d4d7eb6b99011d5aab6e88a9b99e8fd4d86c6e9 | tar -x -C deps/mquickjs'
````

Run: `find deps/mquickjs -type f | wc -l`
Expected: `34`: upstream's tracked files at the pin, no more and no fewer.

Run: `bash -c 'i=$(mktemp -u); GIT_INDEX_FILE=$i git add -- deps/mquickjs && GIT_INDEX_FILE=$i git write-tree --prefix=deps/mquickjs/; s=$?; rm -f $i; exit $s'`
Expected: `b706b80af2c1a11cb553d61e988fdf4ac1c36af7`: the tree of upstream's commit 6d4d7eb (`git -C <checkout> rev-parse 6d4d7eb^{tree}` prints it too), and the tree 51bd5a5f3 holds at `deps/mquickjs`, so the vendored engine is upstream's, byte for byte. The command stages into a scratch index of its own, so the tree's real index is untouched and `deps/mquickjs` stays untracked until the task's commit.

`cmake/mquickjs.cmake`, included from the root `CMakeLists.txt` after the vendored deps' warnings are silenced, builds
`mqjs_stdlib` (upstream's stdlib build tool over `mqjs_stdlib.c`) and `mqjs` (`mqjs.c`, the REPL and compiler the
toolchain compiles a pack with and runs it under), both `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` into `build/bin`, with upstream Makefile's
flags; `cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake` runs the stdlib tool at build time and writes its output to a file (no shell
redirect), so the host-width tables (`mqjs_stdlib.h`, `mquickjs_atom.h`) land in `build/deps/mquickjs/host`, never
beside `mquickjs.c`, whose quoted include would otherwise find a stray one first. On Windows the tools are clang-cl
objects, as SameBoy's core is, with `cmake/mquickjs-win-shim/sys/time.h` giving `mqjs.c` its `gettimeofday`; that half
is written to the pattern and has never been built.

Create `cmake/mquickjs.cmake`:

````cmake
# MicroQuickJS (mquickjs), Fabrice Bellard's JavaScript engine for microcontrollers, vendored at upstream commit
# 6d4d7eb6b99011d5aab6e88a9b99e8fd4d86c6e9 under deps/mquickjs (MIT: deps/mquickjs/LICENSE). The tree is upstream's
# tracked files at that commit, unpatched; what RetroPlug needs on top is a file of its own, here or beside it, never an
# edit in deps/mquickjs. Vendored rather than a submodule so that a fresh clone and CI build it with no fetch of their
# own, and so that the pin cannot drift: the bytecode a device pack ships is only as stable as the engine that compiled
# it (docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 3's table and section 11.1).
#
# This file builds the engine's two host tools for the desktop, both EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL (a target that needs one builds
# it):
#
#   mqjs_stdlib  upstream's stdlib build tool (mquickjs_build.c over mqjs_stdlib.c): writes the C tables of the standard
#                library (mqjs_stdlib.h) and the predefined atoms' offsets (mquickjs_atom.h, `-a`), for the host's word
#                width, or for a 32-bit target's with `-m32`.
#   mqjs         upstream's REPL and compiler (mqjs.c), the tool the device-pack toolchain
#                (packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs) compiles a pack to bytecode with (`-o`, `-m32` for
#                the box) and runs it under (`-b`).
#
# Both are written to build/bin, where the toolchain looks for mqjs.
#
# The tables are generated into build/deps/mquickjs/host, never into deps/mquickjs: mquickjs.c includes
# "mquickjs_atom.h" by a quoted name, which the compiler looks for beside mquickjs.c first, so a generated header left
# in the vendored tree (a `make` run there) would shadow this build's, and dirty the tree besides.
#
# The flags are upstream Makefile's for these files (-D_GNU_SOURCE -fno-math-errno -fno-trapping-math, and -lm), its
# warnings silenced as every vendored dep's are (retroplug_silence_dep_warnings, in the root CMakeLists).
#
# Windows: MSVC's cl cannot compile the engine (GNU attributes and __builtin_*_overflow), so on Windows the tools are
# compiled with clang-cl, MSVC-ABI compatible, as SameBoy's core is (cmake/sameboy.cmake), and mqjs.c gets the one
# header MSVC's C runtime lacks from cmake/mquickjs-win-shim (its gettimeofday). That half has not been built yet: it is
# written to the SameBoy pattern, and the first Windows build is its test.
set(MQUICKJS_DIR "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/deps/mquickjs")
set(MQUICKJS_HOST_GEN "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/deps/mquickjs/host")
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${MQUICKJS_HOST_GEN}")

set(_mqjs_stdlib_sources "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/mqjs_stdlib.c" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/mquickjs_build.c")
set(_mqjs_sources
    "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/mqjs.c" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/readline_tty.c" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/readline.c"
    "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/mquickjs.c" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/dtoa.c" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/libm.c" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/cutils.c")

if(MSVC)
    find_program(MQUICKJS_CLANG_CL clang-cl
        HINTS "$ENV{VCINSTALLDIR}Tools/Llvm/x64/bin"
              "C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/18/Community/VC/Tools/Llvm/x64/bin"
        REQUIRED)
    set(_mqjs_objdir "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/deps/mquickjs/clang")
    file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${_mqjs_objdir}")
    # /MT: the project's static CRT. -w: upstream's warnings are not ours to act on.
    set(_mqjs_cl_flags /nologo /c /MT /O2 /DNDEBUG -D_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS -D_CRT_NONSTDC_NO_WARNINGS
        "-I${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/mquickjs-win-shim" "-I${MQUICKJS_HOST_GEN}" "-I${MQUICKJS_DIR}" -w)
    # _mqjs_clang_objects(<var> <generated headers the sources include> <sources>...)
    function(_mqjs_clang_objects var headers)
        set(_objs "")
        foreach(_src IN LISTS ARGN)
            get_filename_component(_n "${_src}" NAME)
            set(_obj "${_mqjs_objdir}/${_n}.obj")
            add_custom_command(
                OUTPUT "${_obj}"
                COMMAND "${MQUICKJS_CLANG_CL}" ${_mqjs_cl_flags} "/Fo${_obj}" "${_src}"
                DEPENDS "${_src}" ${headers} "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/mquickjs-win-shim/sys/time.h"
                COMMENT "clang-cl (mquickjs) ${_n}"
                VERBATIM)
            list(APPEND _objs "${_obj}")
        endforeach()
        set(${var} ${_objs} PARENT_SCOPE)
    endfunction()
    _mqjs_clang_objects(_mqjs_stdlib_objects "" ${_mqjs_stdlib_sources})
    add_executable(mqjs_stdlib EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL ${_mqjs_stdlib_objects})
    set_target_properties(mqjs_stdlib PROPERTIES LINKER_LANGUAGE C)
else()
    add_executable(mqjs_stdlib EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL ${_mqjs_stdlib_sources})
    target_compile_definitions(mqjs_stdlib PRIVATE _GNU_SOURCE)
    retroplug_silence_dep_warnings(mqjs_stdlib)
endif()

# The host width's tables, which mqjs is compiled with. A command writes each, through cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake (the
# tool prints the table on stdout).
set(_mqjs_host_headers "${MQUICKJS_HOST_GEN}/mqjs_stdlib.h" "${MQUICKJS_HOST_GEN}/mquickjs_atom.h")
add_custom_command(
    OUTPUT ${_mqjs_host_headers}
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} "-DTOOL=$<TARGET_FILE:mqjs_stdlib>" "-DOUTPUT=${MQUICKJS_HOST_GEN}/mqjs_stdlib.h"
            -P "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake"
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} "-DTOOL=$<TARGET_FILE:mqjs_stdlib>" "-DARGS=-a"
            "-DOUTPUT=${MQUICKJS_HOST_GEN}/mquickjs_atom.h" -P "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake"
    DEPENDS mqjs_stdlib "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake"
    COMMENT "mquickjs: the standard library's tables, host width"
    VERBATIM)

if(MSVC)
    _mqjs_clang_objects(_mqjs_objects "${_mqjs_host_headers}" ${_mqjs_sources})
    add_executable(mqjs EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL ${_mqjs_objects})
    set_target_properties(mqjs PROPERTIES LINKER_LANGUAGE C)
else()
    add_executable(mqjs EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL ${_mqjs_sources} ${_mqjs_host_headers})
    target_compile_definitions(mqjs PRIVATE _GNU_SOURCE)
    target_compile_options(mqjs PRIVATE -fno-math-errno -fno-trapping-math)
    # The generated tables include the engine's private header by a quoted name, from the generated directory.
    target_include_directories(mqjs PRIVATE "${MQUICKJS_HOST_GEN}" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}")
    target_link_libraries(mqjs PRIVATE m)
    retroplug_silence_dep_warnings(mqjs)
endif()
set_target_properties(mqjs mqjs_stdlib PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin")
````

Create `cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake`:

````cmake
# cmake -DTOOL=<mqjs_stdlib> [-DARGS=<args>] -DOUTPUT=<file> -P cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake: runs MicroQuickJS's stdlib
# build tool, which prints the table it builds on stdout, into OUTPUT (cmake/mquickjs.cmake's tables). A script rather
# than a shell redirect, so the command is the same on every generator and platform; a tool that fails leaves no
# half-written table behind.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.19)
if(NOT TOOL OR NOT OUTPUT)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "mquickjs-table.cmake: pass -DTOOL=<mqjs_stdlib> and -DOUTPUT=<file>")
endif()
execute_process(COMMAND "${TOOL}" ${ARGS} OUTPUT_FILE "${OUTPUT}.new" RESULT_VARIABLE _result ERROR_VARIABLE _error)
if(NOT _result EQUAL 0)
    file(REMOVE "${OUTPUT}.new")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "mquickjs-table.cmake: ${TOOL} ${ARGS} failed (${_result}):\n${_error}")
endif()
file(RENAME "${OUTPUT}.new" "${OUTPUT}")
````

Create `cmake/mquickjs-win-shim/sys/time.h`:

````cpp
/* <sys/time.h> for MicroQuickJS's host tool on Windows (cmake/mquickjs.cmake): MSVC's C runtime has none, and mqjs.c,
 * upstream's REPL and compiler, reads the time of day through it (Date.now, performance.now and the random seed). This
 * is the part it uses, gettimeofday over the system clock; the engine itself (mquickjs.c) does not include it. */
#ifndef RP_MQUICKJS_WIN_SYS_TIME_H
#define RP_MQUICKJS_WIN_SYS_TIME_H

#include <winsock2.h> /* struct timeval; before windows.h, which readline_tty.c includes after this */
#include <windows.h>

static int gettimeofday(struct timeval *tv, void *tz)
{
    FILETIME ft;
    ULARGE_INTEGER t;
    (void)tz;
    GetSystemTimeAsFileTime(&ft);
    t.LowPart = ft.dwLowDateTime;
    t.HighPart = ft.dwHighDateTime;
    /* 100 ns ticks since 1601-01-01 to microseconds since 1970-01-01 */
    t.QuadPart = (t.QuadPart - 116444736000000000ULL) / 10;
    tv->tv_sec = (long)(t.QuadPart / 1000000);
    tv->tv_usec = (long)(t.QuadPart % 1000000);
    return 0;
}

#endif
````

- [ ] **Step 2: `defineNode` in the engine's subset, with the device pack's refusals**

`defineNode.ts` keeps to ES5's library: local helpers (`isWhole`, `listed`, `startsWith`, `portById`) and an
`Object.create(null)` dictionary for the ids seen, in place of what the engine lacks. `RP_DEVICE_PACK`, a constant the
toolchain alone defines at bundle time (`typeof RP_DEVICE_PACK !== "undefined" && RP_DEVICE_PACK === true`, folded to
`true` by esbuild; every other bundle sees `false`), makes a definition lay its default layout out at once and refuse,
naming the node and the port, an audio port (`<id>: port "<p>" is audio, which a device pack's node cannot have: audio
stays C++`), and a settings field named like an integer, which the engine would order unlike V8 (`settings field "7"
is a number, which a device pack's settings cannot keep in order`, an array item's field named like `taps[].0`); a
settings-dependent audio port is refused by `layout()`. Desktop packs behave exactly as before, which the descriptor
and `buildGraph` goldens inside `pnpm test` hold. `settingsSchema.ts`'s header says it is held to the same rule.

- [ ] **Step 3: The device-pack toolchain**

`packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs` builds one pack (`--entry`, `--name`, `--heap-bytes`, `--out-dir`,
`--pack-dir`, `--mqjs`), every compile and run in `<out>/.<name>.work`, its outputs written only once the last check
passes and the work directory removed on success and on every failure. In order: esbuild bundles the entry as an iife
against an allowlist (the pack's directory and the portable SDK: `defineNode`, `settingsSchema`, `descriptor`,
`script/register`), naming an offender and its importer; the repo's pinned TypeScript 5 lowers it to ES5; a scan
refuses each call the engine lacks (check:portable's list), naming the call and its `file:line` through the source
maps, over the bundle, the lowered helpers and the whole SDK, a name read behind its own `typeof` guard passing and
the host globals (`setTimeout`, `print`, `console.warn`, ...) refused, a name the code declares in an enclosing scope
being its own; a Node reference run prints every registered node's descriptor (a definition refusal surfaces here, at
build time); `mqjs -o` compiles the bytecode at 64 bits and with `-m32`; and the pack and its epilogue, run as
bytecode, must print Node's transcript byte for byte (CRLF normalised), and the pack's own 64-bit bytecode must define
its nodes under `--memory-limit <heapBytes>`, a crash below the engine's least context named as one. Outputs:
`<name>.js`, `<name>.mqjs64.bin`, `<name>.mqjs32.bin`, `<name>.transcript.txt`, each rewritten only when its bytes
change.

Create `packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// The device-pack toolchain (docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 6): a script pack the manifest marks for the
// device, TypeScript to MicroQuickJS bytecode, refused at build time for what the box could not run. The steps are
// check:portable's (feature/launchpad's scripts/check-portable-core.mjs), generalised for packs:
//
// - The bundle: esbuild bundles the pack's entry, and a module outside its allowlist fails the build: the pack's own
//   directory and the portable node SDK (SDK below), so no zod, no backend, no native seam, no UI. The bundle is built
//   with RP_DEVICE_PACK defined true, which is how defineNode learns that its definitions are a device pack's
//   (graph/defineNode.ts): only this toolchain defines it, and it builds device packs alone.
// - The lowering: TypeScript 5 lowers the bundle to ES5 (the workspace's TypeScript 7 no longer emits ES5), as
//   MicroQuickJS parses ES5 plus a little: classes, arrows, let/const, spread and template literals must go.
// - The scan: a library call MicroQuickJS does not have (Map, Set, Object.entries, async, ...), or a global of mqjs's
//   REPL that the box's engine will not have (setTimeout, print, console.warn, ...), fails the build naming the call
//   and the source line it came from (read back through esbuild's source map, and TypeScript's), rather than as a
//   TypeError deep in a run. It covers the pack as bundled, then as lowered (the helpers the lowering adds), and the
//   whole SDK with every export kept. A read behind its own `typeof` guard is accepted, as the lowering's helpers make
//   them.
// - The reference run: the pack runs under Node with a short epilogue that prints every node type it registered (its
//   descriptor JSON). A definition the device refuses (an audio port, graph/defineNode.ts) throws here, at build time,
//   with its own message. Node's run is the REFERENCE, nothing more: a vm context has every standard global whatever
//   it is handed, so it says nothing about what MicroQuickJS has.
// - The bytecode: `mqjs -o` compiles the pack at the host's width (64-bit, for the desktop's mquickjs host) and with
//   `-m32` (the box's). It is relocated to address 0 and names its source by the bundle's file name alone, so the same
//   pack builds the same bytes in any checkout.
// - The engine's run: the pack with the epilogue, compiled as the pack is, runs as bytecode on the engine and must
//   print Node's transcript byte for byte; and the pack's own 64-bit bytecode must define its node types inside the
//   heap its manifest declares (`mqjs --memory-limit`, which holds the whole context, so the figure is the context's
//   size, and a 64-bit context is the larger of the two). The 32-bit bytecode runs on the box alone. Both runs are on
//   upstream's REPL (mqjs.c and its stdlib), not yet on the box's own stdlib.
//
// Writes, under --out-dir and only once every check has passed: <name>.js (the lowered pack, what the bytecode is
// compiled from), <name>.mqjs64.bin and <name>.mqjs32.bin (the bytecode), and <name>.transcript.txt (the engine run's
// transcript), each only when its bytes change. Its work files are in a directory of their own beside them, removed
// whether the pack passes or not. Exits nonzero saying what refused the pack. CMake runs it for a package whose
// manifest declares a script pack (cmake/packages.cmake, retroplug_script_pack), with the manifest's entry and heap;
// the tests run it on fixtures of their own (test/graph/device-pack.test.ts).
//
// Usage: node build-device-pack.mjs --entry <file.ts> --name <pack> --heap-bytes <n> --out-dir <dir>
//                                   [--pack-dir <dir>] [--mqjs <path>]
//   --pack-dir  the pack's own directory, every module under which the bundle may hold (default: the entry's)
//   --mqjs      the engine's host tool (default: MQJS, else build/bin/mqjs, the desktop build's `mqjs` target)

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { runInNewContext } from "node:vm";

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const PKG = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const REPO = resolve(PKG, "../..");

/** The portable node SDK, repo-relative: what a device pack may import beside its own modules. */
const SDK = [
  "packages/retroplug/src/graph/defineNode.ts",
  "packages/retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema.ts",
  "packages/retroplug/src/graph/descriptor.ts",
  "packages/retroplug/src/script/register.ts",
];

// The engine the bytecode is compiled for. Pinned in deps/mquickjs; named in what this prints.
const ENGINE = "MicroQuickJS (deps/mquickjs, 6d4d7eb)";
// The heap the transcript's run gets: that run checks the engine's behaviour, not the pack's heap, which the pack's own
// bytecode is held to after it.
const TRANSCRIPT_HEAP = 1 << 20;

// The globals of upstream mqjs's REPL stdlib (deps/mquickjs/mqjs_stdlib.c), which the engine runs below use and the
// box's stdlib will not have: timers (asynchrony a device pack may not have), print, gc, load, performance and
// scriptArgs.
const REPL_CALLS = ["setTimeout", "setInterval", "clearTimeout", "clearInterval", "setImmediate", "print", "gc",
                    "load"];
const REPL_GLOBALS = ["performance", "scriptArgs"];

/** Library calls MicroQuickJS lacks, which the ES5 lowering leaves alone: check:portable's list. A name here fails
 *  the build. Matched against the code with comments and string literals blanked, and with a read behind its own
 *  `typeof` guard blanked too (blankForScan), so neither a word in a message nor a helper's guarded fallback trips it.
 *  A row is [pattern, what it names, and, for a row that names bare globals, those names]: one of those the code
 *  declares itself in a scope enclosing the use (a local `load`, say) is its own and passes, as blankForScan decides
 *  on the syntax tree. Every other row names a method or a property, which no declaration makes the code's own.
 *  Checked against the pinned engine with `typeof`: it DOES have Number.parseInt/parseFloat/EPSILON/MAX_SAFE_INTEGER,
 *  Math.trunc/sign/fround/imul/clz32/log2/log10, String trim*, codePointAt, repeat and replaceAll,
 *  Object.create/keys/defineProperty/getPrototypeOf/setPrototypeOf, and Array.isArray. */
const MISSING = [
  [/\bnew (Map|Set|WeakMap|WeakSet|Proxy|Date)\b/, "Map/Set/Proxy, or a Date object (only Date.now exists)"],
  [/\b(Symbol|Reflect|Proxy|Promise|WeakRef|Intl)\b/, "Symbol/Reflect/Proxy/Promise/WeakRef/Intl"],
  [/\b(async|await)\b/, "async/await"],
  [/\bObject\.(values|entries|fromEntries|freeze|isFrozen|seal|is|getOwnPropertyNames|getOwnPropertySymbols|getOwnPropertyDescriptors?|defineProperties)\b/,
    "Object.values/entries/fromEntries/freeze/seal/is/getOwnPropertyNames/Symbols/Descriptor(s)/defineProperties"],
  // TypeScript's own __assign helper reads `Object.assign || function...` and falls back, so a guarded use is fine;
  // a bare one is not.
  [/\bObject\.assign\b(?!\s*\|\|)/, "Object.assign"],
  [/\bArray\.(from|of)\b/, "Array.from/of"],
  [/\bNumber\.(isInteger|isFinite|isNaN|isSafeInteger)\b/, "Number.isInteger and friends"],
  [/\bMath\.(hypot|cbrt|log1p|expm1|sinh|cosh|tanh|asinh|acosh|atanh)\b/, "ES2015 Math functions"],
  [/\bString\.raw\b|\.(padStart|padEnd|startsWith|endsWith|normalize)\(/,
    "String.raw / padStart/padEnd/startsWith/endsWith/normalize"],
  [/\.(find|findIndex|findLast|findLastIndex|includes|fill|flat|flatMap|at|copyWithin)\(/, "ES2015+ Array methods"],
  [/\.prototype\.(find|findIndex|includes|fill|flat|flatMap|at|padStart|padEnd|startsWith|endsWith)\b/,
    "ES2015+ methods via .prototype"],
  [/\.(keys|values|entries)\(\)/, "array/iterator .keys()/.values()/.entries()"],
  [/\.(localeCompare|toLocaleString|toLocaleLowerCase|toLocaleUpperCase|matchAll|toISOString|toJSON)\(/,
    "locale / matchAll / Date string methods"],
  [/\bObject\.hasOwn\b|\.substr\(|\.(toSorted|toReversed|toSpliced)\(/, "Object.hasOwn / substr / toSorted & co."],
  [/\b(DataView|BigInt|TextEncoder|TextDecoder|structuredClone|queueMicrotask|encodeURIComponent|decodeURIComponent|encodeURI|decodeURI|escape|unescape)\b/,
    "DataView / BigInt / TextEncoder / structuredClone / queueMicrotask / URI functions"],
  // REPL_CALLS called and REPL_GLOBALS read, not as a property. A stopgap until the engine runs below are on the box's
  // own stdlib: a call through globalThis or an alias (`var t = setTimeout`) passes, and a method shorthand of one of
  // these names in an object literal (`{ load() {} }`) is refused.
  [new RegExp(`(?<![.\\w$])(${REPL_CALLS.join("|")})\\s*\\(|(?<![.\\w$])(${REPL_GLOBALS.join("|")})\\b(?!\\s*:)`),
    "a global of mqjs's REPL (timers, print, gc, load, performance, scriptArgs) that the box's engine will not have",
    [...REPL_CALLS, ...REPL_GLOBALS]],
  // mqjs's console has log alone.
  [/\bconsole\.(?!log\b)\w+/, "a console method other than log, which the box's engine will not have"],
  // Typed-array slice/fill/indexOf are missing too, but read like the Array methods they shadow, so they are left to
  // the engine's run rather than flagging every array .slice() here.
];

// What runs after the pack, on both engines: every node type it registered (graph/defineNode.ts's descriptor, through
// script/register.ts's global), one JSON line each, so the two transcripts compare what the definitions resolved to.
const EPILOGUE = `
;(function () {
  var nodes = globalThis.__rp_scriptNodes || [];
  console.log("# " + nodes.length + " node type(s)");
  for (var i = 0; i < nodes.length; ++i) console.log(JSON.stringify(nodes[i].descriptor()));
})();
`;

// ---- the arguments -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

function parseArgs(argv) {
  const known = { "--entry": "entry", "--name": "name", "--heap-bytes": "heapBytes", "--out-dir": "outDir",
                  "--pack-dir": "packDir", "--mqjs": "mqjs" };
  const out = {};
  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 2) {
    const key = known[argv[i]];
    if (!key || i + 1 >= argv.length) usage(`unknown or incomplete argument ${argv[i]}`);
    out[key] = argv[i + 1];
  }
  for (const need of ["entry", "name", "heapBytes", "outDir"]) if (!out[need]) usage(`--${need} is required`);
  return out;
}

function usage(why) {
  console.error(`build-device-pack: ${why}\nusage: node build-device-pack.mjs --entry <file.ts> --name <pack> ` +
                "--heap-bytes <n> --out-dir <dir> [--pack-dir <dir>] [--mqjs <path>]");
  process.exit(2);
}

const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));
const NAME = args.name;
if (!/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$/.test(NAME)) usage(`--name ${NAME} is not a file-name-safe pack name`);
const ENTRY = resolve(args.entry);
const PACK_DIR = resolve(args.packDir ?? dirname(ENTRY));
const OUT_DIR = resolve(args.outDir);
// The work files' own directory, beside the outputs: mqjs runs in it, and it goes whatever the outcome.
const WORK = join(OUT_DIR, `.${NAME}.work`);
const fail = (msg) => {
  rmSync(WORK, { recursive: true, force: true });
  console.error(`device pack ${NAME}: ${msg}`);
  process.exit(1);
};
if (!/^[1-9][0-9]*$/.test(args.heapBytes)) usage(`--heap-bytes ${args.heapBytes} is not a whole number of bytes`);
const HEAP_BYTES = Number(args.heapBytes);
if (!existsSync(ENTRY)) fail(`no entry ${ENTRY}`);
const MQJS = args.mqjs ?? process.env.MQJS ??
  join(REPO, "build/bin", process.platform === "win32" ? "mqjs.exe" : "mqjs");
if (!existsSync(MQJS)) fail(`no mqjs at ${MQJS} (build the desktop build's \`mqjs\` target, or pass --mqjs)`);

const repoPath = (p) => relative(REPO, p).split(sep).join("/");

// An output written only when its bytes change, so what a build makes from it (the bytecode embedded in an image) is
// remade only then.
function keep(file, bytes) {
  const data = typeof bytes === "string" ? Buffer.from(bytes) : bytes;
  if (existsSync(file) && readFileSync(file).equals(data)) return;
  writeFileSync(file, data);
}

// ---- the bundle and its allowlist --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const esbuild = require("esbuild");
const bundleOptions = {
  absWorkingDir: REPO, // metafile and source-map paths are relative to this; run from anywhere and they still resolve
  bundle: true,
  write: false,
  metafile: true,
  format: "iife",
  platform: "neutral",
  target: "es2020",
  logLevel: "silent",
  define: { RP_DEVICE_PACK: "true" },
};
const bundleFile = join(OUT_DIR, `${NAME}.bundle.js`); // never written: the source map's paths are relative to it
let built;
try {
  built = await esbuild.build({
    ...bundleOptions,
    entryPoints: [ENTRY],
    outfile: bundleFile,
    sourcemap: "external",
    sourcesContent: false,
  });
} catch (e) {
  fail(`bundling ${repoPath(ENTRY)} failed:\n${e.message}`);
}
const inPack = (p) => p === PACK_DIR || p.startsWith(PACK_DIR + sep);
const offenders = [];
for (const input of Object.keys(built.metafile.inputs)) {
  const abs = resolve(REPO, input);
  if (inPack(abs) || SDK.includes(repoPath(abs))) continue;
  // Who brought it in, so the fix is plain.
  const by = Object.entries(built.metafile.inputs)
    .filter(([, other]) => other.imports.some((imp) => resolve(REPO, imp.path) === abs))
    .map(([from]) => repoPath(resolve(REPO, from)));
  offenders.push(`${repoPath(abs)}${by.length ? ` (imported by ${by.join(", ")})` : ""}`);
}
if (offenders.length > 0) {
  fail(`the pack imports modules outside its allowlist (its own directory, ${repoPath(PACK_DIR)}, and the portable ` +
       `node SDK in scripts/build-device-pack.mjs):\n  ${offenders.join("\n  ")}`);
}
const bundleJs = built.outputFiles.find((f) => f.path.endsWith(".js")).text;
const bundleMap = JSON.parse(built.outputFiles.find((f) => f.path.endsWith(".map")).text);
console.log(`  ok: bundled ${Object.keys(built.metafile.inputs).length} modules, all in the pack or the SDK`);

// ---- the lowering to ES5 -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const ts = require("typescript-5");

function lowerToEs5(code, sourceMap) {
  const out = ts.transpileModule(code, {
    reportDiagnostics: true,
    compilerOptions: {
      target: ts.ScriptTarget.ES5,
      module: ts.ModuleKind.CommonJS, // a script with no imports or exports, so this emits no module wrapper
      // Off on purpose: with it, for-of goes through Symbol.iterator. MicroQuickJS iterates arrays only, and the
      // plain lowering turns a for-of over an array into an index loop.
      downlevelIteration: false,
      removeComments: true,
      sourceMap,
    },
  });
  if (out.diagnostics?.length) {
    fail(ts.formatDiagnostics(out.diagnostics, { getCanonicalFileName: (f) => f, getCurrentDirectory: () => REPO,
                                                 getNewLine: () => "\n" }));
  }
  return { code: out.outputText.replace(/\n\/\/# sourceMappingURL=.*\s*$/, "\n"),
           map: sourceMap ? JSON.parse(out.sourceMapText) : null };
}

// MicroQuickJS is always strict; so is the reference run, so a sloppy-mode-only construct fails both.
const STRICT = '"use strict";\n';
const lowered = lowerToEs5(bundleJs, true);
const es5 = STRICT + lowered.code;
const es5Name = `${NAME}.js`;
console.log(`  ok: lowered to ES5 (${(es5.length / 1024).toFixed(1)} KB)`);

// ---- the library scan --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const escapeRegExp = (text) => text.replace(/[.*+?^$()|[\]\\{}]/g, "\\$&");

// A name or a dotted chain of names (Symbol, Object.getOwnPropertySymbols): what a guard may test, spelt; or null.
function dottedName(node) {
  if (ts.isIdentifier(node)) return node.text;
  if (ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(node) && ts.isIdentifier(node.name)) {
    const head = dottedName(node.expression);
    return head && `${head}.${node.name.text}`;
  }
  return null;
}

// `typeof X === "function"` (or `!== "undefined"`, either equality), X a name or a dotted chain: X, or null.
function guardedName(node) {
  if (!ts.isBinaryExpression(node)) return null;
  const op = node.operatorToken.kind;
  const eq = op === ts.SyntaxKind.EqualsEqualsEqualsToken || op === ts.SyntaxKind.EqualsEqualsToken;
  const ne = op === ts.SyntaxKind.ExclamationEqualsEqualsToken || op === ts.SyntaxKind.ExclamationEqualsToken;
  if (!ts.isTypeOfExpression(node.left) || !ts.isStringLiteral(node.right)) return null;
  if (!((eq && node.right.text === "function") || (ne && node.right.text === "undefined"))) return null;
  return dottedName(node.left.expression);
}

// Whether a function-like node, a block or the file declares `name` in its own scope: a parameter, a function's own
// name, or a function, var, let or const among its statements. A var in a nested block is not looked for, so such a
// name is still refused (the safe side).
function declares(scope, name) {
  if (ts.isFunctionLike(scope)) {
    if (scope.name && ts.isIdentifier(scope.name) && scope.name.text === name) return true;
    if (scope.parameters.some((p) => ts.isIdentifier(p.name) && p.name.text === name)) return true;
    return false;
  }
  const statements = ts.isBlock(scope) || ts.isSourceFile(scope) ? scope.statements : [];
  for (const st of statements) {
    if (ts.isFunctionDeclaration(st) && st.name?.text === name) return true;
    if (ts.isVariableStatement(st) &&
        st.declarationList.declarations.some((d) => ts.isIdentifier(d.name) && d.name.text === name)) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

// Whether an identifier names a binding the code declares in a scope enclosing it, rather than a global.
function declaredAround(id) {
  for (let scope = id.parent; scope; scope = scope.parent) if (declares(scope, id.text)) return true;
  return false;
}

// The names a condition's guards test, anywhere in it (`a && typeof X === "function"` guards X).
function guardsIn(node, out = []) {
  const name = guardedName(node);
  if (name) out.push(name);
  else if (ts.isBinaryExpression(node) && node.operatorToken.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.AmpersandAmpersandToken) {
    guardsIn(node.left, out);
    guardsIn(node.right, out);
  } else if (ts.isParenthesizedExpression(node)) guardsIn(node.expression, out);
  return out;
}

/** The code with every comment, and every string and template literal's contents, blanked, for the library scan, so a
 *  word in a message or in a comment (esbuild heads each module's code with a comment naming its file) cannot trip it;
 *  with every read of a name (or a dotted chain) behind its own `typeof` guard blanked, the guard included
 *  (`typeof X === "function" && X(...)`, `if (typeof X === "function") ... X ...`, `typeof X === "function" ? X : Y`,
 *  and `!== "undefined"` for `=== "function"`), which is how the lowering's helpers reach for what an engine may lack
 *  (__rest's Object.getOwnPropertySymbols, __generator's Symbol); and with each of `ownable`'s names blanked where the
 *  code declares it in an enclosing scope. A guard in any other form is not read as one, so what it guards is refused:
 *  `||`, an else-branch, a negated guard, `typeof X === "undefined" ? fallback : X`, and an early
 *  `if (typeof X !== "function") return`. Done on TypeScript's parse of the code, not with a regex: a regex cannot
 *  tell a quote inside a regex literal (`/"/`) from the start of a string, and would then blank real code, exactly
 *  where a forbidden call could hide. */
function blankForScan(code, ownable) {
  const file = ts.createSourceFile("bundle.js", code, ts.ScriptTarget.ES5, /*setParentNodes*/ true, ts.ScriptKind.JS);
  const chars = code.split("");
  const blankRange = (from, to) => {
    for (let i = from; i < to; i++) if (chars[i] !== "\n") chars[i] = " ";
  };
  const blankComments = (pos) => {
    const ranges = [...(ts.getLeadingCommentRanges(code, pos) ?? []),
                    ...(ts.getTrailingCommentRanges(code, pos) ?? [])];
    for (const r of ranges) blankRange(r.pos, r.end);
  };
  const guarded = []; // [from, to, name]: where `name` is read behind its guard
  const visit = (node) => {
    blankComments(node.pos);
    blankComments(node.end);
    if (ts.isStringLiteral(node) || ts.isNoSubstitutionTemplateLiteral(node)) {
      blankRange(node.getStart(file) + 1, node.end - 1);
    } else if (ts.isTemplateExpression(node)) {
      blankRange(node.head.getStart(file) + 1, node.head.end - 1);
      for (const span of node.templateSpans) blankRange(span.literal.getStart(file) + 1, span.literal.end - 1);
    }
    // The guarded part: the guard and the rest of its && chain, an if's then-branch, or a conditional's true side.
    let condition = null;
    let end = node.end;
    if (ts.isBinaryExpression(node) && node.operatorToken.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.AmpersandAmpersandToken) {
      condition = node.left;
    } else if (ts.isIfStatement(node)) {
      condition = node.expression;
      end = node.thenStatement.end;
    } else if (ts.isConditionalExpression(node)) {
      condition = node.condition;
      end = node.whenTrue.end;
    }
    if (condition) for (const name of guardsIn(condition)) guarded.push([node.getStart(file), end, name]);
    // One of the bare globals a row names, declared by the code around it: the code's own, not the global.
    if (ts.isIdentifier(node) && ownable.has(node.text) && declaredAround(node)) {
      blankRange(node.getStart(file), node.end);
    }
    ts.forEachChild(node, visit);
  };
  visit(file);
  let text = chars.join("");
  for (const [from, to, name] of guarded) {
    const re = new RegExp(`(?<![\\w$.])${escapeRegExp(name)}(?![\\w$])`, "g");
    const part = text.slice(from, to).replace(re, (m) => " ".repeat(m.length));
    text = text.slice(0, from) + part + text.slice(to);
  }
  return text;
}

// A source map's mappings, decoded: per generated line, its segments as [column, source, line, column], each 0-based.
const VLQ = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
function decodeMappings(mappings) {
  const lines = [];
  let source = 0, line = 0, column = 0;
  for (const text of mappings.split(";")) {
    const segments = [];
    let generated = 0;
    for (const segment of text.split(",")) {
      if (!segment) continue;
      const values = [];
      let value = 0, shift = 0;
      for (const ch of segment) {
        const digit = VLQ.indexOf(ch);
        value += (digit & 31) << shift;
        if (digit & 32) shift += 5;
        else {
          values.push(value & 1 ? -(value >>> 1) : value >>> 1);
          value = shift = 0;
        }
      }
      generated += values[0];
      if (values.length >= 4) {
        source += values[1];
        line += values[2];
        column += values[3];
        segments.push([generated, source, line, column]);
      }
    }
    lines.push(segments);
  }
  return lines;
}

// Where a generated position came from, through one map: the last segment at or before the column on its line (or
// the line's first), or null for code the map does not cover (a helper's).
function lookup(map, decoded, line, column) {
  const segments = decoded[line] ?? [];
  let hit = null;
  for (const s of segments) if (s[0] <= column || hit === null) hit = s;
  return hit && { source: map.sources[hit[1]], line: hit[2], column: hit[3] };
}

const loweredDecoded = decodeMappings(lowered.map.mappings);
const bundleDecoded = decodeMappings(bundleMap.mappings);

// The module and line a position came from, by esbuild's map, with the line's text; null where the map says nothing.
function moduleLine(line, column) {
  const at = lookup(bundleMap, bundleDecoded, line, column);
  if (!at) return null;
  const file = resolve(dirname(bundleFile), at.source);
  let text = "";
  try {
    text = readFileSync(file, "utf8").split("\n")[at.line]?.trim() ?? "";
  } catch {}
  return { where: `${repoPath(file)}:${at.line + 1}`, text };
}

// The bare-global names the MISSING rows list, which code may declare for itself.
const OWNABLE = new Set(MISSING.flatMap((row) => row[2] ?? []));

// For a hit in a helper (code no map covers: one esbuild or the ES5 lowering wrote), the helper's name and the source
// line that pulled it in: the first call to it that maps to a module, followed through helpers that call helpers.
function helperCaller(lines, i, origin) {
  const chain = [];
  for (let at = i, depth = 0; depth < 4; ++depth) {
    let name = null;
    for (let k = at; k >= 0 && !name; --k) name = /^\s*var (__\w+) = /.exec(lines[k])?.[1] ?? null;
    if (!name) break;
    chain.push(name);
    const call = new RegExp(`\\b${escapeRegExp(name)}\\(`);
    let next = -1;
    for (let k = 0; k < lines.length; ++k) {
      const m = call.exec(lines[k]);
      if (!m) continue;
      const from = origin ? origin(k, m.index) : null;
      if (from) return { chain, from };
      if (next < 0) next = k;
    }
    if (next < 0) break;
    at = next;
  }
  return { chain, from: null };
}

// Each MISSING kind's hit in `code`, named by the module line `origin` maps it to: the first that maps, else the first
// in a helper, named with the source line that called the helper. With no origin (the node SDK's own scan, which has
// no source map), a hit is named as the SDK's, with its line of the lowered code.
function scan(code, origin) {
  const scanned = blankForScan(code, OWNABLE);
  const lines = scanned.split("\n");
  const hits = [];
  for (const [re, what] of MISSING) {
    let helperHit = null;
    let found = null;
    for (let i = 0; i < lines.length && !found; ++i) {
      const m = re.exec(lines[i]);
      if (!m) continue;
      const from = origin ? origin(i, m.index) : null;
      if (from) found = `${from.where}: ${m[0].trim()} (${what}): ${from.text.slice(0, 120)}`;
      else if (!origin) found = `${m[0].trim()} (${what}) in the node SDK: ${code.split("\n")[i].trim().slice(0, 120)}`;
      else if (!helperHit) helperHit = { i, m };
    }
    if (!found && helperHit) {
      const { i, m } = helperHit;
      const { chain, from } = helperCaller(lines, i, origin);
      const helper = chain.length ? ` in the helper ${chain[0]}` : "";
      const through = chain.length > 1 ? ` (through ${chain.slice(1).join(", ")})` : "";
      const pulled = from ? `, which ${from.where} pulls in${through}: ${from.text.slice(0, 120)}`
                          : `: ${code.split("\n")[i].trim().slice(0, 120)}`;
      found = `${m[0].trim()} (${what})${helper} that the bundler or the ES5 lowering wrote${pulled}`;
    }
    if (found) hits.push(found);
  }
  return hits;
}

// The pack as esbuild bundled it, where every line but a helper's is a module's (so `async` is found at its own line,
// before the lowering turns it into a Promise in a helper), then as lowered, where the helpers the lowering adds are
// scanned too: a line of the lowered pack maps back through TypeScript's map to the bundle and esbuild's to the module.
let packHits = scan(bundleJs, moduleLine);
if (packHits.length === 0) {
  packHits = scan(es5, (line, column) => {
    if (line === 0) return null; // the "use strict" line is ours
    const inBundle = lookup(lowered.map, loweredDecoded, line - 1, column);
    return inBundle && moduleLine(inBundle.line, inBundle.column);
  });
}
if (packHits.length > 0) fail(`calls library functions MicroQuickJS does not have:\n  ${packHits.join("\n  ")}`);
// The whole SDK with every export kept, as check:portable scans its whole core: bundling drops what the pack does not
// import, and the scan is the only guard a path the pack never RUNS has. MicroQuickJS parses everything, so syntax is
// caught either way, but a missing library call fails only when executed.
const whole = await esbuild.build({
  ...bundleOptions,
  stdin: { contents: SDK.map((p) => `export * from ${JSON.stringify("./" + p)};`).join("\n"), resolveDir: REPO,
           loader: "ts" },
  format: "esm",
  metafile: false,
  treeShaking: false,
});
const wholeEs5 = lowerToEs5(whole.outputFiles[0].text.replace(/^export \{[\s\S]*?\};?\s*$/m, ""), false).code;
const sdkHits = scan(wholeEs5, null);
if (sdkHits.length > 0) {
  fail(`the node SDK calls library functions MicroQuickJS does not have:\n  ${sdkHits.join("\n  ")}`);
}
console.log("  ok: no library calls outside MicroQuickJS's stdlib, in the pack or anywhere in the SDK");

// ---- the reference run, under Node -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const lines = [];
const sandbox = { console: { log: (s) => lines.push(String(s)) } };
try {
  runInNewContext(es5 + EPILOGUE, sandbox, { filename: es5Name });
} catch (e) {
  fail(`defining its node types threw: ${e?.message ?? e}`);
}
// Line ends as "\n" on both sides of the comparison below (the engine's are read the same way, printed()), so a line a
// definition logs with its own "\r\n" compares as the line it is.
const reference = (lines.join("\n") + "\n").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
const types = lines.filter((l) => l.startsWith("{")).length;
if (types === 0) fail("registers no node type (graph/register.ts's registerScriptNodes)");
console.log(`  ok: defined ${types} node type(s) under Node`);

// ---- the bytecode ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

rmSync(WORK, { recursive: true, force: true });
mkdirSync(WORK, { recursive: true });
writeFileSync(join(WORK, es5Name), es5);

// mqjs in the work directory, with the bundle named by its file name alone: the bytecode carries the name it was
// compiled from, so an absolute path would make the bytes depend on the checkout. mqjs reports a parse error and still
// exits 0, writing nothing, so a missing output is the failure.
function compile(source, out, wide) {
  const run = spawnSync(MQJS, [...(wide ? [] : ["-m32"]), "-o", out, source], { cwd: WORK, encoding: "utf8" });
  if (run.status !== 0 || run.stderr || !existsSync(join(WORK, out))) {
    fail(`mqjs could not compile ${source}${wide ? "" : " (-m32)"}:\n${run.stderr}${run.stdout}`);
  }
  return readFileSync(join(WORK, out));
}
const bytecode64 = compile(es5Name, `${NAME}.mqjs64.bin`, true);
const bytecode32 = compile(es5Name, `${NAME}.mqjs32.bin`, false);
console.log(`  ok: compiled to bytecode, ${bytecode64.length} bytes at 64-bit and ${bytecode32.length} at 32-bit`);

// ---- the bytecode on the engine ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// mqjs writes its output through the C runtime's stdout, which on Windows is in text mode: each line ends "\r\n" there.
// Read as lines, as Node's transcript is, so the comparison is of what was printed.
const printed = (run) => run.stdout.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
// How a run ended when it did not exit: a signal (POSIX), or an exception code as its status (Windows, 0xC0000005 and
// the like, past any exit status a program returns). Null for an ordinary exit.
const crash = (run) => run.signal ?? (run.status > 255 ? `0x${run.status.toString(16).toUpperCase()}` : null);
// The least 64-bit context the engine sets itself up in, with mqjs's REPL stdlib, as measured: below it JS_NewContext
// writes past its buffer and dereferences the allocation that failed, rather than throwing. The manifest refuses a
// figure below it (cmake/packages.cmake); the box's own floor, per width and stdlib, is its loader's to enforce.
const LEAST_CONTEXT = 4096;
// What a failed run said, for a message: its error printing colours the text for a terminal.
const said = (run) => `${run.stderr}${printed(run)}`.replace(/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/g, "").trim();

writeFileSync(join(WORK, `${NAME}.transcript.js`), es5 + EPILOGUE);
compile(`${NAME}.transcript.js`, `${NAME}.transcript.bin`, true);
const run = spawnSync(MQJS, ["--memory-limit", String(TRANSCRIPT_HEAP), "-b", `${NAME}.transcript.bin`],
                      { cwd: WORK, encoding: "utf8" });
if (run.status !== 0) {
  const how = crash(run) ? `the engine crashed (${crash(run)})` : `exit ${run.status}`;
  fail(`its bytecode failed on ${ENGINE} (${how})${said(run) ? `: ${said(run)}` : ""}`);
}
const engineTranscript = printed(run);
if (engineTranscript !== reference) {
  const a = reference.split("\n");
  const b = engineTranscript.split("\n");
  let i = 0;
  while (i < a.length && a[i] === b[i]) ++i;
  fail(`${ENGINE} disagrees with Node at line ${i + 1} of the transcript:\n  node: ${a[i]}\n  mqjs: ${b[i]}`);
}
console.log(`  ok: ${ENGINE} runs the bytecode and matches Node byte for byte (${lines.length} lines)`);

const own = spawnSync(MQJS, ["--memory-limit", String(HEAP_BYTES), "-b", `${NAME}.mqjs64.bin`],
                      { cwd: WORK, encoding: "utf8" });
if (own.status !== 0) {
  const small = HEAP_BYTES < LEAST_CONTEXT ? `, as it does in a context under its least, ${LEAST_CONTEXT} bytes` : "";
  const how = crash(own) ? `the engine crashed (${crash(own)})${small}${said(own) ? `: ${said(own)}` : ""}` : said(own);
  fail(`its bytecode does not define its node types in its declared heap of ${HEAP_BYTES} bytes ` +
       `(the manifest's heapBytes): ${how}`);
}
console.log(`  ok: the pack's bytecode defines its node types in its declared heap (${HEAP_BYTES} bytes)`);

// ---- the outputs, now that every check has passed ----------------------------------------------------------------

mkdirSync(OUT_DIR, { recursive: true });
keep(join(OUT_DIR, es5Name), es5);
keep(join(OUT_DIR, `${NAME}.mqjs64.bin`), bytecode64);
keep(join(OUT_DIR, `${NAME}.mqjs32.bin`), bytecode32);
keep(join(OUT_DIR, `${NAME}.transcript.txt`), reference);
rmSync(WORK, { recursive: true, force: true });
console.log(`device pack ${NAME} OK (${repoPath(OUT_DIR)})`);
````
