- [ ] **Step 4: The manifest's script member, the seed pack, and the manifests that must be refused**

`cmake/packages.cmake`: `_retroplug_read_script` reads `retroplug.script` into global properties, refusing in words a
member that is not an object, one with no `entry` or an entry that does not exist, one without `"device": true or
false`, `device: false` (a desktop script pack, reserved: nothing builds one yet) and a `heapBytes` that is not a JSON
number, a whole number of bytes from 4096 to 524288 (4 KiB is the least 64-bit context the engine sets itself up in;
below it `JS_NewContext` writes past its buffer); a package may have `native`, `script` or both, neither being
refused; and `retroplug_script_pack(<package> [TARGET <t>])`, desktop only, is a custom target
(`retroplug-<package>-script-pack`) that runs the toolchain into `build/packages/<package>/script/` on every build of
it. `packages/devtest/package.json` gains `"script": { "entry": "ts/index.ts", "device": true, "heapBytes": 16384 }`
and `ts/index.ts` defines `rp.devtest.script-transpose` (a note on or off moved by `semitones` and clamped, from a
three-byte array of its own; everything else passed through), which `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.json` now
type-checks. The root `package.json`'s `test` script builds `retroplug-devtest-script-pack` beside `tjs-cli`.
`tests.cmake` holds every scratch manifest under `packages/native/test/packages/refused` to its own reason at each
configure (eleven new ones, with `scratch-pack.ts` as the entry they name), reads devtest's manifest and
`test/packages/read/ScriptOnly.json` (a script pack alone), and calls `retroplug_script_pack(devtest)`.

Create `packages/devtest/ts/index.ts`:

````ts
// The devtest script pack (packages/devtest/package.json's retroplug.script): a device pack of test node types, which
// the device-pack toolchain (packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs) compiles to MicroQuickJS bytecode
// through cmake/packages.cmake's retroplug_script_pack. Like the package's C++ types, no product that ships carries it;
// the tests build it, at both widths (packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack.test.ts).
import { defineNode, events } from "../../retroplug/src/graph/defineNode";
import { s } from "../../retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../retroplug/src/script/register";

const clamp7 = (v: number): number => (v < 0 ? 0 : v > 127 ? 127 : v);

// A note on or off moved by `semitones` and held to 0..127; every other message passed on as it came. Each keeps its
// frame and flags, and the output's capacity is its input's. A moved note goes out from a three-byte array of the
// node's own, refilled for each, so a warmed block allocates nothing.
export const scriptTransposeNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.devtest.script-transpose",
  name: "Script transpose (devtest)",
  category: "test",
  settings: s.object({ semitones: s.int({ min: -127, max: 127, default: 0 }) }),
  ports: { in: events.in(), out: events.out({ match: "in" }) },
  create: ({ settings }) => {
    let semitones = settings.semitones;
    const note = new Uint8Array(3);
    return {
      onSettings(next) {
        semitones = next.semitones;
      },
      process(b) {
        const messages = b.messages("in");
        for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i++) {
          const m = messages[i];
          const kind = m.data[0] & 0xf0;
          if ((kind === 0x80 || kind === 0x90) && m.data.length === 3) {
            note[0] = m.data[0];
            note[1] = clamp7(m.data[1] + semitones);
            note[2] = m.data[2];
            b.send("out", m.frame, note, m.flags);
          } else {
            b.send("out", m.frame, m.data, m.flags);
          }
        }
      },
    };
  },
});

registerScriptNodes([scriptTransposeNode]);
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack.test.ts`:

````ts
// The device-pack toolchain (scripts/build-device-pack.mjs, docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 6) and
// defineNode in MicroQuickJS's subset. A device pack's TypeScript is bundled against an allowlist, lowered to ES5,
// scanned for library calls the engine lacks and compiled to bytecode, and its definitions run under Node and as
// bytecode on the engine (the desktop build's mqjs, which `pnpm test` builds), whose transcripts must match byte for
// byte: check:portable's method, on feature/launchpad. Here:
//
// - test/graph/device-pack/scenario.ts, defineNode and its helpers at work as a device pack (every port kind a device
//   pack may have, every param type, settings and the ports that follow them, every refusal, a node's process on a
//   block), runs the same on both engines;
// - the toolchain refuses a pack that calls what the engine lacks (a Map, an `async`, a timer of mqjs's REPL, a method
//   whose name the SDK declares, a use beside a guard, a call in a helper the bundler wrote), naming the call and its
//   source line; one whose node has an audio port, as defineNode refuses it at definition, naming the node and the
//   port; one that imports outside its allowlist, naming the module and its importer; one the engine runs unlike Node,
//   naming the transcript line; and one whose bytecode does not define its node types in its declared heap;
// - the devtest package's script pack (packages/devtest/ts), which CMake compiles from its manifest
//   (retroplug_script_pack in packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake), has its bytecode at both widths, and the toolchain
//   run by hand on the same entry writes the same bytes.
//
// The toolchain is Node's (esbuild and TypeScript are not txiki modules), so the test runs it in a node child: the
// runner's own node (RP_NODE, which scripts/run-tests.mjs sets), else the node on the PATH when run by hand.
import { test, expect } from "../../testing/harness";

// Just enough of txiki's spawn, a child's pipe and its file reads, declared locally as bundle-no-zod.test.ts does.
interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  readFile(path: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  stat(path: string): Promise<unknown>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

// The suite runs from packages/retroplug.
const FIXTURES = "test/graph/device-pack";
const OUT = ".test-build/device-pack";
const DEVTEST_BYTECODE = "../../build/packages/devtest/script";
// What defineNode says of a device pack's audio port, after naming the node and the port.
const NO_AUDIO = "which a device pack's node cannot have: audio stays C++";
// And of a device pack's settings field named like an integer, after naming the node and the field.
const NO_ORDER = "which a device pack's settings cannot keep in order";

/** Whether a path exists. */
async function exists(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    await tjs.stat(path);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/** `part` is in `whole`, which the failure prints. */
function contains(whole: string, part: string): void {
  expect(whole.includes(part), `${JSON.stringify(part)} is not in:\n${whole}`).toBe(true);
}

/** The toolchain on one entry, into OUT/<name>: its exit status and what it printed. */
async function buildPack(entry: string, name: string, heapBytes: number, packDir?: string) {
  const args = [tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "scripts/build-device-pack.mjs", "--entry", entry, "--name", name,
                "--heap-bytes", String(heapBytes), "--out-dir", `${OUT}/${name}`];
  if (packDir) args.push("--pack-dir", packDir);
  const child = tjs.spawn(args, { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  // Both pipes drained beside the wait, so a child that fills one cannot block on it.
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  return { ok: !status.term_signal && status.exit_status === 0, out, err };
}

test("defineNode and its helpers run on MicroQuickJS as on Node, byte for byte", async () => {
  const run = await buildPack(`${FIXTURES}/scenario.ts`, "scenario", 65536);
  expect(run.ok, `the toolchain refused the scenario:\n${run.out}${run.err}`).toBe(true);
  contains(run.out, "matches Node byte for byte");
  // The transcript the two engines agreed on: what the scenario prints, then every registered node's descriptor.
  const transcript = new TextDecoder().decode(await tjs.readFile(`${OUT}/scenario/scenario.transcript.txt`));
  const lines = transcript.split("\n");
  console.log(`# scenario transcript: ${lines.length - 1} lines`);
  for (const line of [
    `an audio input: rp.test.portable.audio: port "in" is audio, ${NO_AUDIO}`,
    `audio by settings: rp.test.portable.audio-later: port "sound" is audio, ${NO_AUDIO}`,
    '__proto__ twice: rp.t: "__proto__" is used by more than one port or param',
    "toString once: accepted",
    'capacity stray field: rp.t: port "o": capacity: unknown field "frames"',
    "an enum twice: rp.t: param \"m\": an enum lists a value twice",
    "an int's fraction: rp.t: param \"i\": an int param needs whole-number min, max and default",
    'fan-in settings {"inputs":99}: node type "rp.test.portable.fan-in": settings: inputs: Too big: expected ' +
      "number to be <=8",
    "counter sent: out@0=144,63/0 out@5=128,4/0 count@31=36 out@0=144,69/0 out@5=128,10/0 count@31=42",
    `an integer-like settings field: rp.t: settings field "7" is a number, ${NO_ORDER}`,
    `one in an array's items: rp.t: settings field "taps[].0" is a number, ${NO_ORDER}`,
    "# 4 node type(s)",
  ])
    expect(lines.includes(line), line).toBe(true);
});

test("a device pack that calls what MicroQuickJS lacks is refused, naming the call and its source line", async () => {
  const map = await buildPack(`${FIXTURES}/missing-call.ts`, "missing-call", 65536);
  expect(map.ok).toBe(false);
  contains(map.err, "calls library functions MicroQuickJS does not have");
  contains(map.err, "packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/missing-call.ts:10: new Map");
  // Found as written, at its own line, before the lowering turns it into a Promise in a helper.
  const later = await buildPack(`${FIXTURES}/async-process.ts`, "async-process", 65536);
  expect(later.ok).toBe(false);
  contains(later.err, "packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/async-process.ts:14: async (async/await)");
  // Globals of upstream mqjs's REPL, which the toolchain's own runs have and the box's engine will not; a function the
  // pack declares itself under one of their names is its own.
  const host = await buildPack(`${FIXTURES}/host-global.ts`, "host-global", 65536);
  expect(host.ok).toBe(false);
  contains(host.err, "device-pack/host-global.ts:20: setTimeout( (a global of mqjs's REPL");
  contains(host.err, "device-pack/host-global.ts:21: console.warn (a console method other than log");
  expect(host.err.includes("load("), host.err).toBe(false);
  // A method call in process() whose name the bundled SDK also declares (defineNode's startsWith, settingsSchema's
  // `from`): a declaration of the name elsewhere makes no call the pack's own.
  const methods = await buildPack(`${FIXTURES}/method-calls.ts`, "method-calls", 65536);
  expect(methods.ok).toBe(false);
  contains(methods.err, "device-pack/method-calls.ts:16: Array.from (Array.from/of)");
  contains(methods.err, "device-pack/method-calls.ts:16: .startsWith( (String.raw");
  // A guard accepts only what runs when it holds: the else-branch's Symbol is refused.
  const unguarded = await buildPack(`${FIXTURES}/guard-else.ts`, "guard-else", 65536);
  expect(unguarded.ok).toBe(false);
  contains(unguarded.err, "device-pack/guard-else.ts:15: Symbol (Symbol/Reflect/Proxy/Promise/WeakRef/Intl)");
  // A call in a helper the bundler wrote (esbuild's `using` reads Symbol), named with the line that pulled it in.
  const helper = await buildPack(`${FIXTURES}/using-resource.ts`, "using-resource", 65536);
  expect(helper.ok).toBe(false);
  contains(
    helper.err,
    "Symbol (Symbol/Reflect/Proxy/Promise/WeakRef/Intl) in the helper __knownSymbol that the bundler or the ES5 " +
      "lowering wrote, which packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/using-resource.ts:15 pulls in (through __using)",
  );
});

test("a device pack the engine runs unlike Node is refused, at the transcript line where they part", async () => {
  // A computed "__proto__" key, which the ES5 lowering makes an assignment: Node sets the prototype, the engine an own
  // key, so the node has one port on the reference and two on the engine.
  const run = await buildPack(`${FIXTURES}/proto-key.ts`, "proto-key", 65536);
  expect(run.ok).toBe(false);
  contains(run.err, "MicroQuickJS (deps/mquickjs, 6d4d7eb) disagrees with Node at line 2 of the transcript");
  contains(run.err, '"ports":[{"id":"out","dir":"out","kind":"events"}]');
  contains(run.err, '"ports":[{"id":"__proto__","dir":"in","kind":"events"},{"id":"out","dir":"out","kind":"events"}]');
  // Refused after its bytecode was made: nothing of it is left, neither an output nor the work files.
  for (const file of ["proto-key.js", "proto-key.mqjs64.bin", "proto-key.mqjs32.bin", "proto-key.transcript.txt",
                      ".proto-key.work"])
    expect(await exists(`${OUT}/proto-key/${file}`), file).toBe(false);
});

// A bytecode file's header (mquickjs.h's JSBytecodeHeader): magic 0xacfb and the version, whose bit 15 says 64-bit,
// then the address it is relocated to, which the toolchain leaves at 0 (the loader relocates it to where it lies).
function header(bytes: Uint8Array, wide: boolean) {
  const word = (at: number) => bytes[at] | (bytes[at + 1] << 8);
  let base = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < (wide ? 8 : 4); i++) base += bytes[4 + i];
  return { magic: word(0), version: word(2), base };
}

test("devtest's script pack is built from its manifest at both widths, the same bytes every time", async () => {
  const wide = await tjs.readFile(`${DEVTEST_BYTECODE}/devtest.mqjs64.bin`);
  const narrow = await tjs.readFile(`${DEVTEST_BYTECODE}/devtest.mqjs32.bin`);
  console.log(`# devtest bytecode: ${wide.length} bytes at 64-bit, ${narrow.length} at 32-bit`);
  expect(header(wide, true)).toEqual({ magic: 0xacfb, version: 0x8001, base: 0 });
  expect(header(narrow, false)).toEqual({ magic: 0xacfb, version: 0x0001, base: 0 });
  // A pointer's width, and no more, between them: the 32-bit form is the smaller.
  expect(narrow.length > 1024 && narrow.length < wide.length).toBe(true);
  // The toolchain by hand, on the entry and heap the manifest names, writes what CMake's target wrote.
  const run = await buildPack("../devtest/ts/index.ts", "devtest", 16384, "../devtest");
  expect(run.ok, `${run.out}${run.err}`).toBe(true);
  const same = async (file: string, built: Uint8Array) => {
    const again = await tjs.readFile(`${OUT}/devtest/${file}`);
    return again.length === built.length && again.every((b, i) => b === built[i]);
  };
  expect(await same("devtest.mqjs64.bin", wide)).toBe(true);
  expect(await same("devtest.mqjs32.bin", narrow)).toBe(true);
});
````

````ts
// A device pack whose process is asynchronous: the box's engine has no Promise, so the device-pack toolchain must
// refuse it, naming the `async` and this file's line (test/graph/device-pack.test.ts).
import { defineNode, events } from "../../../src/graph/defineNode";
import type { Block } from "../../../src/graph/defineNode";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../../src/script/register";

const later = (b: Block): Block => b;

export const slowThru = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.device.slow-thru",
  ports: { in: events.in(), out: events.out({ match: "in" }) },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      void (async () => {
        const block = await later(b);
        block.send("out", 0, [0xf8]);
      })();
    },
  }),
});

registerScriptNodes([slowThru]);
````

````ts
// A device pack that tests for Symbol and then uses it on the branch where the test failed: only what runs when a guard
// holds is accepted, so the else-branch's Symbol must be refused, naming its line (test/graph/device-pack.test.ts).
import { defineNode, events } from "../../../src/graph/defineNode";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../../src/script/register";

export const iterates = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.device.iterates",
  ports: { in: events.in() },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      let key: unknown = 0;
      if (typeof Symbol === "function") {
        key = 1;
      } else {
        key = Symbol.iterator;
      }
      void b.messages(String(key));
    },
  }),
});

registerScriptNodes([iterates]);
````

````ts
// A device pack that reaches for globals upstream mqjs's REPL has and the box's engine will not: a timer (asynchrony a
// device pack may not have) and console.warn. The device-pack toolchain must refuse it, naming each and its line
// (test/graph/device-pack.test.ts). Its own function named `load` is its own, and passes.
import { defineNode, events } from "../../../src/graph/defineNode";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../../src/script/register";

declare function setTimeout(f: () => void, ms: number): number;
declare const console: { log(s: string): void; warn(s: string): void };

function load(n: number): number {
  return n + 1;
}

export const later = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.device.later",
  ports: { in: events.in(), out: events.out({ match: "in" }) },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const n = load(b.messages("in").length);
      setTimeout(() => b.send("out", 0, [n]), 1);
      console.warn("deferred");
    },
  }),
});

registerScriptNodes([later]);
````

````ts
// A device pack whose process() calls startsWith and Array.from, which MicroQuickJS does not have, while the node SDK
// it bundles declares functions of those names (defineNode's startsWith, settingsSchema's `from`): a declaration
// elsewhere must not make a method call the pack's own. The device-pack toolchain must refuse it, naming each call and
// its line (test/graph/device-pack.test.ts).
import { defineNode, events } from "../../../src/graph/defineNode";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../../src/script/register";

export const sysexOnly = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.device.sysex-only",
  ports: { in: events.in(), out: events.out({ match: "in" }) },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const ms = b.messages("in");
      for (let i = 0; i < ms.length; i++) {
        const hex = ms[i].data[0].toString(16);
        if (hex.startsWith("f0")) b.send("out", ms[i].frame, Array.from(ms[i].data));
      }
    },
  }),
});

registerScriptNodes([sysexOnly]);
````

````ts
// defineNode and its helpers at work, line by line, as a device pack: the device-pack toolchain
// (scripts/build-device-pack.mjs) runs it under Node and as MicroQuickJS bytecode, and the two transcripts must match
// byte for byte (test/graph/device-pack.test.ts). What a device pack's definitions resolve to, refuse and say is then
// the same on the box's engine as here. Every line is the helpers' own work: nothing printed is an engine's message.
import {
  audio, bytes, channels, control, defineNode, events, layoutChannels, link, param, resource, startValue,
} from "../../../src/graph/defineNode";
import type { Block, Message, PortSpec } from "../../../src/graph/defineNode";
import { plainId, wellFormed } from "../../../src/graph/descriptor";
import { s } from "../../../src/graph/settingsSchema";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../../src/script/register";

const log = (line: string): void => console.log(line);
const noop = () => ({ process() {} });

// What f does: "accepted", or the message it threw. Only the helpers' own Errors reach here.
function attempt(what: string, f: () => unknown): void {
  try {
    f();
    log(`${what}: accepted`);
  } catch (e) {
    log(`${what}: ${(e as Error).message}`);
  }
}

function ownKey<T>(key: string, value: T): Record<string, T> {
  const map: Record<string, T> = {};
  Object.defineProperty(map, key, { value, enumerable: true, writable: true, configurable: true });
  return map;
}

// ---- the descriptor's own rules ----

const layouts = ["mono", "stereo", "5.1", "7.1", "discrete(3)", "discrete(0)", "discrete(4294967296)", "any", "quad"];
for (const name of layouts)
  log(`layoutChannels(${name}) = ${String(layoutChannels(name))}`);
for (const id of ["a", "", "a b", "tab\t", "del\u007f", "lone\ud800", "pair😀", "rp.core.midi-filter"])
  log(`plainId(${JSON.stringify(id)}) = ${plainId(id)}, wellFormed = ${wellFormed(id)}`);

// ---- a node with every port kind a device pack may have, every param type, and an exclusive group ----

const everything = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.portable.everything",
  version: "2.1.0",
  name: "Everything",
  category: "test",
  unique: true,
  ports: {
    out: events.out({ messages: 64, bytes: 1024 }),
    "out.alt": events.out({ messages: 8 }),
    midi: events.in(),
    serial: bytes.in(),
    serialOut: bytes.out({ match: "serial" }),
    gate: control.in(),
    level: control.out(),
    rom: resource.in("rp.rom"),
    sram: resource.write("rp.sram"),
    made: resource.out("rp.sample"),
    cart: link(),
  },
  params: {
    gain: param.float({ name: "Gain", min: -60, max: 12, default: 0, unit: "dB" }),
    steps: param.int({ name: "Steps", min: 1, max: 16, default: 4, unit: "" }),
    on: param.bool({ name: "On" }),
    mode: param.enum({ name: "Mode", values: ["a", "b", "c"], default: "b" }),
  },
  exclusive: [["out", "level"], ["out.*"]],
  create: noop,
});
log(`everything: ${JSON.stringify(everything.descriptor())}`);

// ---- settings, and ports that follow them ----

const fanIn = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.portable.fan-in",
  settings: s.object({
    inputs: s.int({ min: 1, max: 8, default: 2 }),
    mode: s.enum(["merge", "first"], "merge"),
    thru: s.bool(true),
    scale: s.number(0.5),
    label: s.string("fan"),
    taps: s.array(s.object({ at: s.int({ default: 0 }), on: s.bool(false) }),
                  [{ at: 3 } as { at: number; on: boolean }]),
    blob: s.json<{ k: number }>({ k: 1 }),
  }),
  ports: (settings) => {
    const ports: Record<string, PortSpec> = {};
    for (let k = 1; k <= settings.inputs; ++k) ports[`in${k}`] = events.in();
    ports.out = events.out({ match: "in1" });
    return ports;
  },
  params: (settings): Record<string, ReturnType<typeof param.bool>> =>
    settings.thru ? { thru: param.bool({ name: "Thru", default: true }) } : {},
  reshapes: true,
  create: noop,
});
log(`fan-in defaults: ${JSON.stringify(fanIn.parseSettings({}))}`);
log(`fan-in, 4 inputs: ${JSON.stringify(fanIn.layout(fanIn.parseSettings({ inputs: 4, thru: false })))}`);
log(`fan-in, taps: ${JSON.stringify(fanIn.parseSettings({ taps: [{ on: true }, { at: 7 }], toString: 1 }))}`);
const refusedSettings = [{ inputs: 99 }, { inputs: 1.5 }, { inputs: "2" }, { mode: "x" }, { taps: [1] },
                         { scale: "x" }];
for (const raw of [...refusedSettings, [], null, "x", 3])
  attempt(`fan-in settings ${JSON.stringify(raw)}`, () => fanIn.parseSettings(raw));
log(`fan-in schema: ${JSON.stringify(fanIn.descriptor().settings)}`);

// ---- what a device pack refuses, and what every pack refuses ----

attempt("an audio input", () =>
  defineNode({ id: "rp.test.portable.audio", ports: { in: audio.in(), out: events.out() }, create: noop }));
attempt("an audio output", () =>
  defineNode({
    id: "rp.test.portable.audio-out",
    ports: { midi: events.in(), out: audio.out(channels.stereo()) },
    create: noop,
  }));
// Defined, since its default layout has none, and refused the moment a layout would.
const audioLater = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.portable.audio-later",
  settings: s.object({ withAudio: s.bool(false) }),
  ports: (st): Record<string, PortSpec> => (st.withAudio ? { sound: audio.in() } : { midi: events.in() }),
  create: noop,
});
attempt("audio by settings", () => audioLater.layout(audioLater.parseSettings({ withAudio: true })));

// A definition with nothing but what each case gives: no ports, a create that does nothing.
const node = (given: Record<string, unknown>) =>
  defineNode({ id: "rp.t", ports: {}, create: noop, ...given } as never);

const refusals: [string, () => unknown][] = [
  ["a bad id", () => node({ id: "rp test" })],
  ["a bad dir", () => node({ ports: { x: { dir: "up", kind: "events" } as unknown as PortSpec } })],
  ["a bad kind", () => node({ ports: { x: { dir: "in", kind: "video" } as unknown as PortSpec } })],
  ["a link that is not", () => node({ ports: { x: { dir: "in", kind: "link" } as unknown as PortSpec } })],
  ["an input's capacity", () =>
    node({ ports: { x: { dir: "in", kind: "events", capacity: { messages: 2 } } as unknown as PortSpec } })],
  ["capacity match and size", () =>
    node({ ports: { i: events.in(), o: events.out({ match: "i", messages: 2 } as never) } })],
  ["capacity stray field", () => node({ ports: { o: events.out({ messages: 2, frames: 3 } as never) } })],
  ["capacity empty", () => node({ ports: { o: events.out({ messages: undefined }) } })],
  ["capacity zero", () => node({ ports: { o: events.out({ messages: 0 }) } })],
  ["capacity fraction", () => node({ ports: { o: bytes.out({ bytes: 1.5 }) } })],
  ["capacity too big", () => node({ ports: { o: events.out({ messages: 1048577 }) } })],
  ["capacity not an object", () => node({ ports: { o: events.out(7 as never) } })],
  ["capacity match a bytes input", () => node({ ports: { i: bytes.in(), o: events.out({ match: "i" }) } })],
  ["capacity match nothing", () => node({ ports: { o: bytes.out({ match: "nope" }) } })],
  ["a port and a param share an id", () =>
    node({ ports: { x: events.in() }, params: { x: param.bool({ name: "X" }) } })],
  // Own keys made with defineProperty: an assignment, or a computed key as the ES5 lowering spells it (one), sets the
  // prototype under Node and an own key under MicroQuickJS, which has no __proto__ accessor.
  ["__proto__ twice", () =>
    node({ ports: ownKey("__proto__", events.in()), params: ownKey("__proto__", param.bool({ name: "P" })) })],
  ["toString once", () => node({ ports: { toString: events.in(), constructor: events.out() } })],
  ["an integer-like id", () => node({ ports: { ["7"]: events.in() } })],
  ["a star in an id", () => node({ ports: { "a*": events.in() } })],
  ["a resource port's type", () => node({ ports: { r: resource.in("") } })],
  ["a written resource output", () =>
    node({ ports: { r: { dir: "out", kind: "resource", resourceType: "x", access: "write" } as never } })],
  ["an enum twice", () => node({ params: { m: param.enum({ name: "M", values: ["a", "b", "a"], default: "a" }) } })],
  ["an enum's default", () => node({ params: { m: param.enum({ name: "M", values: ["a"], default: "z" }) } })],
  ["an empty enum", () => node({ params: { m: param.enum({ name: "M", values: [], default: "" }) } })],
  ["a float's infinity", () => node({ params: { f: param.float({ name: "F", min: 0, max: 1 / 0, default: 0 }) } })],
  ["an int's fraction", () => node({ params: { i: param.int({ name: "I", min: 0, max: 9, default: 2.5 }) } })],
  ["min above max", () => node({ params: { f: param.float({ name: "F", min: 2, max: 1, default: 1 }) } })],
  ["default outside", () => node({ params: { f: param.float({ name: "F", min: 0, max: 1, default: 2 }) } })],
  ["a bool's default", () => node({ params: { b: { type: "bool", name: "B", default: 1 } as never } })],
  ["a param type", () => node({ params: { b: { type: "complex", name: "B" } as never } })],
  ["a unit", () => node({ params: { b: { type: "bool", name: "B", default: true, unit: 3 } as never } })],
  ["unique false", () => node({ unique: false as never })],
  ["reshapes false", () => node({ reshapes: false as never })],
  ["requires.heap", () => node({ requires: { heap: "yes" as never } })],
  ["a version", () => node({ version: 5 as never })],
  ["an empty exclusive group", () => node({ ports: { o: events.out() }, exclusive: [[]] })],
  ["an exclusive input", () => node({ ports: { i: events.in(), o: events.out() }, exclusive: [["i"]] })],
  ["exclusive overlap", () =>
    node({ ports: { "o.a": events.out(), "o.b": events.out() }, exclusive: [["o.*", "o.a"]] })],
  ["exclusive twice", () => node({ ports: { o: events.out() }, exclusive: [["o", "o"]] })],
  ["an integer-like settings field", () => node({ settings: s.object({ ["7"]: s.bool(false) }) })],
  ["one in an array's items", () =>
    node({ settings: s.object({ taps: s.array(s.object({ ["0"]: s.int({ default: 1 }) }), []) }) })],
  ["an int schema's bounds", () => s.int({ min: 3, max: 1, default: 2 })],
  ["an int schema's default", () => s.int({ min: 0, max: 9, default: 12 })],
  ["an enum schema twice", () => s.enum(["x", "y", "x"], "x")],
  ["an array schema's default", () => s.array(s.int({ default: 0 }), [1, "2" as never])],
];
for (const [what, f] of refusals) attempt(what, f);

// ---- a node at work, on a block of the script host's shape ----

const counter = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.portable.counter",
  settings: s.object({ step: s.int({ min: 1, max: 4, default: 1 }) }),
  ports: { in: events.in(), out: events.out({ match: "in" }), count: control.out(), rate: control.in() },
  create: ({ settings }) => {
    let total = 0;
    const out = new Uint8Array(2);
    return {
      process(b: Block) {
        const ms = b.messages("in");
        for (let i = 0; i < ms.length; i++) {
          total += settings.step;
          out[0] = ms[i].data[0];
          out[1] = (ms[i].data[1] + total) & 0x7f;
          b.send("out", ms[i].frame, out, ms[i].flags);
        }
        b.emit("count", b.frames - 1, total + startValue(b.control("rate")));
      },
    };
  },
});
const instance = counter.create({ settings: counter.parseSettings({ step: 3 }), sampleRate: 48000, maxFrames: 64 });
const sent: string[] = [];
const message = (frame: number, data: number[]): Message => ({ frame, data: new Uint8Array(data), flags: 0 });
const block = {
  frames: 32,
  transport: { sampleRate: 48000, tempo: 120, ppq: 0, playing: false },
  audio: () => [],
  messages: () => [message(0, [0x90, 60]), message(5, [0x80, 126])],
  send: (port: string, frame: number, data: ArrayLike<number>, flags?: number) => {
    sent.push(`${port}@${frame}=${Array.prototype.join.call(data, ",")}/${flags ?? 0}`);
    return true;
  },
  control: () => ({ start: 10, changes: [{ frame: 0, value: 20 }, { frame: 0, value: 30 }, { frame: 9, value: 40 }] }),
  emit: (port: string, frame: number, value: number) => {
    sent.push(`${port}@${frame}=${value}`);
    return true;
  },
} as Block;
instance.process(block);
instance.process(block);
log(`counter sent: ${sent.join(" ")}`);

registerScriptNodes([everything, fanIn, audioLater, counter]);
````

````ts
  ports: { in: events.in() },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {

      void held;

  }),
});
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to the day the prototype's
hashes were taken against, 4 November 2026 (the command spells the string out), as the gate's record does
(`/tmp/e4pro/gate-commands.txt`); nothing else may differ, and the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the
date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash compares only an image built from this worktree's path,
against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check, `/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same
Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1: an image built elsewhere (the `env
-i` runs' clones under `/tmp/e4-ci`, a scratch worktree) is judged by its sizes, never hashed.

````bash
  target that compiles one; the configure's scratch manifests hold each new refusal.
````

### Task 2: the MicroQuickJS script host, and package memory in the SDK and the loader

Design sections 4 and 5 and section 8's second commit. `MqjsHost` (`packages/graph-runtime/native/src/script/`,
beside the loader) runs a device pack's nodes on MicroQuickJS: one portable source built two ways, as `graph/node.hpp`
is. The device build (`RP_DEVICE`: no heap, no exceptions, no RTTI) registers a pack's types from the ids its build
recorded and runs no JavaScript to do it, keeps static storage for `RP_MQJS_MAX_PACKS` x `RP_MQJS_MAX_TYPES` (4 x 16 by
default), creates a node from the blob's msgpack and runs it in the pack's context; the desktop build adds the
descriptors, `layout_for`, prepare / commit / release and `rp.sdk.settings-json/1` from a control context per pack per
process, so `exportPlan` writes a script node's settings. RetroPlug's own standard library (`rp_mqjs_stdlib.c`) and the
generated tables (`rp_mqjs_table.c`) give the engine the block API's classes. A pack's memory is its package's: the
node SDK's `rp_package` gains `memory` and `ctx`, `rp.host.packages/1` hands a node its package's block, and the loader
sizes, places, sets up and tears down each package's memory in its one pass. The toolchain now runs its transcript and
heap check on `retroplug-mqjs-run`, the runner over our stdlib, and writes the pack's C sources.

A red comes first, on Task 1's binary as it is. Then package memory in the SDK, the loader and the desktop's hosts, the
script host and its CMake, the packs wired into the products, the exporter and the toolchain, and the tests. The tree is
built once, in Step 6: build nothing in Steps 2 to 5.

- [ ] **Step 2: Package memory: the SDK, the loader and the desktop's hosts**

`rp_node.h`: `rp_package` gains `const rp_package_memory* memory` (`name`, `query`, `setup`, `teardown`) and `void*
ctx`, last, so every C++ package's four-field aggregate initialiser leaves them null, and the ABI note names them;
`rp.host.packages/1` gives a node its package's block. `rp_script.h` holds the script host's interfaces a host answers
or reads: `rp.script.fault/1` (the reason; threw, deadline, heap, refused), `rp.script.heap/1`, `rp.host.clock/1`
(micros and a deadline; 0 is the box's 10 ms) and `rp.host.script-log/1` (where `console.log` goes), and the desktop's
default deadline (`RP_SCRIPT_DESKTOP_DEADLINE_MICROS`, 500000). `PlanLoader` sizes each package with memory once in
`layout()`'s one pass and places it after the plan's structures and before the nodes, in the order the plan first
names one of its types; run-up sets it up before any node and unwinding and `unloadPlan` tear it down after the last;
the nodes are created under a host of the loader's own (`LoadedPlan::host`) that answers `rp.host.packages/1` and
forwards everything else; new codes `package-memory` and `package-setup`, an overrun being `arena` with the pack
named; `PlanSize` gains `structureBytes`, `packageBytes` and `packages`, and the blob's format does not change.
`graph/Text.hpp` is the one text builder, its writers out of line (`RP_NOINLINE`), which makes the device loader
smaller than before with the package pass in it. `graph/PackageMemory` is the desktop's answer, allocating and setting
a package up at its first ask; GraphHost holds one, torn down after `live_.clear()`. `graph/ThreadClock.hpp` is the
thread CPU clock the desktop times a script call by (`CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID`, `GetThreadTimes`).

````cpp
/* rp_script.h - what a host and a script node say to each other beyond the node ABI (graph/rp_node.h), for the
 * MicroQuickJS script host (graph-runtime's script/MqjsHost.hpp, docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 4).
 * Plain C, so a device's host (the box) answers the host's half without the script host's header, and the exporter
 * reads a script node's fault with no more than this.
 *
 * Every id is asked by rp_get_interface as any optional interface is: a host's through rp_host.get_interface, a node's
 * through its vtable's. A host that offers neither host interface is still a host a script node runs under. */
#ifndef RP_SCRIPT_H
#define RP_SCRIPT_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "graph/rp_node.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* The clock a host offers its script nodes' deadline [audio]: microseconds from any start, on the thread that runs
 * blocks, 0 when it cannot read one (a call it could not time runs untimed, never at once past its deadline).
 * deadline_micros is each call's deadline; 0 asks the script host's default for a host's clock (the box's figure,
 * script/MqjsHost.hpp's kHostClockDeadlineMicros). */
#define RP_HOST_CLOCK_INTERFACE "rp.host.clock/1"
typedef struct rp_host_clock {
    void*    ctx;
    uint64_t (*micros)(void* ctx);
    uint32_t deadline_micros;
} rp_host_clock;

/* The deadline a desktop times a script node's call by, by the calling thread's CPU time, when its host offers no
 * clock, and the one the exporter's trial load offers (script/MqjsHost.hpp says why it is this long). */
#define RP_SCRIPT_DESKTOP_DEADLINE_MICROS 500000u

/* Where a script pack's console.log goes [audio]: the bytes it prints, its newline included, in pieces of any size. A
 * host that offers none drops what a pack logs. A string argument is written as it is; any other is MicroQuickJS's own
 * print of the value (JS_PrintValueF, which mquickjs_priv.h's JS_DUMP builds in: an engine built without it writes
 * nothing for one). */
#define RP_HOST_SCRIPT_LOG_INTERFACE "rp.host.script-log/1"
typedef struct rp_host_script_log {
    void* ctx;
    void (*write)(void* ctx, const char* text, size_t size);
} rp_host_script_log;

/* A script node's fault, through the node's get_interface [any, once the node has faulted, or while no call into it
 * runs]: the words of its first fault, NUL-terminated, or null while it has none; and its kind (RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_*, 0
 * for none). A script node's instance is made at its first call on the thread that runs blocks, so a fault create
 * or its first block causes is there after one block: the exporter's trial load runs one, then reads every node's. */
#define RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_INTERFACE "rp.script.fault/1"
enum {
    RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_THREW = 1,    /* a call threw (create, layout, process or a hook) */
    RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_DEADLINE = 2, /* a call ran past its deadline */
    RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_HEAP = 3,     /* its pack's heap ran out, in its call or another node's */
    RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_REFUSED = 4   /* what a call returned, or what it was handed, breaks the contract */
};
typedef struct rp_script_fault {
    const char* (*reason)(rp_node* node);
    uint32_t (*kind)(rp_node* node);
} rp_script_fault;

/* A script node's pack's context as it stands, through the node's get_interface [the thread that runs blocks, or
 * while none runs], read from the engine's own JSContext. `collect` runs a collection first, so `heap` is what the
 * live objects take; without, it is how far the heap has grown since the last collection, which a block that allocates
 * nothing leaves where it was. `bytes` is the context's buffer (the manifest's heapBytes), `fixed` what MicroQuickJS
 * takes of it before its heap (its JSContext and the class prototypes) and `stack` the stack's depth at the call.
 * False while the node has no instance (before its first call on that thread). */
#define RP_SCRIPT_HEAP_INTERFACE "rp.script.heap/1"
typedef struct rp_script_heap_use {
    size_t bytes;
    size_t fixed;
    size_t heap;
    size_t stack;
} rp_script_heap_use;
typedef struct rp_script_heap {
    bool (*use)(rp_node* node, bool collect, rp_script_heap_use* out);
} rp_script_heap;

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* RP_SCRIPT_H */
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <string_view>

#include "graph/noinline.hpp"

namespace rp::graph {

// A sentence built into a fixed buffer, cut where it no longer fits: an rp_error's text, or any other a portable piece
// of the runtime writes (the plan loader's refusals, the MicroQuickJS host's faults), with no heap. Its writes are out
// of line: every refusal builds one, and a device keeps one copy of each rather than one a refusal.
struct Text {
    char*       out;
    std::size_t capacity;
    std::size_t length = 0;

    Text(char* buffer, std::size_t size) : out(buffer), capacity(size) { out[0] = '\0'; }
    RP_NOINLINE Text& put(const char* s, std::size_t n) {
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n && length + 1 < capacity; ++i) out[length++] = s[i];
        out[length] = '\0';
        return *this;
    }
    Text& operator<<(const char* s) { return put(s, std::strlen(s)); }
    Text& operator<<(std::string_view s) { return put(s.data(), s.size()); }
    RP_NOINLINE Text& operator<<(std::uint64_t v) {
        char digits[20];
        std::size_t n = 0;
        do {
            digits[n++] = static_cast<char>('0' + v % 10);
            v /= 10;
        } while (v);
        while (n) put(&digits[--n], 1);
        return *this;
    }
    Text& hex(std::uint32_t v) {
        char digits[10] = {'0', 'x'};
        for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) digits[2 + i] = "0123456789abcdef"[(v >> (28 - 4 * i)) & 0xF];
        return put(digits, 10);
    }
    // A string from outside, quoted: a type id or a node id, which may hold anything the document did.
    RP_NOINLINE Text& quoted(std::string_view s) { return *this << "\"" << s << "\""; }
};

}  // namespace rp::graph
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The calling thread's CPU time, in microseconds (0 where it cannot be read): what a desktop host times a script
// node's deadline by when it offers no clock of its own (script/MqjsHost.hpp), and the clock the exporter's trial load
// offers (graph/PlanExport.hpp). A preemption, or any stall that is not the thread's own work, costs it nothing.
// Windows counts it in scheduler ticks of about 15.6 ms. Desktop only.

#include <cstdint>

#if defined(_WIN32)
#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#endif
#ifndef NOMINMAX
#define NOMINMAX
#endif
#include <windows.h>
#else
#include <ctime>
#endif

namespace rp::graph {

inline std::uint64_t threadCpuMicros(void* = nullptr) {
#if defined(_WIN32)
    FILETIME created{}, exited{}, kernel{}, user{};
    if (!::GetThreadTimes(::GetCurrentThread(), &created, &exited, &kernel, &user)) return 0;
    const auto us = [](const FILETIME& f) {
        return ((static_cast<std::uint64_t>(f.dwHighDateTime) << 32) | f.dwLowDateTime) / 10;
    };
    return us(kernel) + us(user);
#else
    timespec t{};
    if (clock_gettime(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID, &t) != 0) return 0;
    return static_cast<std::uint64_t>(t.tv_sec) * 1000000 + static_cast<std::uint64_t>(t.tv_nsec) / 1000;
#endif
}

}  // namespace rp::graph
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <mutex>
#include <vector>

#include "graph/rp_node.h"

namespace rp::graph {

// Package memory as a desktop host gives it (rp_package_memory, docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 5): a
// block of the host's own for each package with memory that one of its nodes asks for (rp.host.packages/1, which a
// node's create asks), sized, allocated and set up at that first ask, and torn down and freed when the host goes, after
// its nodes. Where the device's loader sets every package of a plan up before its first node (graph/PlanLoader.hpp),
// a desktop host plans document after document, so a package is set up when the first node that needs it is created,
// and kept for the host's life. Desktop only: it allocates.
//
// One per host: GraphHost holds one, and the exporter one for the plan it makes. The host answers
// RP_HOST_PACKAGES_INTERFACE with service(), and destroys every node before clear() (or the destructor) tears the
// packages down. memory() is the control thread's; a mutex keeps two control threads of one host from setting one
// package up twice.
class PackageMemory {
public:
    PackageMemory() = default;
    ~PackageMemory() { clear(); }
    PackageMemory(const PackageMemory&) = delete;
    PackageMemory& operator=(const PackageMemory&) = delete;

    // What the host answers rp.host.packages/1 with.
    const rp_host_packages* service() const { return &service_; }
    // Every package torn down, the last set up first, and its block freed: once no node made under them is left.
    void clear();
    // The packages set up so far.
    std::size_t size() const;

private:
    struct Block {
        const rp_package* package = nullptr;
        void*             memory = nullptr;
        std::size_t       align = 0;
    };
    static void* memory(void* ctx, const rp_package* package, rp_error* err);

    mutable std::mutex mutex_;
    std::vector<Block> blocks_;
    rp_host_packages   service_{this, &PackageMemory::memory};
};

}  // namespace rp::graph
````

Create `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/graph/PackageMemory.cpp`:

````cpp
#include "graph/PackageMemory.hpp"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <new>

namespace rp::graph {

namespace {

void writeError(rp_error* err, const char* name, const char* what, const char* why) {
    if (err) std::snprintf(err->message, sizeof err->message, "the \"%.48s\" pack%s%.160s", name, what, why);
}

}  // namespace

void* PackageMemory::memory(void* ctx, const rp_package* package, rp_error* err) {
    auto* self = static_cast<PackageMemory*>(ctx);
    if (!package || !package->memory) {
        if (err) std::snprintf(err->message, sizeof err->message, "%s", "the package has no memory of its own");
        return nullptr;
    }
    const rp_package_memory& hooks = *package->memory;
    const char* name = hooks.name ? hooks.name : "unnamed";
    const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(self->mutex_);
    for (const Block& b : self->blocks_)
        if (b.package == package) return b.memory;
    if (!hooks.query || !hooks.setup || !hooks.teardown) {
        writeError(err, name, " has package memory without its query, setup and teardown", "");
        return nullptr;
    }
    rp_memory_req req{};
    rp_error why{};
    if (!hooks.query(package, &req, &why)) {
        writeError(err, name, "'s memory cannot be sized: ", why.message);
        return nullptr;
    }
    std::size_t align = req.align ? req.align : alignof(std::max_align_t);
    if ((align & (align - 1)) != 0) {
        writeError(err, name, " asked for an alignment that is not a power of two", "");
        return nullptr;
    }
    const std::size_t size = req.size ? req.size : 1;
    void* block = ::operator new(size, std::align_val_t(align), std::nothrow);
    if (!block) {
        writeError(err, name, "'s memory could not be allocated", "");
        return nullptr;
    }
    std::memset(block, 0, size);
    if (!hooks.setup(package, block, &why)) {
        ::operator delete(block, std::align_val_t(align));
        writeError(err, name, " would not set up in its memory: ", why.message);
        return nullptr;
    }
    self->blocks_.push_back({package, block, align});
    return block;
}

void PackageMemory::clear() {
    const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
    while (!blocks_.empty()) {
        const Block b = blocks_.back();
        blocks_.pop_back();
        b.package->memory->teardown(b.package, b.memory);
        ::operator delete(b.memory, std::align_val_t(b.align));
    }
}

std::size_t PackageMemory::size() const {
    const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mutex_);
    return blocks_.size();
}

}  // namespace rp::graph
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The script host, its standard library and its runner**

`rp_mqjs.h` is the C side the host and the engine share, and `rp_mqjs_pack.h` the struct a pack's generated source
defines (bytecode, size, `heap_bytes`, type ids). `rp_mqjs_engine.c` includes `mquickjs.c` whole, unpatched, and reads
the context's memory figures (`rp_mqjs_memory_of`). `rp_mqjs_stdlib.c` includes upstream's `mqjs_stdlib.c` unpatched,
its REPL global object and `main` renamed out of the way, and defines a global object without `print`, `gc`, `load`,
the timers, `Date`, `performance` or `eval`, with a `console` (`log` only) and the block API's classes (`RpBlock`,
`RpMessage`, `RpTransport`, `RpControlStream`, `RpControlChange`, whose constructors refuse); `rp_mqjs_table.c`
compiles the generated tables with two dispatchers that hand every method and getter to the host through the context's
opaque, so one table serves both builds of the host in one binary. `MqjsHost` makes a JS instance at a node's first
call on the thread that runs blocks (`create` never enters the context; `destroy` queues the slot for the block
thread), at most 64 instances a pack and 64 ports and params a node; message, change and stream objects are user-class
objects with getters, so a block sets no JS property; `messages(port)` hands one of a set of arrays per port, and a
node's input pools are made to its queue's capacity at its first block, outside its deadline, so a warmed block
allocates nothing at 64 bits; an object kept past its block throws rather than reading another node's port. Any throw
faults the node with no retry, and so do an overrun, a promise or thenable and a missing `process`; a heap that runs
out kills the pack's context and every node of it faults with the same words, and on the desktop the pack is set up
again once its last node is gone. The desktop gives each pack twice its `heapBytes` (a re-plan holds two instances);
the trial load and the device build give it exactly. `cmake/mquickjs.cmake` gains `retroplug_mquickjs_stdlib` (a
stdlib's tables at 64 and 32 bits, into `build/mquickjs/<name>/`) and `retroplug_mquickjs_engine`;
`mquickjs-table.cmake` runs the tools with `detect_leaks=0`, since upstream's tools free nothing. graph-runtime
defines `retroplug-mqjs-engine`, `-host`, `-host-device` (the device compile, in the ordinary build) and
`retroplug-mqjs-run` (`mqjs-run/main.cpp`: `script` runs a transcript, `pack` sets a pack up as a host does, creates
one node of each type and runs blocks at its inputs' capacity, then bisects for the least context the run needs);
`warnings.cmake` puts the three host targets on the Windows `/W4 /WX` list.

Create `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/script/rp_mqjs.h`:

````cpp
/* rp_mqjs.h - RetroPlug's standard library for MicroQuickJS, as the host sees it
 * (docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 4).
 *
 * A context runs against one standard library: the tables MicroQuickJS's build tool compiles from a list of the
 * globals, classes and C functions it offers (mquickjs_build.c). RetroPlug's is rp_mqjs_stdlib.c: upstream's standard
 * classes (Object, Array, String, Number, Math, JSON, RegExp, the errors, ArrayBuffer and the typed arrays) and none of
 * its REPL's globals (print, gc, load, the timers, Date, performance, eval), plus a console whose log the host routes,
 * and the classes of the block API a script node's process sees: RpBlock (messages, send, control, emit, audio,
 * frames, transport), RpMessage (frame, data, flags), RpTransport (sampleRate, tempo, ppq, playing), RpControlStream
 * (start, changes) and RpControlChange (frame, value). cmake/mquickjs.cmake (retroplug_mquickjs_stdlib) builds the
 * tables at the host's width and at the box's 32 bits, and rp_mqjs_table.c compiles them with the C functions they
 * name.
 *
 * Every one of those C functions is one of two dispatchers, which hand the call to the host through the context's
 * opaque: a context's opaque points to a struct whose first member is a `const rp_mqjs_api*`. So one table, linked
 * once, serves every build of the host a binary holds (the desktop's and the device's, side by side in the device-mode
 * test), each reaching its own functions through the contexts it made. */
#ifndef RP_MQJS_H
#define RP_MQJS_H

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* MicroQuickJS's header declares its C API with no linkage of its own, so C++ takes it inside this block. */
#include "mquickjs.h"

/* The block API's classes, after MicroQuickJS's own. */
#define RP_MQJS_CLASS_BLOCK          (JS_CLASS_USER + 0)
#define RP_MQJS_CLASS_MESSAGE        (JS_CLASS_USER + 1)
#define RP_MQJS_CLASS_TRANSPORT      (JS_CLASS_USER + 2)
#define RP_MQJS_CLASS_CONTROL_STREAM (JS_CLASS_USER + 3)
#define RP_MQJS_CLASS_CONTROL_CHANGE (JS_CLASS_USER + 4)
#define RP_MQJS_CLASS_COUNT          (JS_CLASS_USER + 5)

/* What a method call asks for (rp_mqjs_api.call's `magic`). */
#define RP_MQJS_MESSAGES 0
#define RP_MQJS_SEND     1
#define RP_MQJS_CONTROL  2
#define RP_MQJS_EMIT     3
#define RP_MQJS_AUDIO    4
#define RP_MQJS_LOG      5 /* console.log */

/* What a getter reads (rp_mqjs_api.get's `magic`). */
#define RP_MQJS_FRAMES         0  /* RpBlock */
#define RP_MQJS_TRANSPORT      1
#define RP_MQJS_MESSAGE_FRAME  2  /* RpMessage */
#define RP_MQJS_MESSAGE_DATA   3
#define RP_MQJS_MESSAGE_FLAGS  4
#define RP_MQJS_SAMPLE_RATE    5  /* RpTransport */
#define RP_MQJS_TEMPO          6
#define RP_MQJS_PPQ            7
#define RP_MQJS_PLAYING        8
#define RP_MQJS_STREAM_START   9  /* RpControlStream */
#define RP_MQJS_STREAM_CHANGES 10
#define RP_MQJS_CHANGE_FRAME   11 /* RpControlChange */
#define RP_MQJS_CHANGE_VALUE   12

/* The host's side of the standard library's C functions. */
typedef struct rp_mqjs_api {
    JSValue (*call)(JSContext* ctx, JSValue* this_val, int argc, JSValue* argv, int magic);
    JSValue (*get)(JSContext* ctx, JSValue* this_val, int argc, JSValue* argv, int magic);
} rp_mqjs_api;

/* The standard library's tables, at the width this is compiled for (rp_mqjs_table.c). */
extern const JSSTDLibraryDef rp_mqjs_stdlib;

/* What the public API reaches only by a property's name, which costs an allocation each time (JS_GetPropertyStr and
 * JS_SetPropertyStr make the name a string first), through the engine's own accessors instead, allocating nothing:
 * what a warmed block must not do. rp_mqjs_table.c, which compiles against the engine's private header. */
/* An array's or a typed array's length; UINT32_MAX for any other value. */
uint32_t rp_mqjs_length(JSContext* ctx, JSValue v);
/* An array's length set to n: 0, or -1 with the exception pending. Within the array's capacity and at least half of
 * it, the engine neither grows nor shrinks the array's storage; past it the engine grows it, which may collect, and
 * writes the array back through `array` after: so `array` must point at a rooted slot (a JSGCRef's), never at a copy
 * of the value on the C stack, which the collector cannot see. */
int rp_mqjs_set_length(JSContext* ctx, JSValue* array, uint32_t n);
/* An error's message (stack 0) or its stack (stack 1), as the error holds it; undefined for a value that is not an
 * error. */
JSValue rp_mqjs_error_field(JSContext* ctx, JSValue error, int stack);

/* A context's buffer as the engine has it at the call, read from its own JSContext (rp_mqjs_engine.c, which compiles
 * the engine): `fixed` what the engine takes of the buffer before its heap (its JSContext and the class prototypes),
 * `heap` how far the heap has grown (the live objects and, until the next collection, the garbage), `stack` the
 * stack's depth and `free_bytes` what lies between the two. */
typedef struct rp_mqjs_memory {
    size_t fixed;
    size_t heap;
    size_t stack;
    size_t free_bytes;
} rp_mqjs_memory;
void rp_mqjs_memory_of(JSContext* ctx, rp_mqjs_memory* out);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* RP_MQJS_H */
````

````cpp
/* rp_mqjs_pack.h - a device script pack as a binary carries it (docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md sections 3
 * and 4).
 *
 * The device-pack toolchain (packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs) writes one C source per width for each
 * pack it compiles, <pack>.pack64.c and <pack>.pack32.c, which define the pack's bytecode and the node type ids its
 * definitions register, and nothing else; cmake/packages.cmake builds the one of the binary's width into a library of
 * its own, and a product that lists the pack registers it from that (script/MqjsHost.hpp, rp::mqjs::package). Plain C
 * with no other header, so any compiler a product uses builds it.
 *
 * The bytecode is const, as mqjs -o wrote it, and is never run where it lies: each context the host makes runs a copy
 * of its own, in the pack's memory beside the context. MicroQuickJS relocates bytecode in place (it swaps the
 * bytecode's strings for the atoms of the standard library it runs against, which only a context over that library can
 * do), and a context that runs it writes into it as well: a string constant the code first uses as a property name is
 * marked unique where it lies, in that context's atom table alone, so a second context loading the same bytes would
 * look the name up in vain. */
#ifndef RP_MQJS_PACK_H
#define RP_MQJS_PACK_H

#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef struct rp_mqjs_pack_source {
    const char*        name;          /* the package's name, as its manifest's directory is ("devtest") */
````

````cpp
/* The engine itself, compiled from this file in place of deps/mquickjs/mquickjs.c (cmake/mquickjs.cmake's
 * retroplug_mquickjs_engine, ENGINE), so that it is compiled once and RetroPlug's reads of the context's own
 * bookkeeping sit in the translation unit that defines struct JSContext, which no header declares: the vendored source
 * is included whole and unpatched, and what follows it is RetroPlug's (rp_mqjs.h declares it). */
#include "mquickjs.c"

#include "rp_mqjs.h"

void rp_mqjs_memory_of(JSContext* ctx, rp_mqjs_memory* out) {
    out->fixed = (size_t)(ctx->heap_base - (uint8_t*)ctx);
    out->heap = (size_t)(ctx->heap_free - ctx->heap_base);
    out->stack = (size_t)(ctx->stack_top - (uint8_t*)ctx->sp);
    out->free_bytes = (size_t)((uint8_t*)ctx->sp - ctx->heap_free);
}
````

Create `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/script/rp_mqjs_table.c`:

````cpp
/* RetroPlug's standard library for MicroQuickJS at run time (rp_mqjs.h): the tables the build tool generated from
 * rp_mqjs_stdlib.c for this width, compiled with the C functions they name. Upstream's are the engine's own (declared
 * in mquickjs_priv.h, which the generated header includes); RetroPlug's are the three below, which hand every call to
 * the host that made the context, and the accessors rp_mqjs.h declares. Compiled into the engine's library
 * (cmake/mquickjs.cmake), once per binary. */
#include <stddef.h>

#include "rp_mqjs.h"

/* The host's functions, through the context's opaque: a struct whose first member is the host's rp_mqjs_api. */
static const rp_mqjs_api* rp_mqjs_api_of(JSContext* ctx) {
    return *(const rp_mqjs_api* const*)JS_GetContextOpaque(ctx);
}

static JSValue js_rp_call(JSContext* ctx, JSValue* this_val, int argc, JSValue* argv, int magic) {
    return rp_mqjs_api_of(ctx)->call(ctx, this_val, argc, argv, magic);
}

static JSValue js_rp_get(JSContext* ctx, JSValue* this_val, int argc, JSValue* argv, int magic) {
    return rp_mqjs_api_of(ctx)->get(ctx, this_val, argc, argv, magic);
}

/* The block API's objects are the host's to make: their classes' constructors only refuse. */
static JSValue js_rp_construct(JSContext* ctx, JSValue* this_val, int argc, JSValue* argv, int magic) {
    (void)this_val;
    (void)argc;
    (void)argv;
    (void)magic;
    return JS_ThrowTypeError(ctx, "the host makes the block's objects");
}

#define JS_CLASS_COUNT RP_MQJS_CLASS_COUNT
#include "rp_mqjs_stdlib.h"

uint32_t rp_mqjs_length(JSContext* ctx, JSValue v) {
    const int id = JS_GetClassID(ctx, v);
    JSValue n;
    if (id == JS_CLASS_ARRAY)
        n = js_array_get_length(ctx, &v, 0, NULL);
    else if (id >= JS_CLASS_UINT8C_ARRAY && id <= JS_CLASS_FLOAT64_ARRAY)
        n = js_typed_array_get_length(ctx, &v, 0, NULL, 0);
    else
        return UINT32_MAX;
    return JS_IsInt(n) ? (uint32_t)JS_VALUE_GET_INT(n) : UINT32_MAX;
}

int rp_mqjs_set_length(JSContext* ctx, JSValue* array, uint32_t n) {
    JSValue length = JS_NewInt32(ctx, (int32_t)n);
    return JS_IsException(js_array_set_length(ctx, array, 1, &length)) ? -1 : 0;
}

JSValue rp_mqjs_error_field(JSContext* ctx, JSValue error, int stack) {
    if (!JS_IsError(ctx, error)) return JS_UNDEFINED;
    return js_error_get_message(ctx, &error, 0, NULL, stack);
}
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The MicroQuickJS script host (docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 4): a device script pack's nodes behind
// the node ABI (graph/rp_node.h), on the engine the box runs, built two ways from this one source, as graph/node.hpp
// is. The device's build (RP_DEVICE: no heap, no exceptions, no RTTI) is what a device runs a plan's script nodes with:
// each type has query_memory, create and destroy, and nothing that describes or re-plans. The desktop's adds what
// planning needs (the descriptor, layout_for, prepare_settings and its swap, rp.sdk.settings-json/1 for exportPlan), so
// a device pack runs on this engine on the desktop as well, and the desktop runs the source and the bytecode the box
// runs (decision 2). A desktop-only pack stays on the QuickJS script host (host/script/ScriptHost.hpp).
//
// A pack. Its bytecode (rp_mqjs_pack.h; the device-pack toolchain compiles it, once per width) defines its nodes with
// defineNode and hands them to registerScriptNodes (packages/retroplug/src/script/register.ts), which appends them to
// the global __rp_scriptNodes. package() makes one rp_package for it, one rp_node_type per definition, in the order the
// toolchain recorded them (the pack source's type ids), each type's ctx naming its definition. Registration runs no
// JavaScript on the device: the ids are the build's. The desktop's runs the bytecode once in a context of its own (the
// control context, below) to read each definition's descriptor, and refuses a pack whose definitions are not the ids
// the build recorded.
//
// Its context. A pack's nodes share one MicroQuickJS context, which lives in the pack's package memory
// (rp_package_memory: graph/PlanLoader.hpp places it in a device's arena, graph/PackageMemory.hpp on the desktop), one
// per host: the block is the pack's state, then the context's own copy of the bytecode, then the context's buffer, the
// manifest's heapBytes, which is the whole context (MicroQuickJS's JSContext, its class prototypes, its heap and its
// stack), as the toolchain holds the pack to it. So a pack's memory is heapBytes plus a fixed overhead, the state and
// the bytecode (packageBytes()). The device's build, the exporter's trial load and the toolchain's runner
// (exactPackage()) give the context heapBytes exactly; the desktop's hosts give it kDesktopHeapFactor times that, since
// a re-plan there holds two instances of a node for a while (below). A desktop pack whose heap ran out is set up again,
// a fresh context, once its last node is destroyed, so a re-plan without its nodes and then with them brings it back.
// The copy is the context's alone because running bytecode writes into it (rp_mqjs_pack.h says how), so two contexts
// never share one. Setting the package up makes the context, copies the bytecode, relocates the copy against the
// standard library, loads it and runs it, and checks its definitions against the build's ids; tearing it down frees the
// context, with every value in it.
//
// Its nodes. A node's create (control thread) makes only the native shim, holding its settings (the device's: the
// msgpack the blob carries, in the shim's own memory; the desktop's: its settings as the definition parsed them) and
// the pack's memory, which it asks its host for (rp.host.packages/1). The device's build runs no definition's
// parseSettings: the exporter wrote each node's settings as the desktop parsed them, every default filled in, and the
// device hands create those, decoded. Its JS instance is made at its first call on the
// thread that runs blocks (the ports_changed a plan's adoption sends, or its first process): the settings decoded into
// a JS object, the definition's create({settings, sampleRate, maxFrames}) and layout(settings) called, and the result
// kept in the pack's instance table, at most kMaxInstances a pack. So a pack's context is entered only by the thread
// that runs blocks, while the control thread plans: a destroy (control thread) only queues the instance's slot, which
// the block thread frees at its next entry into the pack. activate's and a settings swap's hooks wait for the node's
// next call there in the same way.
//
// The block API is defineNode.ts's Block, as RetroPlug's standard library's classes (script/rp_mqjs.h): messages(),
// send(), control(), emit(), frames and transport. Every object a block hands out is made at the node's first block and
// refilled after: each input port's pool is made to its queue's capacity before the node's JS first runs on it (a
// message object per place the queue holds, each with a Uint8Array of its own for each payload length up to
// kPlacedLengths over three bytes of a buffer of the port's, and every array messages() hands out), each control
// stream's to its capacity, so what a node's ports take of the heap is fixed by the plan it is in, and its first block,
// which the exporter's trial load runs, measures it. What a block's contents take is not: a payload longer than
// kPlacedLengths gets a Uint8Array made for its block, and a node may make things a message; the toolchain's heap
// check, which fills every input to its queue's capacity, SysEx included, on the node's default settings, is what holds
// a pack to a full block. (The box loads one plan and keeps it. A desktop host that re-plans makes a replacing
// instance's pools at its first block, while the instance it replaces waits for its plan to be reclaimed, so for that
// while the pack's heap holds both: hence kDesktopHeapFactor.) messages(port) is one of a set of arrays the port keeps,
// by the power of two that holds the count (its length set within half its capacity, so the engine neither grows nor
// shrinks it, on a rooted slot, so it is right if JS spliced the array meanwhile), over the pool, whose frame and flags
// are getters on the block's queue and whose data is the place's view of the payload's length, refilled. control(id) is
// the port's stream object, whose changes are kept as the messages are. A message's frame and flags, a stream's start
// and changes and a change's frame and value are read through the port its object names, checked against the running
// node's layout and block (integers the host keeps natively), so an object a pack kept past its block, of a node whose
// slot another now holds, never reads out of bounds: it throws a TypeError when the new node has no port of that
// ordinal, side and kind, and reads that port's when it has one. A message's data is its own value in the JS heap, what
// it last held, and is not checked. send copies the data into the output queue at the call, so a node may refill and
// send one array again; a frame earlier than the port's last is raised to it, and a negative one wraps through
// ToUint32, as the desktop's host does.
//
// What a warmed block allocates: nothing native, ever; in the JS heap, nothing at 64 bits for the whole API but a
// payload longer than kPlacedLengths (a SysEx), whose Uint8Array is made for its block. At 32 bits, the box's width,
// MicroQuickJS boxes every number that is not a 31-bit integer (it has short floats at 64 bits alone), so there each
// read of a non-integer number allocates its box: a control stream's start and a change's value, the transport's
// tempo, ppq and sampleRate when they are not whole, and any such number the node computes. A node that keeps to
// bytes, frames, flags and integers (a MIDI policy) allocates nothing at either width.
//
// Faults (design section 4). A throw from process (or from create, layout or a hook), a process that returns a promise
// or a thenable, a create that returns no process, and an entry that runs past its deadline each fault the node: its
// process answers RP_FAULT from then on, so the executor silences it and counts it once, and the node keeps the first
// fault's words (graph/rp_script.h's rp.script.fault/1). A node does not run again after a throw, unlike the desktop's
// QuickJS host: the box has no one to retry for. A heap that runs out (an out-of-memory error that reaches the host)
// kills the pack's context: every node of the pack faults at its next call, with the same words, and the context runs
// nothing more. MicroQuickJS throws out of memory as an ordinary InternalError, which a node may catch: one that does
// runs on in a heap with no room, and the host does not see it run out. Each entry into a context (a block, a hook, a
// settings check) is held to a deadline through the engine's interrupt handler, polled every 10000 instructions, over
// everything the entry runs: by the host's clock (rp.host.clock/1, the box's, at kHostClockDeadlineMicros unless it
// says otherwise), or, on the desktop when its host offers none, by the calling thread's CPU time at
// kDesktopDeadlineMicros, so a stall that is not the node's costs it nothing. On the device, a host that offers no
// clock runs its script nodes with no deadline.

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "graph/rp_node.h"
#include "graph/rp_script.h"
#include "script/rp_mqjs_pack.h"

#ifndef RP_DEVICE
#include <string>
#endif


namespace rp::mqjs {

// How many instances one pack's context holds at once, all of its types together.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxInstances = 64;
// How many ports and params one node may have: a message's object names its port in 6 bits.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxPorts = 64;
// The payload lengths a message place keeps a Uint8Array for, from 1: every MIDI message but a SysEx.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kPlacedLengths = 3;
// An entry's deadline by a host's clock that names none (the box's): 10 ms. A MIDI-rate node's process takes
// microseconds, the box's block is about a millisecond and its watchdog 3 s, so a node this far over is stuck, and the
// box's other nodes lose at most this long before it is silenced.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kHostClockDeadlineMicros = 10000;
// An entry's deadline by the desktop's own clock, the thread's CPU time: 500 ms. Windows counts that time in scheduler
// ticks of about 15.6 ms, so a deadline must be many ticks long to be measured at all; a Debug or sanitizer build's
// first entry (the settings decoded, create and layout) takes tens of milliseconds; and a desktop host's audio thread
// can lose half a second to a node that hangs where the box could not.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kDesktopDeadlineMicros = RP_SCRIPT_DESKTOP_DEADLINE_MICROS;
// How many times its manifest's heapBytes a desktop host gives a pack's context: a re-plan holds the instance it
// replaces beside the new one until its plan is reclaimed, both with their pools. The device's build, the exporter's
// trial load and the toolchain's runner give heapBytes exactly, which is the box's figure and its check.
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kDesktopHeapFactor = 2;
// The least context the host makes, at this build's width: below it MicroQuickJS's JS_NewContext sets the standard
// library up past its buffer and through the allocation that failed, rather than throwing (its assertion, 1 KiB, is no
// working floor). Measured over RetroPlug's standard library: at 64 bits a context of 4096 bytes sets itself up and one
// of 4088 crashes (ScriptPack.test.cpp holds the figure); at 32 bits, on i386 (the box's word width), 2552 and 2544.
// On ARM's EABI a uint64_t aligns to 8 in a struct, where i386 aligns it to 4, and MicroQuickJS's JSContext holds one,
// so the M33's floor may be a few bytes higher than the 32-bit figure here: the device check settles it on the box.
#if INTPTR_MAX >= INT64_MAX
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kLeastContextBytes = 4096;
#else
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kLeastContextBytes = 2560;
#endif

// The build's rp_package for a pack, made the first time it is asked for and the same after: its context heapBytes on
// the device's build, kDesktopHeapFactor times that on the desktop's. Null when the pack's name
// is not one a manifest's id holds, the build holds no more packs or types (RP_MQJS_MAX_PACKS, RP_MQJS_MAX_TYPES), or
// (on the desktop) the bytecode does not define the types it was built with; packageRefusal() then says why, and the
// desktop's build says it on stderr too. The source must outlive every use of the package.
const rp_package* package(const rp_mqjs_pack_source& source);
#ifndef RP_DEVICE
// The desktop build's rp_package for a pack at heapBytes exactly, as the box runs it: the toolchain's runner, which
// holds a pack to its manifest. A registration of its own, beside package()'s.
const rp_package* exactPackage(const rp_mqjs_pack_source& source);
#endif
// Why the last package() or exactPackage() answered null (the registration's own thread), or empty.
const char* packageRefusal();

// A pack's package memory as the box gives it: its context (the manifest's heapBytes), the host's state and the
// context's copy of the bytecode, at this width.
std::size_t packageBytes(const rp_mqjs_pack_source& source);


#ifndef RP_DEVICE
// The desktop's tools (the device-pack toolchain's runner, retroplug-mqjs-run): `bytecode` (mqjs -o's output, which
// this relocates where it lies, and which the run writes into) run in a context of `contextBytes` over RetroPlug's
// standard library, its console.log written to `log`. Empty when it ran to its end; else what stopped it (its
// exception, or why it could not start).
std::string runScript(std::uint8_t* bytecode, std::size_t size, std::size_t contextBytes,
                      void (*log)(void* ctx, const char* text, std::size_t size), void* logCtx);
#endif

}  // namespace rp::mqjs
````

````cpp
namespace rp::mqjs {

namespace {

// How many packs and types one build registers: the device's is fixed storage, so it keeps what a box carries.
#ifdef RP_DEVICE
#ifndef RP_MQJS_MAX_PACKS
#define RP_MQJS_MAX_PACKS 4
#endif
#ifndef RP_MQJS_MAX_TYPES
#define RP_MQJS_MAX_TYPES 16
#endif
#else
#define RP_MQJS_MAX_PACKS 32
#define RP_MQJS_MAX_TYPES 64
#endif
constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxPacks = RP_MQJS_MAX_PACKS;
constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxTypes = RP_MQJS_MAX_TYPES;

// A message's and a change's object name their node's slot, their port and their place in the port's list, in 6, 6 and
// 20 bits: a queue holds at most 2^20 messages (Descriptor.hpp's kMaxQueueMessages).
constexpr std::uint32_t kItemBits = 20;
constexpr std::uint32_t kBuckets = kItemBits + 2;  // the empty array, then one per power of two up to 2^20

// ---- what a context points to -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

enum class Kind : std::uint8_t { Pack, Control, Script };

// The state every context the host makes has as its opaque: what the standard library's dispatchers (rp_mqjs.h),
// the interrupt handler and the log function find through it. `api` first, as rp_mqjs_table.c reads it.
struct ContextState {
    const rp_mqjs_api* api = nullptr;
    Kind               kind = Kind::Pack;
    JSContext*         ctx = nullptr;
    // The deadline: armed by the outermost entry into the context (Armed), polled by the interrupt handler.
    std::uint64_t (*clock)(void* ctx) = nullptr;
    void*         clockCtx = nullptr;
    std::uint64_t start = 0;
    std::uint64_t limit = kHostClockDeadlineMicros;
    std::uint32_t depth = 0;
    bool          timed = false;    // the entry's start was read: an entry the clock could not time runs untimed
    bool          expired = false;  // this entry ran past its deadline
    // console.log's bytes, and what MicroQuickJS's own printing writes (JS_PrintValueF).
    void (*log)(void* ctx, const char* text, std::size_t size) = nullptr;
    void* logCtx = nullptr;
};

struct Pack;
struct TypeInfo {
    Pack*         pack = nullptr;
    std::uint32_t index = 0;
};

#ifndef RP_DEVICE
// The desktop's control context for a pack (the header comment): one per process, entered under its mutex.
struct Control {
    std::mutex                    mutex;
    std::unique_ptr<std::uint64_t[]> memory;
    std::unique_ptr<std::uint64_t[]> bytecode;  // the context's own copy (rp_mqjs_pack.h)
    ContextState                  state;
    JSGCRef                       defs{};
    std::vector<std::string>      descriptors;
};
// The control context's size and its calls' deadline (the thread's CPU time): it reads definitions and checks settings,
// on the control thread, where nothing waits on a block.
constexpr std::size_t   kControlBytes = std::size_t{1} << 20;
constexpr std::uint64_t kControlDeadlineMicros = 2000000;
#endif

// One pack this build registered: its rp_package and its types.
struct Pack {
    const rp_mqjs_pack_source* source = nullptr;
    rp_package                 package{};
    rp_package_memory          memory{};
    rp_node_type               types[kMaxTypes]{};
    const rp_node_type*        typeList[kMaxTypes]{};
    TypeInfo                   infos[kMaxTypes]{};
    char                       manifest[96]{};
    std::uint32_t              heapFactor = 1;  // the context is this many times the manifest's heapBytes
#ifndef RP_DEVICE
    Control*                   control = nullptr;
#endif
};

// The pack's context, in bytes.
std::uint32_t heapOf(const Pack& pack) { return pack.source->heap_bytes * pack.heapFactor; }

Pack          gPacks[kMaxPacks];
std::uint32_t gPackCount = 0;
char          gRefusal[200] = {};  // why the last package() answered null (packageRefusal)
// The longest pack name a manifest's id holds ({"id":"rp.<name>.script",...} in Pack::manifest).
constexpr std::size_t kMaxNameLength = 48;

// ---- a pack's state in its package memory --------------------------------------------------------------------------

// The pack's root object's slots, its instance records' slots, and a port's state's slots.
enum : std::uint32_t { kRootDefs, kRootInstances, kRootTransport, kRootLength };
enum : std::uint32_t {
    kRecInstance, kRecProcess, kRecPortsChanged, kRecOnSettings, kRecActivate, kRecBlock, kRecPortIds, kRecPortState,
    kRecLength
};
// A port's state: its head (a queue's empty Uint8Array, a control stream's object), its pool of message or change
// objects, how many the pool holds, a queue's byte buffer for the payloads, then its arrays by bucket.
enum : std::uint32_t {
    kStateHead, kStatePool, kStatePooled, kStateBuffer, kStateBuckets, kStateLength = kStateBuckets + kBuckets
};

struct Node;

// The state at the start of a pack's package memory (its layout is below).
struct PackState {
    ContextState  base;  // first: the context's opaque is this
    const Pack*   pack = nullptr;
    JSGCRef       root{};  // [defs, instances, transport]
    // The thread that runs blocks: the block a process call is running, its node and its node's slot.
    const rp_process*  block = nullptr;
    const Node*        running = nullptr;
    std::int32_t       runningSlot = -1;
    bool               dead = false;
    char               deadReason[160] = {};
    std::uint8_t       freeSlots[kMaxInstances] = {};
    std::uint32_t      freeCount = 0;
    // Slots the control thread released (destroy), which the block thread frees at its next entry.
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> releaseHead{0};
````
