````cpp
// retroplug-mqjs-run: the device-pack toolchain's runner (packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs,
// docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 6). It runs MicroQuickJS bytecode on RetroPlug's own standard library
// and the MicroQuickJS script host (script/MqjsHost.hpp), the desktop's build of what the box runs, so what the
// toolchain checks a pack against is the engine as the hosts configure it, not upstream's REPL (mqjs), whose globals a
// pack could otherwise lean on unseen.
//
//   retroplug-mqjs-run script <bytecode> [--context-bytes <n>]
//       Runs the bytecode in a context of n bytes (default 1 MiB), its console.log on stdout. Exits 1, saying what
//       stopped it on stderr, when it throws.
//
//   retroplug-mqjs-run pack <bytecode> --name <pack> --heap-bytes <n> --types <id,...> [--blocks <n>]
//       Holds a pack's 64-bit bytecode to its declared heap: in a context of n bytes, set up as a host sets a pack up
//       (its definitions run and checked against the ids), it creates one node of each type from its default settings,
//       runs it up as a plan does (activate, then its connected outputs) and runs every node for --blocks blocks of 256
//       frames (default 16) under the host's deadline. Each events or bytes input is a queue of a plan's default
//       capacity (graph/PortTypes.hpp: 256 messages, 4096 bytes), full every block: note messages on even blocks, 64
//       SysEx of 64 bytes on odd ones; each control stream holds a plan's 64 changes and gets two a block. A node's
//       ports are sized to those queues at its first block (script/MqjsHost.hpp), so this is the heap the node needs in
//       a plan whose sources declare no smaller capacity, and the most a burst can ask of it. Then it finds the least
//       context that does the same, to 64 bytes. Prints "ok least=<bytes> declared=<n> live=<bytes> fixed=<bytes>"
//       (live: the live heap after the last block, collected; fixed: what MicroQuickJS takes of the context before its
//       heap) and exits 0; or says
//       what failed at the declared heap on stderr ("define", "create" or "run", the node and its words) and exits 1.
//       A node that faults for any reason but the heap running out (one that throws by design, or wants settings other
//       than its defaults) is reported on stdout as a note, and the run goes on without it.
//       The check is at 64 bits, the desktop's width: a 64-bit context needs more of its heap than the box's 32-bit
//       one does for the same objects, so a pack that runs in its heap here runs in it on the box.

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <fstream>
#include <iterator>
#include <memory>
#include <new>
#include <sstream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "graph/Descriptor.hpp"
#include "graph/PortTypes.hpp"
#include "graph/Queue.hpp"
#include "graph/rp_node.h"
#include "script/MqjsHost.hpp"

namespace {

[[noreturn]] void usage(const char* why) {
    std::fprintf(stderr,
                 "retroplug-mqjs-run: %s\n"
                 "usage: retroplug-mqjs-run script <bytecode> [--context-bytes <n>]\n"
                 "       retroplug-mqjs-run pack <bytecode> --name <pack> --heap-bytes <n> --types <id,...> "
                 "[--blocks <n>]\n",
                 why);
    std::exit(2);
}

// A file's bytes, in storage aligned for MicroQuickJS's words (a script's bytecode is relocated where it lies).
std::vector<std::uint64_t> readFile(const std::string& path, std::size_t* size) {
    std::ifstream in(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!in) usage(("cannot read " + path).c_str());
    const std::string bytes((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
    std::vector<std::uint64_t> words(bytes.size() / 8 + 1);
    std::memcpy(words.data(), bytes.data(), bytes.size());
    *size = bytes.size();
    return words;
}

void writeStdout(void*, const char* text, std::size_t size) { std::fwrite(text, 1, size, stdout); }

// ---- pack -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// The host the nodes are created under: the pack's memory (rp.host.packages/1), nothing else.
struct Host {
    const rp_package* package = nullptr;
    void*             memory = nullptr;
    rp_host_packages  service{this, &Host::give};
    rp_host           host{RP_ABI_VERSION, this, nullptr, nullptr, &Host::log, &Host::interfaceOf};
    static void* give(void* ctx, const rp_package* p, rp_error* err) {
        auto* h = static_cast<Host*>(ctx);
        if (p == h->package) return h->memory;
        if (err) std::snprintf(err->message, sizeof err->message, "%s", "not the pack under test");
        return nullptr;
    }
    static void        log(void*, int, const char*) {}
    static const void* interfaceOf(const rp_host* h, const char* id) {
        return std::strcmp(id, RP_HOST_PACKAGES_INTERFACE) == 0 ? &static_cast<Host*>(h->ctx)->service : nullptr;
    }
};

// One node under test, with the ports and params its default layout gives it.
struct Rig {
    const rp_node_type*                type = nullptr;
    std::vector<std::uint64_t>         memory;
    rp_node*                           node = nullptr;
    std::vector<rp_port_view>          inputs, outputs;
    std::vector<rp_control_queue*>     params;
    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<rp_queue>>         queues;
    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<rp_control_queue>> streams;
    std::vector<std::vector<rp_message>>           items;
    std::vector<std::vector<std::uint8_t>>         bytes;
    std::vector<std::vector<rp_control_change>>    changes;
    std::vector<rp_queue*>         feeds;    // the inputs the run fills
    std::vector<rp_control_queue*> moves;    // the control inputs and params it moves
    std::vector<rp_queue*>         drains;   // the outputs it empties
    std::vector<rp_control_queue*> rolls;    // the control outputs it rolls
    rp_resource*                   slot = nullptr;
    bool                           faulted = false;

    rp_queue* queue(std::uint32_t messages, std::uint32_t capacity) {
        items.emplace_back(messages);
        bytes.emplace_back(capacity);
        queues.push_back(std::make_unique<rp_queue>(
            rp_queue{items.back().data(), 0, messages, bytes.back().data(), 0, capacity, 0}));
        return queues.back().get();
    }
    rp_control_queue* stream(double start) {
        changes.emplace_back(64);
        streams.push_back(std::make_unique<rp_control_queue>(rp_control_queue{start, changes.back().data(), 0, 64, 0}));
        return streams.back().get();
    }
};

struct Outcome {
    std::string stage;  // empty: it ran
    std::string reason;
    rp_script_heap_use use{};
};

const rp_script_fault* faultOf(rp_node* node) {
    return static_cast<const rp_script_fault*>(node->vt->get_interface(node, RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_INTERFACE));
}

Outcome runPack(const rp_package* package, std::uint32_t blocks, std::vector<std::string>* notes = nullptr) {
    Outcome out;
    const rp_package_memory& hooks = *package->memory;
    rp_memory_req req{};
    rp_error err{};
    if (!hooks.query(package, &req, &err)) return {"define", err.message, {}};
    std::vector<std::uint64_t> memory(req.size / 8 + 1);
    if (!hooks.setup(package, memory.data(), &err)) return {"define", err.message, {}};
    Host host;
    host.package = package;
    host.memory = memory.data();

    constexpr std::uint32_t kFrames = 256;
    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Rig>> rigs;
    auto finish = [&](Outcome o) {
        // The pack's heap after the run, collected, through a node that made its instance.
        for (auto& r : rigs) {
            const void* found = r->node ? r->node->vt->get_interface(r->node, RP_SCRIPT_HEAP_INTERFACE) : nullptr;
            const auto* heap = static_cast<const rp_script_heap*>(found);
            if (heap && heap->use(r->node, true, &o.use)) break;
        }
        for (auto& r : rigs)
            if (r->node) r->type->destroy(r->node);
        hooks.teardown(package, memory.data());
        return o;
    };
    for (std::uint32_t t = 0; t < package->node_type_count; ++t) {
        auto rig = std::make_unique<Rig>();
        rig->type = package->node_types[t];
        const rp_settings none{nullptr, 0, RP_SETTINGS_JSON};
        std::string layoutJson(4096, '\0');
        std::size_t n = rig->type->layout_for(rig->type, &none, layoutJson.data(), layoutJson.size(), &err);
        if (n >= layoutJson.size()) {
            layoutJson.assign(n + 1, '\0');
            n = rig->type->layout_for(rig->type, &none, layoutJson.data(), layoutJson.size(), &err);
        }
        if (n == 0) return finish({"create", std::string(rig->type->id) + ": " + err.message, {}});
        layoutJson.resize(n);
        auto layout = rp::graph::parseLayout(layoutJson);
        if (!layout) return finish({"create", std::string(rig->type->id) + ": its layout does not parse", {}});
        rp_memory_req nodeReq{};
        if (!rig->type->query_memory(rig->type, &none, &nodeReq, &err))
            return finish({"create", std::string(rig->type->id) + ": " + err.message, {}});
        rig->memory.resize(nodeReq.size / 8 + 1);
        rig->node = rig->type->create(rig->type, &host.host, rig->memory.data(), &none, &err);
        if (!rig->node) return finish({"create", std::string(rig->type->id) + ": " + err.message, {}});
        if (!rig->node->vt->activate(rig->node, 48000.0, kFrames, &err))
            return finish({"create", std::string(rig->type->id) + ": " + err.message, {}});
        for (const auto& p : layout->ports) {
            rp_port_view v{};
            v.kind = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(p.kind);
            const bool out = p.dir == rp::graph::PortDir::Out;
            switch (p.kind) {
                case rp::graph::PortKind::Events:
                case rp::graph::PortKind::Bytes:
                    v.u.queue = rig->queue(rp::graph::kDefaultQueueMessages, rp::graph::kDefaultQueueBytes);
                    (out ? rig->drains : rig->feeds).push_back(v.u.queue);
                    break;
                case rp::graph::PortKind::Control:
                    v.u.control = rig->stream(0.0);
                    (out ? rig->rolls : rig->moves).push_back(v.u.control);
                    break;
                case rp::graph::PortKind::Resource: v.u.resource = &rig->slot; break;
                default: break;
            }
            (out ? rig->outputs : rig->inputs).push_back(v);
        }
        for (const auto& p : layout->params) {
            rig->params.push_back(rig->stream(p.def));
            rig->moves.push_back(rig->params.back());
        }
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> connected(rig->outputs.size(), 1);
        rig->node->vt->ports_changed(rig->node, connected.data(), static_cast<std::uint32_t>(connected.size()));
        rigs.push_back(std::move(rig));
    }
    const rp_transport transport{48000.0, 120.0, 0.0, RP_TRANSPORT_PLAYING};
    for (std::uint32_t b = 0; b < blocks; ++b) {
        for (auto& rig : rigs) {
            for (rp_queue* q : rig->feeds) {
                rp::graph::clearQueue(*q);
                if (b % 2 == 0) {
                    for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < q->capacity; ++k) {
                        const std::uint8_t note[3] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k % 2 ? 0x80 : 0x90),
                                                      static_cast<std::uint8_t>(48 + (b + k) % 24), 100};
                        rp::graph::pushMessage(*q, k * kFrames / q->capacity, note);
                    }
                } else {
                    std::uint8_t sysex[64] = {0xF0, 0x7D};
                    sysex[63] = 0xF7;
                    for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < q->bytes_capacity / 64; ++k)
                        rp::graph::pushMessage(*q, k * kFrames * 64 / q->bytes_capacity, sysex);
                }
            }
            for (rp_control_queue* c : rig->moves) {
                c->count = 0;
                rp::graph::pushControl(*c, 0, 0.25 * (b % 4));
                rp::graph::pushControl(*c, kFrames / 2, 0.5);
            }
            for (rp_queue* q : rig->drains) rp::graph::clearQueue(*q);
            for (rp_control_queue* c : rig->rolls) rp::graph::rollControl(*c);
            rp_process block{kFrames,
                             &transport,
                             rig->inputs.data(),
                             static_cast<std::uint32_t>(rig->inputs.size()),
                             rig->outputs.data(),
                             static_cast<std::uint32_t>(rig->outputs.size()),
                             rig->params.data(),
                             static_cast<std::uint32_t>(rig->params.size())};
            if (rig->faulted || rig->node->vt->process(rig->node, &block) == RP_OK) continue;
            // The heap running out fails the check; any other fault is the node's own (one that throws by design, or
            // wants settings other than its defaults), which the run reports and goes on without.
            const rp_script_fault* f = faultOf(rig->node);
            const std::string why = f && f->reason(rig->node) ? f->reason(rig->node) : "it faulted";
            if (!f || f->kind(rig->node) == RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_HEAP)
                return finish({"run", std::string(rig->type->id) + ": " + why, {}});
            rig->faulted = true;
            if (notes) notes->push_back(std::string(rig->type->id) + " faulted on its default settings: " + why);
        }
    }
    return finish({});
}

int pack(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc < 3) usage("pack needs a bytecode file");
    std::string name, types;
    std::uint32_t heap = 0, blocks = 16;
    for (int i = 3; i < argc; ++i) {
        const std::string a = argv[i];
        if (i + 1 >= argc) usage(("no value for " + a).c_str());
        const std::string v = argv[++i];
        if (a == "--name") name = v;
        else if (a == "--heap-bytes") heap = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::stoul(v));
        else if (a == "--types") types = v;
        else if (a == "--blocks") blocks = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::stoul(v));
        else usage(("unknown option " + a).c_str());
    }
    if (name.empty() || !heap || types.empty()) usage("pack needs --name, --heap-bytes and --types");
    std::vector<std::string> ids;
    std::stringstream        list(types);
    for (std::string id; std::getline(list, id, ',');) ids.push_back(id);
    std::vector<const char*> idPointers;
    for (const auto& id : ids) idPointers.push_back(id.c_str());

    std::size_t size = 0;
    const std::vector<std::uint64_t> words = readFile(argv[2], &size);
    rp_mqjs_pack_source source{name.c_str(), reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(words.data()),
                               static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size), heap, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(ids.size()),
                               idPointers.data()};
    const rp_package* package = rp::mqjs::exactPackage(source);
    if (!package) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "define: its bytecode is not a pack this host registers (said above)\n");
        return 1;
    }
    // The declared heap first: what the toolchain refuses or passes. Then the least that does the same, by halving.
    std::vector<std::string> notes;
    const Outcome declared = runPack(package, blocks, &notes);
    if (!declared.stage.empty()) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "%s: %s\n", declared.stage.c_str(), declared.reason.c_str());
        return 1;
    }
    for (const auto& note : notes) std::printf("note: %s\n", note.c_str());
    std::uint32_t lo = rp::mqjs::kLeastContextBytes, hi = heap;
    source.heap_bytes = lo;
    if (runPack(package, blocks).stage.empty()) hi = lo;
    while (hi - lo > 64) {
        const std::uint32_t mid = (lo + (hi - lo) / 2) & ~7u;
        source.heap_bytes = mid;
        (runPack(package, blocks).stage.empty() ? hi : lo) = mid;
    }
    std::printf("ok least=%u declared=%u live=%zu fixed=%zu\n", hi, heap, declared.use.heap, declared.use.fixed);
    return 0;
}

int script(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc < 3) usage("script needs a bytecode file");
    std::size_t contextBytes = std::size_t{1} << 20;
    for (int i = 3; i < argc; ++i) {
        const std::string a = argv[i];
        if (a == "--context-bytes" && i + 1 < argc) contextBytes = std::stoul(argv[++i]);
        else usage(("unknown option " + a).c_str());
    }
    std::size_t size = 0;
    std::vector<std::uint64_t> words = readFile(argv[2], &size);
    const std::string failed =
        rp::mqjs::runScript(reinterpret_cast<std::uint8_t*>(words.data()), size, contextBytes, &writeStdout, nullptr);
    std::fflush(stdout);
    if (failed.empty()) return 0;
    std::fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", failed.c_str());
    return 1;
}

}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc < 2) usage("no command");
    const std::string command = argv[1];
    if (command == "script") return script(argc, argv);
    if (command == "pack") return pack(argc, argv);
    usage(("unknown command " + command).c_str());
}
````

````diff
+# retroplug_mquickjs_stdlib(<name> SOURCE <file.c> [INCLUDES <dir>...]): a standard library of the engine's
+# (docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 4), its tables generated at both widths a script pack runs at. The
+# build tool <name>-tool is SOURCE (a list of the library's globals, classes and C functions by name, whose main calls
+# build_atoms) with upstream's mquickjs_build.c, built for the host; it prints the tables, <name>.h, and the
+# predefined atoms' offsets, mquickjs_atom.h, for the host's width and, with -m32, for a 32-bit target's (the box's).
+# Written into build/mquickjs/<name>/64 and build/mquickjs/<name>/32: a compile that runs against the library at a

+# 32-bit atoms, and a context at a width takes that width's tables.
+function(retroplug_mquickjs_stdlib name)
+    cmake_parse_arguments(P "" "SOURCE" "INCLUDES" ${ARGN})

+        message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_mquickjs_stdlib(${name}): SOURCE is required, and nothing else is unnamed")

+        add_executable(${_tool} EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL ${_objs})

+    else()
+        add_executable(${_tool} EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL "${P_SOURCE}" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/mquickjs_build.c")
+        target_compile_definitions(${_tool} PRIVATE _GNU_SOURCE)
+        target_include_directories(${_tool} PRIVATE "${MQUICKJS_DIR}" ${P_INCLUDES})
+        retroplug_silence_dep_warnings(${_tool})
+    endif()
+    set_target_properties(${_tool} PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin")
+    set(_root "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/mquickjs/${name}")
+    foreach(_width 64 32)
+        set(_dir "${_root}/${_width}")
+        file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${_dir}")
+        if(_width EQUAL 32)
+            set(_m "-m32")
+        else()
+            set(_m "-m64")
+        endif()
+        set(_headers "${_dir}/${name}.h" "${_dir}/mquickjs_atom.h")
+        add_custom_command(
+            OUTPUT ${_headers}
+            COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} "-DTOOL=$<TARGET_FILE:${_tool}>" "-DARGS=${_m}" "-DOUTPUT=${_dir}/${name}.h"
+                    -P "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake"
+            COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} "-DTOOL=$<TARGET_FILE:${_tool}>" "-DARGS=${_m};-a"
+                    "-DOUTPUT=${_dir}/mquickjs_atom.h" -P "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake"
+            DEPENDS ${_tool} "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/mquickjs-table.cmake"
+            COMMENT "mquickjs: ${name}'s tables, ${_width}-bit"
+            VERBATIM)
+        set(${name}_DIR_${_width} "${_dir}" PARENT_SCOPE)
+        set(${name}_HEADERS_${_width} ${_headers} PARENT_SCOPE)
+    endforeach()
+endfunction()
+
+# retroplug_mquickjs_engine(<target> STDLIB <name> SOURCES <c>... [ENGINE <c>]): the engine as a static library for the
+# desktop's own width, with the standard library <name> (retroplug_mquickjs_stdlib) whose run-time half SOURCES are (the
+# C file that compiles the generated tables with the functions they name). ENGINE, if given, is compiled in place of
+# mquickjs.c: a file that includes mquickjs.c whole and defines after it what must read the engine's own structures. The
+# engine's sources are upstream's, unpatched, at upstream Makefile's flags, their warnings silenced as a dep's are;
+# position-independent, as a product module links it. Its users get deps/mquickjs's headers (mquickjs.h). A device
+# builds the engine its own way, at its own width, and must compile the same ENGINE file the host's build names
+# (graph-runtime's script/rp_mqjs_engine.c) in place of mquickjs.c: the host's device build calls what it defines.
+function(retroplug_mquickjs_engine target)
+    cmake_parse_arguments(P "" "STDLIB;ENGINE" "SOURCES;INCLUDES" ${ARGN})
+    if(NOT P_STDLIB OR NOT P_SOURCES OR P_UNPARSED_ARGUMENTS)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_mquickjs_engine(${target}): STDLIB and SOURCES are required")
+    endif()
+    if(NOT P_ENGINE)
+        set(P_ENGINE "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/mquickjs.c")
+    endif()
+    set(_engine "${P_ENGINE}" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/dtoa.c" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/libm.c" "${MQUICKJS_DIR}/cutils.c")
+    set(_dir "${${P_STDLIB}_DIR_64}")
+    set(_headers ${${P_STDLIB}_HEADERS_64})
+    if(NOT _dir)
+        message(FATAL_ERROR "retroplug_mquickjs_engine(${target}): no standard library `${P_STDLIB}` "
+                            "(retroplug_mquickjs_stdlib)")
+    endif()
+    if(MSVC)
+        # clang-cl, as the tools above; the generated tables and the sources' own directories first.
+        set(_saved_flags ${_mqjs_cl_flags})
+        set(_mqjs_cl_flags ${_mqjs_cl_flags} "-I${_dir}")

+        file(MAKE_DIRECTORY "${_mqjs_objdir}")
+        _mqjs_clang_objects(_objs "${_headers}" ${_engine} ${P_SOURCES})
+        set(_mqjs_cl_flags ${_saved_flags})
+        add_library(${target} STATIC ${_objs})
+        set_target_properties(${target} PROPERTIES LINKER_LANGUAGE C)
+    else()
+        add_library(${target} STATIC ${_engine} ${P_SOURCES} ${_headers})
+        target_compile_definitions(${target} PRIVATE _GNU_SOURCE)
+        target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE -fno-math-errno -fno-trapping-math)
+        # The generated tables before the vendored tree: mquickjs.c includes "mquickjs_atom.h" by a quoted name.
+        target_include_directories(${target} PRIVATE "${_dir}" ${P_INCLUDES})
+        set_target_properties(${target} PROPERTIES POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)
+        retroplug_silence_dep_warnings(${target})
+        target_link_libraries(${target} PRIVATE m)
+    endif()
+    target_include_directories(${target} PUBLIC "${MQUICKJS_DIR}")
+endfunction()
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The tests: the host on both builds, and the fixture packs**

`ScriptPack.test.cpp` (`[device-mode][script-pack]`, in `retroplug-device-mode-test`): registration; every C++ package
without memory; the transpose through the block API, both builds identical; the block API's probe (frames, transport,
control and param, events and bytes with flags, emit, three TypeErrors, objects refilled next block); settings from
JSON and msgpack, and the device's limits; the hooks; the desktop's settings swap; each fault; a heap running out
silencing only its pack, and a dead pack set up again; an array JS emptied grown again on a rooted slot through
collections, at a heap halved to the least that runs; kept objects; the deadline's clock rules; a first block sizing
the heap and a warmed block allocating nothing (C and C++ allocations, and the JS heap's top); a plan exported and
loaded over the device-mode builds, digest-identical to GraphHost and allocating nothing from load to unload; the
loader's sizing, placement and refusals; the 64-bit floor; the threaded case (an audio thread running blocks while the
control thread plans 200 documents), which ThreadSanitizer runs; and a hidden `[script-bench]`. The fixture packs
(`script-packs/scripttest`, `hog`) are type-checked by `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.json`; `tests.cmake` builds their
packs and adds the test. `device-pack.test.ts` reads the runner's lines, and `guard-else.ts`'s else-branch gains the
cast that makes `pnpm typecheck` pass again (the scan still finds `Symbol` at its line 15).

````ts
// device-pack toolchain as a test fixture (packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake), never by a product.
//
//   rp.scripttest.probe     every part of the block API: what it reads (frames, transport, a control input and a param,
//                           its events and bytes inputs) it sends on, and it calls what a block refuses
//   rp.scripttest.settings  its settings as create was given them, sent back as text, a byte a character
//   rp.scripttest.hooks     what portsChanged and activate were told, sent each block
//   rp.scripttest.steady    the whole block API with nothing made a block: what a warmed block is held to
//   rp.scripttest.keeper    keeps a message, a stream and a change of its block in the pack's globals
//   rp.scripttest.reader    reads what the keeper kept, as another node, and sends what each read did
//   rp.scripttest.busy      a fixed count of work a block, long enough for the engine to poll its interrupt handler
//   rp.scripttest.throws, .spins, .thenable, .fault, .no-process, .create-throws: one fault each
import { bytes, control, defineNode, events, param } from "../../../../../retroplug/src/graph/defineNode";
import { s } from "../../../../../retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../../../../retroplug/src/script/register";

const byte = (v: number): number => v & 0xff;

export const probeNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.probe",
  ports: {
    ctl: control.in(),
    ev: events.in(),
    raw: bytes.in(),
    out: events.out({ messages: 64, bytes: 1024 }),
    bout: bytes.out({ messages: 64, bytes: 1024 }),
    level: control.out(),
  },
  params: { gain: param.float({ name: "Gain", min: 0, max: 1, default: 0.5 }) },
  create: () => {
    const summary = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
    return {
      process(b) {
        const t = b.transport;
        summary[0] = byte(b.frames);
        summary[1] = byte(b.frames >> 8);
        summary[2] = t.playing ? 1 : 0;
        summary[3] = byte(Math.round(t.tempo));
        summary[4] = byte(Math.floor(t.ppq * 4));
        summary[5] = byte(Math.round(t.sampleRate / 1000));
        summary[6] = byte(Math.round(b.control("gain").start * 100));
        summary[7] = b.control("gain").changes.length;
        b.send("out", 0, summary);
        // The control input, doubled, at the frames it changed.
        const ctl = b.control("ctl");
        b.emit("level", 0, ctl.start * 2);
        for (let i = 0; i < ctl.changes.length; i++) b.emit("level", ctl.changes[i].frame, ctl.changes[i].value * 2);
        // Every message of each input on, at its frame, with its flags.
        const ev = b.messages("ev");
        for (let i = 0; i < ev.length; i++) b.send("out", ev[i].frame, ev[i].data, ev[i].flags);
        const raw = b.messages("raw");
        for (let i = 0; i < raw.length; i++) b.send("bout", raw[i].frame, raw[i].data, raw[i].flags);
        // What a block refuses: a port it does not have, an input named as an output, an audio port. Each a
        // TypeError, which the node sends as a code. (Each catch binds a name of its own: MicroQuickJS refuses two
        // catch clauses of one function that bind the same name.)
        const codes = [0xe0];
        try {
          b.messages("nope");
        } catch (e1) {
          codes.push(e1 instanceof TypeError ? 1 : 0x7f);
        }
        try {
          b.send("ev", 0, [1]);
        } catch (e2) {
          codes.push(e2 instanceof TypeError ? 2 : 0x7f);
        }
        try {
          b.audio("ev");
        } catch (e3) {
          codes.push(e3 instanceof TypeError ? 3 : 0x7f);
        }
        b.send("out", b.frames - 1, codes);
      },
    };
  },
});

export const settingsNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.settings",
  settings: s.object({
    count: s.int({ min: -1000, max: 100000, default: 7 }),
    ratio: s.number(0.25),
    on: s.bool(false),
    name: s.string("abc"),
    mode: s.enum(["slow", "fast"], "slow"),
    taps: s.array(s.int({ min: 0, max: 255, default: 0 }), [1, 2, 3]),
    inner: s.object({ depth: s.int({ min: 0, max: 9, default: 4 }) }),
    // Any JSON at all: what holds a field name or a nesting a device's decode refuses.
    extra: s.json<unknown>({}),
  }),
  ports: { out: events.out({ messages: 4, bytes: 512 }) },
  create: ({ settings }) => {
    const text = JSON.stringify(settings);
    const data = new Uint8Array(text.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < text.length; i++) data[i] = text.charCodeAt(i);
    return {
      process(b) {
        b.send("out", 0, data);
      },
    };
  },
});

export const hooksNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.hooks",
  ports: { out: events.out({ messages: 4, bytes: 64 }), spare: events.out() },
  create: ({ sampleRate, maxFrames }) => {
    const seen = [0, 0, 0, 0, byte(Math.round(sampleRate / 1000)), byte(maxFrames >> 4)];
    return {
      portsChanged(connected) {
        seen[0]++;
        seen[1] = connected.length;
        seen[2] = (connected[0] ? 1 : 0) | (connected[1] ? 2 : 0);
      },
      activate(rate, frames) {
        seen[3]++;
        seen[4] = byte(Math.round(rate / 1000));
        seen[5] = byte(frames >> 4);
      },
      process(b) {
        b.send("out", 0, seen);
      },
    };
  },
});

// Every read of the API a MIDI-rate node makes, each block, and an emit and a send of what it read, with nothing made:
// numbers it reads are whole (frames, flags, bytes, the stream's values as the test sets them), arrays refilled.
export const steadyNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.steady",
  ports: { ctl: control.in(), ev: events.in(), out: events.out({ messages: 64, bytes: 1024 }), level: control.out() },
  params: { gain: param.int({ name: "Gain", min: 0, max: 100, default: 50 }) },
  create: () => {
    const summary = [0, 0, 0, 0];
    return {
      process(b) {
        const t = b.transport;
        summary[0] = b.frames & 0xff;
        summary[1] = t.playing ? 1 : 0;
        summary[2] = t.tempo & 0xff;
        summary[3] = b.control("gain").start & 0xff;
        b.send("out", 0, summary);
        const ctl = b.control("ctl");
        let total = ctl.start;
        const changes = ctl.changes;
        for (let i = 0; i < changes.length; i++) total += changes[i].value + changes[i].frame;
        b.emit("level", 0, total);
        const ev = b.messages("ev");
        for (let i = 0; i < ev.length; i++) b.send("out", ev[i].frame, ev[i].data, ev[i].flags);
      },
    };
  },
});

// What a pack must not do, and the host must survive: objects of a block kept past it, in the pack's globals, read
// later by another node, which may hold the keeper's slot by then.
let keptMessage: { frame: number; data: Uint8Array; flags: number } | null = null;
let keptStream: { start: number; changes: readonly { frame: number; value: number }[] } | null = null;
let keptChange: { frame: number; value: number } | null = null;

export const keeperNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.keeper",
  ports: { a: control.in(), b: control.in(), ev: events.in(), out: events.out() },
  create: () => ({
    process(blk) {
      const ev = blk.messages("ev");
      if (ev.length > 0) keptMessage = ev[ev.length - 1];
      keptStream = blk.control("b");
      if (keptStream.changes.length > 0) keptChange = keptStream.changes[0];
    },
  }),
});

// Sends, a byte a read, what reading each kept object did: 1 it read a value, 2 it threw the host's TypeError for an
// object kept past its block, 4 another TypeError, 3 anything else.
export const readerNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.reader",
  ports: { out: events.out() },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const codes = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
      const reads = [
        () => keptMessage && keptMessage.frame,
        () => keptMessage && keptMessage.data,
        () => keptStream && keptStream.start,
        () => keptStream && keptStream.changes,
        () => keptChange && keptChange.value,
      ];
      for (let i = 0; i < reads.length; i++) {
        try {
          reads[i]();
          codes[i] = 1;
        } catch (e) {
          const kept = e instanceof TypeError && String(e.message).indexOf("kept past its block") >= 0;
          codes[i] = kept ? 2 : e instanceof TypeError ? 4 : 3;
        }
      }
      b.send("out", 0, codes);
    },
  }),
});

const quiet = { out: events.out() };

export const throwsNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.throws",
  ports: quiet,
  create: () => ({
    process() {
      throw new RangeError("the throws node threw");
    },
  }),
});

export const busyNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.busy",
  ports: quiet,
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      let n = 0;
      for (let i = 0; i < 200000; i++) n += i & 1;
      b.send("out", 0, [n & 0x7f]);
    },
  }),
});

export const spinsNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.spins",
  ports: quiet,
  create: () => ({
    process() {
      let n = 0;
      for (;;) n++;
    },
  }),
});

export const thenableNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.thenable",
  ports: quiet,
  create: () => ({
    process() {
      return { then() {} } as unknown as void;
    },
  }),
});

export const faultNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.fault",
  ports: quiet,
  create: () => ({
    process() {
      return "fault" as const;
    },
  }),
});

export const noProcessNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.no-process",
  ports: quiet,
  create: () => ({}) as unknown as { process(): void },
});

export const createThrowsNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.scripttest.create-throws",
  ports: quiet,
  create: () => {
    throw new TypeError("create would not");
  },
});

registerScriptNodes([probeNode, settingsNode, hooksNode, steadyNode, keeperNode, readerNode, busyNode, throwsNode,
                     spinsNode, thenableNode, faultNode, noProcessNode, createThrowsNode]);
````

````ts
// The hog pack: a node that keeps what it makes until its pack's heap runs out, beside one that makes little, for
// ScriptPack.test.cpp's case that a heap running out silences its own pack's nodes and no other's; and a node that
// empties the array messages() hands it every block, which the host must then grow again on a rooted slot, run in a
// heap that collects at every allocation. A test fixture of the device-pack toolchain
// (packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake), never built by a product.
import { defineNode, events } from "../../../../../retroplug/src/graph/defineNode";
import { s } from "../../../../../retroplug/src/graph/settingsSchema";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../../../../retroplug/src/script/register";

// It keeps what it makes only when its settings say `grow`, so the toolchain's heap check, which runs every node on
// its default settings, passes the pack.
export const hogNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.hog.hog",
  settings: s.object({ grow: s.bool(false) }),
  ports: { out: events.out() },
  create: ({ settings }) => {
    const kept: number[][] = [];
    return {
      process() {
        if (!settings.grow) return;
        for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) kept.push([i, i, i, i, i, i, i, i]);
      },
    };
  },
});

export const quietNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.hog.quiet",
  ports: { out: events.out() },
  create: () => {
    let blocks = 0;
    return {
      process(b) {
        blocks++;
        b.send("out", 0, [blocks & 0x7f]);
      },
    };
  },
});

// Each message on, then the array emptied: its storage freed, so the next block's array is grown again by the host.
export const emptierNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.hog.emptier",
  ports: { in: events.in(), out: events.out({ match: "in" }) },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const messages = b.messages("in");
      for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i++) b.send("out", messages[i].frame, messages[i].data, messages[i].flags);
      (messages as unknown as unknown[]).length = 0;  // what the contract allows a node to do with its own array
    },
  }),
});

registerScriptNodes([hogNode, quietNode, emptierNode]);
````

````cpp
// Device script packs on the MicroQuickJS host (graph-runtime's script/MqjsHost.hpp,
// docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md sections 4, 5 and 7), both its builds: the desktop's, which plans, and the
// device's (RP_DEVICE, renamed in the device-mode objects), which a device runs a plan's script nodes with. The packs
// are devtest's (packages/devtest/ts) and the test's own (script-packs/: scripttest and hog), each compiled by the
// device-pack toolchain to bytecode, and each node is made and run through the C ABI as a host makes it, under a host
// of the case's own (its package memory, a clock, a console sink).
//
// - A pack registers on both builds: one rp_package with memory of its own and a type per definition, described on
//   the desktop's build alone, where every C++ package has no package memory.
// - The block API (frames, transport, a control input and a param, events and bytes in and out, emit) and what a block
//   refuses, the same on both builds; settings reach create as the definition parsed them, from JSON or msgpack; the
//   hooks run when the host says.
// - Each fault: a throw, a deadline overrun, a promise, "fault", no process, a create that throws; and a heap that runs
//   out silencing every node of its pack and no other pack's.
// - A warmed block allocates nothing: not the C allocator, not the JS heap.
// - A plan with a script node, exported and loaded over the device-mode builds in an arena, renders what GraphHost
//   renders from the same document, and the loader sizes, places and sets up the pack's memory, refusing a plan that
//   cannot hold it, a pack that cannot be sized and one that will not set up, each in its words.
// - The least context the host makes is one MicroQuickJS sets itself up in without writing past it.
// A hidden case ([.script-bench]) measures a script node's cost a message, and a pack's heap use.

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <memory>
#include <span>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#if defined(_WIN32)
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <windows.h>
#else
#include <ctime>
#endif

#include "DeviceModeEntries.hpp"
#include "graph/CountingAllocator.hpp"
#include "graph/Executor.hpp"
#include "graph/GraphHost.hpp"
#include "graph/JsonToMsgpack.hpp"
#include "graph/NodeRegistry.hpp"
#include "graph/PackageMemory.hpp"
#include "graph/PlanExport.hpp"
#include "graph/PlanLoader.hpp"
#include "graph/Queue.hpp"
#include "graph/ResourceTable.hpp"
#include "graph/node_desc.hpp"
#include "graph/rp_device.h"
#include "script/MqjsHost.hpp"
#include "script/rp_mqjs.h"

extern "C" {
// The packs' registrations: the desktop's build, and the device's (the device-mode objects, renamed).
const rp_package* rp_devtest_script_package(void);
const rp_package* rp_devtest_script_package_device_mode(void);
const rp_package* rp_scripttest_script_package(void);
const rp_package* rp_scripttest_script_package_device_mode(void);
const rp_package* rp_hog_script_package(void);
const rp_package* rp_hog_script_package_device_mode(void);
const rp_package* rp_devtest_plan_package(void);
const rp_package* rp_core_package(void);
const rp_package* rp_dsp_package(void);
const rp_package* rp_n8_package(void);
// The bytecode the toolchain compiled for devtest and hog (their pack64.c).
extern const rp_mqjs_pack_source rp_script_devtest;
extern const rp_mqjs_pack_source rp_script_hog;
}

// Every device entry with both its builds (the generated device-entries.cpp).
std::vector<DeviceEntry> deviceEntries();

namespace {

using namespace rp::graph;

// ---- a host and a node, by hand ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// The calling thread's CPU time in microseconds, as the desktop's own deadline clock reads it: what the cases' hosts
// offer as their clock, so a preempted thread on a loaded machine (a parallel or sanitizer run) costs a node nothing.
std::uint64_t cpuMicros(void*) {
#if defined(_WIN32)
    FILETIME created{}, exited{}, kernel{}, user{};
    if (!::GetThreadTimes(::GetCurrentThread(), &created, &exited, &kernel, &user)) return 0;
    const auto us = [](const FILETIME& f) {
        return ((static_cast<std::uint64_t>(f.dwHighDateTime) << 32) | f.dwLowDateTime) / 10;
    };
    return us(kernel) + us(user);
#else
    timespec t{};
    if (clock_gettime(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID, &t) != 0) return 0;
    return static_cast<std::uint64_t>(t.tv_sec) * 1000000 + static_cast<std::uint64_t>(t.tv_nsec) / 1000;
#endif
}
void ignoreLog(void*, int, const char*) {}

// A host for script nodes made by hand: package memory of its own (rp.host.packages/1, set up at a node's first ask
// and torn down with the host, after its nodes), a CPU-time clock whose deadline the case may set (rp.host.clock/1;
// the desktop's own figure unless it does), and console.log collected (rp.host.script-log/1). Declare it before the
// nodes made under it.
struct Host {
    PackageMemory      packages;
    std::string        log;
    rp_host_clock      clock{this, &cpuMicros, rp::mqjs::kDesktopDeadlineMicros};
    rp_host_script_log sink{this, &Host::write};
    rp_host            host{RP_ABI_VERSION, this, nullptr, nullptr, &ignoreLog, &Host::interfaceOf};

    explicit Host(std::uint32_t deadlineMicros = rp::mqjs::kDesktopDeadlineMicros) {
        clock.deadline_micros = deadlineMicros;
    }
    static void write(void* ctx, const char* text, std::size_t size) {
        static_cast<Host*>(ctx)->log.append(text, size);
    }
    static const void* interfaceOf(const rp_host* h, const char* id) {
        auto* self = static_cast<Host*>(h->ctx);
        if (std::strcmp(id, RP_HOST_PACKAGES_INTERFACE) == 0) return self->packages.service();
        if (std::strcmp(id, RP_HOST_CLOCK_INTERFACE) == 0) return &self->clock;
        if (std::strcmp(id, RP_HOST_SCRIPT_LOG_INTERFACE) == 0) return &self->sink;
        return nullptr;
    }
};

const rp_node_type* typeOf(const rp_package* p, std::string_view id) {
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < p->node_type_count; ++i)
        if (id == p->node_types[i]->id) return p->node_types[i];
    return nullptr;
}

std::vector<std::uint8_t> msgpackOf(const char* json) {
    auto bytes = settingsToMsgpack(json);
    REQUIRE(bytes);
    return *bytes;
}

// A message as a queue held it.
struct Sent {
    std::uint32_t             frame = 0;
    std::uint32_t             flags = 0;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
    bool operator==(const Sent&) const = default;
};

// What a port of a node made by hand is: its kind and whether it is an output.
struct PortSpec {
    rp_port_kind kind;
    bool         out;
};

// One node made by hand, as a host makes it: its memory, its create from `settings` (msgpack), activate, then the
// connected outputs (all of them unless `connected` says otherwise), and a block at a time over queues and streams of
// its own, in the order `ports` lists them (the layout's: inputs, then outputs), with `params` streams at the defaults
// `starts` gives.
struct Made {
    struct Queue {
        std::vector<rp_message>   items;
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
        rp_queue                  q;
        explicit Queue(std::uint32_t capacity)
            : items(capacity), bytes(4096), q{items.data(), 0, capacity, bytes.data(), 0, 4096, 0} {}
    };
    struct Stream {
        std::vector<rp_control_change> changes = std::vector<rp_control_change>(64);
        rp_control_queue               q{0.0, changes.data(), 0, 64, 0};
    };

    const rp_node_type*                  type = nullptr;
    std::vector<std::max_align_t>        memory;
    rp_node*                             node = nullptr;
    std::string                          error;
    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Queue>>  queues;
    std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Stream>> streams;
    std::vector<rp_port_view>            inputs, outputs;
    std::vector<rp_control_queue*>       params;
    rp_transport                         transport{48000.0, 120.0, 0.0, 0};

    Made(const rp_node_type* t, Host& host, const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& settings, std::vector<PortSpec> ports,
         std::vector<double> starts = {}, std::vector<std::uint8_t> connected = {},
         std::uint32_t encoding = RP_SETTINGS_MSGPACK, std::uint32_t capacity = 256)
        : type(t) {
        REQUIRE(type);
        const rp_settings s{reinterpret_cast<const char*>(settings.data()), settings.size(), encoding};
        rp_memory_req req{};
        rp_error err{};
        REQUIRE(type->query_memory(type, &s, &req, &err));
        memory.resize(req.size / sizeof(std::max_align_t) + 1);
        node = type->create(type, &host.host, memory.data(), &s, &err);
        error = err.message;
        if (!node) return;
        REQUIRE(node->vt->activate(node, 48000.0, 256, &err));
        for (const PortSpec& p : ports) {
            rp_port_view v{};
            v.kind = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(p.kind);
            if (p.kind == RP_PORT_CONTROL) {
                streams.push_back(std::make_unique<Stream>());
                v.u.control = &streams.back()->q;
            } else {
                queues.push_back(std::make_unique<Queue>(capacity));
                v.u.queue = &queues.back()->q;
            }
            (p.out ? outputs : inputs).push_back(v);
        }
        for (double start : starts) {
            streams.push_back(std::make_unique<Stream>());
            streams.back()->q.start = start;
            params.push_back(&streams.back()->q);
        }
        if (connected.empty()) connected.assign(outputs.size(), 1);
        node->vt->ports_changed(node, connected.data(), static_cast<std::uint32_t>(connected.size()));
    }
    ~Made() {
        if (node) type->destroy(node);
    }
    Made(const Made&) = delete;
    Made& operator=(const Made&) = delete;

    rp_queue&         in(std::size_t i) { return *inputs[i].u.queue; }
    rp_control_queue& control(std::size_t i) { return *inputs[i].u.control; }
    rp_queue&         out(std::size_t i) { return *outputs[i].u.queue; }

    // One block: every output emptied (and a control output rolled) first, as an executor does.
    rp_status run(std::uint32_t frames = 256) {
        for (rp_port_view& v : outputs) {
            if (v.kind == RP_PORT_CONTROL) {
                rollControl(*v.u.control);
            } else {
                clearQueue(*v.u.queue);
            }
        }
        const rp_process block{frames,          &transport,
                               inputs.data(),   static_cast<std::uint32_t>(inputs.size()),
                               outputs.data(),  static_cast<std::uint32_t>(outputs.size()),
                               params.data(),   static_cast<std::uint32_t>(params.size())};
        return node->vt->process(node, &block);
    }

    std::vector<Sent> sent(std::size_t output) {
        std::vector<Sent> out;
        const rp_queue& q = *outputs[output].u.queue;
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < q.count; ++i) {
            const auto data = messageData(q, q.items[i]);
            out.push_back({q.items[i].frame, q.items[i].flags, {data.begin(), data.end()}});
        }
        return out;
    }

    std::string fault() const {
        const auto* f = static_cast<const rp_script_fault*>(node->vt->get_interface(node, RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_INTERFACE));
        const char* why = f ? f->reason(node) : nullptr;
        return why ? why : "";
    }
    std::uint32_t faultKind() const {
        const auto* f = static_cast<const rp_script_fault*>(node->vt->get_interface(node, RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_INTERFACE));
        return f ? f->kind(node) : 0;
    }
    rp_script_heap_use heap(bool collect) const {
        const auto* h = static_cast<const rp_script_heap*>(node->vt->get_interface(node, RP_SCRIPT_HEAP_INTERFACE));
        rp_script_heap_use use{};
        if (h) h->use(node, collect, &use);
        return use;
    }
};

// The two builds of each pack.
struct Build {
    const char*       name;
    const rp_package* devtest;
    const rp_package* scripttest;
    const rp_package* hog;
};
std::vector<Build> builds() {
    std::vector<Build> out = {
        {"desktop", rp_devtest_script_package(), rp_scripttest_script_package(), rp_hog_script_package()},
        {"device", rp_devtest_script_package_device_mode(), rp_scripttest_script_package_device_mode(),
         rp_hog_script_package_device_mode()}};
    for (const Build& b : out) {
        INFO(b.name);
        REQUIRE(b.devtest);
        REQUIRE(b.scripttest);
        REQUIRE(b.hog);
    }
    return out;
}

void push(rp_queue& q, std::uint32_t frame, std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes, std::uint32_t flags = 0) {
    REQUIRE(pushMessage(q, frame, bytes, flags));
}

const std::vector<PortSpec> kTransposePorts = {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, false}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}};

std::string describe(const std::vector<Sent>& sent) {
    std::string out;
    char        buf[16];
    for (const Sent& s : sent) {
        std::snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%u/%u:", s.frame, s.flags);
        out += buf;
        for (std::uint8_t b : s.bytes) {
            std::snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, " %u", b);
            out += buf;
        }
        out += "\n";
    }
    return out;
}

}  // namespace

// ---- registration ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("a script pack registers on both builds of the host, with memory of its own", "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    const rp_package* desktop = rp_devtest_script_package();
    const rp_package* device = rp_devtest_script_package_device_mode();
    REQUIRE(desktop);
    REQUIRE(device);
    for (const rp_package* p : {desktop, device}) {
        CHECK(p->abi_version == RP_ABI_VERSION);
        CHECK(std::string(p->manifest_json) == R"({"id":"rp.devtest.script","version":"1.0.0"})");
        REQUIRE(p->node_type_count == 1);
        CHECK(std::string(p->node_types[0]->id) == "rp.devtest.script-transpose");
        REQUIRE(p->memory);
        CHECK(std::string(p->memory->name) == "devtest");
        rp_memory_req req{};
        rp_error err{};
        REQUIRE(p->memory->query(p, &req, &err));
        // The pack's heap, its context's own copy of the bytecode, and the host's state; the desktop's context is
        // kDesktopHeapFactor times the heap.
        const std::size_t extra = p == desktop ? (rp::mqjs::kDesktopHeapFactor - 1) * rp_script_devtest.heap_bytes : 0;
        CHECK(req.size == rp::mqjs::packageBytes(rp_script_devtest) + extra);
        CHECK(req.size > rp_script_devtest.heap_bytes + rp_script_devtest.bytecode_size);
        CHECK(req.align <= 8);
    }
    // Asked twice, the same package.
    CHECK(rp_devtest_script_package() == desktop);
    // The desktop's build describes its types, and a registry takes it; the device's describes nothing.
    const rp_node_type* d = desktop->node_types[0];
    REQUIRE(d->descriptor);
    REQUIRE(d->layout_for);
    CHECK(std::string(d->descriptor(d)).find(R"("id":"rp.devtest.script-transpose")") != std::string::npos);
    NodeRegistry registry;
    std::string  why;
    CHECK(registry.addPackage(desktop, &why));
    INFO(why);
    REQUIRE(registry.find("rp.devtest.script-transpose"));
    CHECK(registry.find("rp.devtest.script-transpose")->descriptor.layout.ports.size() == 2);
    CHECK_FALSE(device->node_types[0]->descriptor);
    CHECK_FALSE(device->node_types[0]->layout_for);
}

TEST_CASE("every C++ package has no package memory, on either build", "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    for (const DeviceEntry& e : deviceEntries()) {
        INFO(e.package << ": " << e.entry);
        CHECK_FALSE(e.desktop()->memory);
        CHECK_FALSE(e.desktop()->ctx);
        CHECK_FALSE(e.device()->memory);

    }
    for (const rp_package* p : {rp_core_package(), rp_dsp_package(), rp_n8_package(), rp_devtest_plan_package()})

}

// ---- the block API ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("a script node transposes through the block API, the same on both builds", "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    std::vector<std::vector<Sent>> runs;
    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
        INFO(b.name);
        Host host;
        Made n(typeOf(b.devtest, "rp.devtest.script-transpose"), host, msgpackOf(R"({"semitones":5})"),
               kTransposePorts);
        REQUIRE(n.node);
        std::vector<Sent> all;
        for (int block = 0; block < 3; ++block) {
            clearQueue(n.in(0));
            push(n.in(0), 0, {0x90, 60, 100});
            push(n.in(0), 3, {0x80, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(124 + block), 0}, 1);  // past 127 by 2 in the last block
            push(n.in(0), 3, {0xB0, 7, 64});
            push(n.in(0), 9, {0xC0, 5});
            push(n.in(0), 40, {0xF0, 0x7D, 1, 2, 0xF7}, 1);
            REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
            const std::vector<Sent> sent = n.sent(0);
            INFO(describe(sent));
            const std::vector<Sent> expected = {
                {0, 0, {0x90, 65, 100}},
                {3, 1, {0x80, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(std::min(129 + block, 127)), 0}},
                {3, 0, {0xB0, 7, 64}},
                {9, 0, {0xC0, 5}},
                {40, 1, {0xF0, 0x7D, 1, 2, 0xF7}},
            };
            CHECK(sent == expected);
            all.insert(all.end(), sent.begin(), sent.end());
        }
        CHECK(n.fault().empty());
        runs.push_back(all);
    }
    CHECK(runs[0] == runs[1]);
}

TEST_CASE("the block API: frames, transport, control and params, events and bytes, and what a block refuses",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    // The probe's layout: ctl, ev and raw in; out, bout and level out; the gain param.
    const std::vector<PortSpec> ports = {{RP_PORT_CONTROL, false}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, false}, {RP_PORT_BYTES, false},
                                         {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true},   {RP_PORT_BYTES, true},   {RP_PORT_CONTROL, true}};
    std::vector<std::string> transcripts;
    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
        INFO(b.name);
        Host host;
        Made n(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.probe"), host, {}, ports, {0.5});
        REQUIRE(n.node);
        n.transport = rp_transport{48000.0, 120.0, 2.5, RP_TRANSPORT_PLAYING};
        n.control(0).start = 0.25;
        REQUIRE(pushControl(n.control(0), 10, 0.5));
        REQUIRE(pushControl(n.control(0), 20, 1.0));
        REQUIRE(pushControl(*n.params[0], 3, 0.75));
        push(n.in(1), 1, {0x90, 60, 100});
        push(n.in(1), 5, {0xB0, 7, 64}, 0);
        push(n.in(2), 2, {0xF0, 1, 2, 0xF7}, RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH);
        REQUIRE(n.run(300) == RP_OK);
        INFO(n.fault());
        const std::vector<Sent> out = n.sent(0);
        INFO(describe(out));
        const std::vector<Sent> expected = {
            // frames 300 (44, 1), playing, tempo 120, ppq 2.5 * 4, 48 kHz, gain 0.5 at its start, one gain change
            {0, 0, {44, 1, 1, 120, 10, 48, 50, 1}},
            {1, 0, {0x90, 60, 100}},
            {5, 0, {0xB0, 7, 64}},
            // A port it does not have, an input named as an output and an audio port: three TypeErrors.
            {299, 0, {0xe0, 1, 2, 3}},
        };
        CHECK(out == expected);
        const std::vector<Sent> bytesOut = n.sent(1);
        CHECK(bytesOut == std::vector<Sent>{{2, RP_MESSAGE_FLUSH, {0xF0, 1, 2, 0xF7}}});
        const rp_control_queue& level = *n.outputs[2].u.control;
        REQUIRE(level.count == 3);
        CHECK(level.changes[0].frame == 0);
        CHECK(level.changes[0].value == 0.5);
        CHECK(level.changes[1].frame == 10);
        CHECK(level.changes[1].value == 1.0);
        CHECK(level.changes[2].frame == 20);
        CHECK(level.changes[2].value == 2.0);
        // The same objects, refilled, the next block: fewer messages, no changes.
        clearQueue(n.in(1));
        clearQueue(n.in(2));
        n.control(0).count = 0;
        n.params[0]->count = 0;
        push(n.in(1), 7, {0x80, 60, 0});
        REQUIRE(n.run(64) == RP_OK);
        const std::vector<Sent> second = n.sent(0);
        INFO(describe(second));
        REQUIRE(second.size() == 3);
        CHECK(second[0].bytes == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{64, 0, 1, 120, 10, 48, 50, 0});
        CHECK(second[1] == Sent{7, 0, {0x80, 60, 0}});
        transcripts.push_back(describe(out) + describe(second));
    }
    CHECK(transcripts[0] == transcripts[1]);
}

TEST_CASE("settings reach create as the definition parsed them, from JSON or msgpack", "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    const rp_package* desktop = rp_scripttest_script_package();
    const rp_package* device = rp_scripttest_script_package_device_mode();
    const std::vector<PortSpec> ports = {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}};
    auto textOf = [](Made& n) {
        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
        const std::vector<Sent> sent = n.sent(0);
        REQUIRE(sent.size() == 1);
        return std::string(sent[0].bytes.begin(), sent[0].bytes.end());
    };
    for (const char* json : {R"({"count":42,"name":"zz","taps":[9],"inner":{"depth":2}})",
                             R"({"count":-5,"ratio":1.5,"on":true,"mode":"fast"})", "{}"}) {
        INFO(json);
        Host host;
        // The desktop's build from JSON, as a graph document carries them: what it writes back is what it parsed.
        const std::string text(json);
        Made fromJson(typeOf(desktop, "rp.scripttest.settings"), host,
                      std::vector<std::uint8_t>(text.begin(), text.end()), ports, {}, {}, RP_SETTINGS_JSON);
        REQUIRE(fromJson.node);
        const auto* writer = static_cast<const SettingsJsonInterface*>(
            fromJson.node->vt->get_interface(fromJson.node, kSettingsJsonInterface));
        REQUIRE(writer);
        std::string parsed(512, '\0');
        parsed.resize(writer->write(fromJson.node, parsed.data(), parsed.size()));
        CHECK(textOf(fromJson) == parsed);
        // The device's build from the msgpack the exporter writes from that.
        Made fromMsgpack(typeOf(device, "rp.scripttest.settings"), host, msgpackOf(parsed.c_str()), ports);
        REQUIRE(fromMsgpack.node);
        CHECK(textOf(fromMsgpack) == parsed);
    }
    // Every default filled, and the fields in the schema's order.
    Host host;
    Made n(typeOf(desktop, "rp.scripttest.settings"), host, {}, ports);
    CHECK(textOf(n) ==
          R"({"count":7,"ratio":0.25,"on":false,"name":"abc","mode":"slow","taps":[1,2,3],"inner":{"depth":4},)"
          R"("extra":{}})");
    // Refused settings: the definition's words.
    const std::string bad = R"({"count":1e9})";
    const rp_settings s{bad.data(), bad.size(), RP_SETTINGS_JSON};
    rp_memory_req req{};
    rp_error err{};
    const rp_node_type* t = typeOf(desktop, "rp.scripttest.settings");
    CHECK_FALSE(t->query_memory(t, &s, &req, &err));
    CHECK(std::string(err.message).find("settings: count:") != std::string::npos);
    // Settings the definition takes and a device's decode would not: refused on the desktop as well, in the decode's
    // words, so both builds take the same settings and a planned node never faults on the box for its settings.
    const std::string longName = R"({"extra":{")" + std::string(64, 'k') + R"(":1}})";
    // The decode reads 8 containers deep: `fits` below is the settings object, extra's object and six arrays; `deep`
    // one array more.
    std::string deep = R"({"extra":{"k":)";
    for (int i = 0; i < 7; ++i) deep += "[";
    deep += "1";
    for (int i = 0; i < 7; ++i) deep += "]";
    deep += "}}";
    for (const std::string& text : {longName, deep}) {
        INFO(text);
        const rp_settings refused{text.data(), text.size(), RP_SETTINGS_JSON};
        CHECK_FALSE(t->query_memory(t, &refused, &req, &err));
        CHECK(std::string(err.message).find("its settings are not ones a device reads: TypeError: the settings ") == 0);
    }
    const std::string fits = R"({"extra":{")" + std::string(63, 'k') + R"(":[[[[[[1]]]]]]}})";
    const rp_settings taken{fits.data(), fits.size(), RP_SETTINGS_JSON};
    CHECK(t->query_memory(t, &taken, &req, &err));
}

TEST_CASE("portsChanged and activate run when the host says, create seeing the rate and block size",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
        INFO(b.name);
        Host host;

               {}, {1, 0});
        REQUIRE(n.node);
        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
````
