````cpp
TEST_CASE("the desktop's build keeps its instance through a settings change that keeps its layout",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    Host host;
    Made n(typeOf(rp_devtest_script_package(), "rp.devtest.script-transpose"), host, msgpackOf(R"({"semitones":2})"),
           kTransposePorts);
    REQUIRE(n.node);
    push(n.in(0), 0, {0x90, 60, 100});
    REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
    CHECK(n.sent(0) == std::vector<Sent>{{0, 0, {0x90, 62, 100}}});
    const std::string next = R"({"semitones":-12})";
    const rp_settings s{next.data(), next.size(), RP_SETTINGS_JSON};
    void*    prepared = nullptr;
    rp_error err{};
    REQUIRE(n.node->vt->prepare_settings(n.node, &s, &prepared, &err) == RP_PREPARE_SWAP);
    void* old = nullptr;
    n.node->vt->commit_settings(n.node, prepared, &old);
    n.node->vt->release_settings(n.node, old);
    REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
    CHECK(n.sent(0) == std::vector<Sent>{{0, 0, {0x90, 48, 100}}});
    const std::string refused = R"({"semitones":500})";
    const rp_settings r{refused.data(), refused.size(), RP_SETTINGS_JSON};
    CHECK(n.node->vt->prepare_settings(n.node, &r, &prepared, &err) == RP_PREPARE_INVALID);
    CHECK(std::string(err.message).find("semitones") != std::string::npos);
}

// ---- faults ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("a script node faults on a throw, a deadline, a promise, \"fault\" and no process, and stays faulted",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    struct Case {
        const char*   id;
        std::uint32_t kind;
        const char*   words;
    };
    const std::vector<Case> cases = {
        {"rp.scripttest.throws", RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_THREW, "process threw: RangeError: the throws node threw"},
        {"rp.scripttest.spins", RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_DEADLINE, "process ran past its deadline of 50000 us"},
        {"rp.scripttest.thenable", RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_REFUSED,
         "process returned a promise or a thenable: a device pack's node runs synchronously"},
        {"rp.scripttest.fault", RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_REFUSED, "process returned \"fault\""},
        {"rp.scripttest.no-process", RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_REFUSED, "create returned no object with a process function"},
        {"rp.scripttest.create-throws", RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_THREW, "create threw: TypeError: create would not"},
    };
    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
        Host host(50000);  // 50 ms of the thread's CPU time: what a preempted thread does not use up
        Made probe(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.probe"), host, {},
                   {{RP_PORT_CONTROL, false}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, false}, {RP_PORT_BYTES, false},
                    {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}, {RP_PORT_BYTES, true}, {RP_PORT_CONTROL, true}},
                   {0.5});
        REQUIRE(probe.node);
        for (const Case& c : cases) {
            INFO(b.name << ": " << c.id);
            Made n(typeOf(b.scripttest, c.id), host, {}, {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}});
            REQUIRE(n.node);
            const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
            CHECK(n.run() == RP_FAULT);
            CHECK(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start < std::chrono::seconds(2));
            CHECK(n.faultKind() == c.kind);
            CHECK(n.fault().find(c.words) == 0);
            // Faulted, it runs nothing more: the next block answers the same at once.
            CHECK(n.run() == RP_FAULT);
            CHECK(n.fault().find(c.words) == 0);
            // A fault is the node's own: another node of the pack runs on.
            CHECK(probe.run() == RP_OK);
        }
        CHECK(probe.fault().empty());
    }
}

TEST_CASE("a clock reading of 0 is no reading: the call runs on, and its deadline holds once the clock reads again",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    // The host's clock, scripted once the nodes are made, by the reading's number: `start` readings (the entry's start,
    // and its restart once the ports are ready), then `zeros` of 0 (a clock that answers nothing for a while), then
    // each `step` on from `from`.
    struct Scripted {
        bool          live = false;
        std::uint32_t calls = 0;
        std::uint64_t start = 1000, from = 1000, step = 10000;
        std::uint32_t zeros = 20;
        static std::uint64_t read(void* c) {
            auto& s = *static_cast<Scripted*>(c);
            if (!s.live) return cpuMicros(nullptr);
            const std::uint32_t k = s.calls++;
            if (k < 2) return s.start;
            if (k < 2 + s.zeros) return 0;
            return s.from + std::uint64_t{k - 1 - s.zeros} * s.step;
        }
    };
    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
        INFO(b.name);
        {
            Scripted clock;
            Host host(50000);
            host.clock.ctx = &clock;
            host.clock.micros = &Scripted::read;
            Made spins(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.spins"), host, {}, {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}});
            REQUIRE(spins.node);
            clock.live = true;
            CHECK(spins.run() == RP_FAULT);
            CHECK(spins.faultKind() == RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_DEADLINE);
            CHECK(spins.fault() == "process ran past its deadline of 50000 us");
            // The twenty readings of 0 timed nothing; the sixth poll after them, 60 ms from the start, faulted it.
            CHECK(clock.calls == 2 + 20 + 6);
        }
        {
            // An entry whose start reads 0 runs untimed: polls that read a time far past any deadline after it fault
            // nothing, where taking the 0 as a reading would fault the node at its first poll.
            Scripted clock;
            clock.start = 0;
            clock.zeros = 0;
            clock.from = std::uint64_t{1} << 40;
            Host host(1);
            host.clock.ctx = &clock;
            host.clock.micros = &Scripted::read;
            Made busy(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.busy"), host, {}, {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}});
            REQUIRE(busy.node);
            clock.live = true;
            REQUIRE(busy.run() == RP_OK);
            CHECK(clock.calls == 2);  // the start and the restart: an untimed entry's polls read no clock
            CHECK(busy.fault().empty());
        }
    }
}

TEST_CASE("a pack whose heap runs out silences every node of the pack, and no other pack's",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
        INFO(b.name);
        Host host;
        Made hog(typeOf(b.hog, "rp.hog.hog"), host, msgpackOf(R"({"grow":true})"), {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}});
        Made quiet(typeOf(b.hog, "rp.hog.quiet"), host, {}, {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}});
        Made other(typeOf(b.devtest, "rp.devtest.script-transpose"), host, msgpackOf(R"({"semitones":0})"),
                   kTransposePorts);
        REQUIRE(hog.node);
        REQUIRE(quiet.node);
        REQUIRE(other.node);
        // The quiet node's first block makes its pools, before the hog grows into the rest.
        REQUIRE(quiet.run() == RP_OK);
        // The heap runs out in whichever node's process allocates when it is full: the quiet node makes an array a
        // block too.
        int blocks = 0;
        while (blocks < 10000 && hog.run() == RP_OK && quiet.run() == RP_OK) ++blocks;
        CHECK(blocks > 0);
        CHECK(blocks < 10000);
        // Both nodes of the pack, at their next call, with the same words; the other pack's node runs on.
        CHECK(hog.run() == RP_FAULT);
        CHECK(quiet.run() == RP_FAULT);
        CHECK(hog.faultKind() == RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_HEAP);
        // The desktop's context is kDesktopHeapFactor times the manifest's heapBytes.
        const std::string heap = b.name == std::string("desktop") ? "163840" : "81920";
        CHECK(hog.fault() == "the pack's heap of " + heap +
                                 " bytes ran out (in a node's process), so every node of the pack is silenced");
        CHECK(quiet.faultKind() == RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_HEAP);
        CHECK(quiet.fault() == hog.fault());
        push(other.in(0), 4, {0x90, 64, 1});
        CHECK(other.run() == RP_OK);
        INFO(describe(other.sent(0)) << other.fault());
        CHECK(other.sent(0) == std::vector<Sent>{{4, 0, {0x90, 64, 1}}});
        CHECK(other.fault().empty());
    }
}

// ---- a warmed block -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("a script node's first block sizes its heap: no later block, a full queue's included, makes anything",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
        INFO(b.name);
        Host host;
        Made n(typeOf(b.devtest, "rp.devtest.script-transpose"), host, msgpackOf(R"({"semitones":3})"),
               kTransposePorts);
        REQUIRE(n.node);
        // Messages of every length up to three bytes, `count` of them, up to the queue's whole capacity.
        auto fill = [&](std::uint32_t block, std::uint32_t count) {
            clearQueue(n.in(0));
            for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < count; ++k) {
                const std::uint32_t length = 1 + (block + k) % 3;
                const std::uint8_t status = length == 3 ? 0x90 : length == 2 ? 0xC0 : 0xF8;
                const std::uint8_t bytes[3] = {status, static_cast<std::uint8_t>((block + k) % 100), 90};
                pushMessage(n.in(0), k, std::span<const std::uint8_t>(bytes, length));
            }
        };
        fill(0, 1);
        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
        const rp_script_heap_use first = n.heap(false);
        bool ran = true;
        std::uint32_t sentFull = 0;
        rp::test::beginCountingAllocations(rp::test::countsCAllocations());
        for (std::uint32_t block = 1; block < 320; ++block) {
            const std::uint32_t count = block == 100 || block == 300 ? 256 : block % 17;
            fill(block, count);
            ran = ran && n.run() == RP_OK;
            if (count == 256) sentFull = n.out(0).count;
        }
        const auto counted = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
        const rp_script_heap_use after = n.heap(false);
        CHECK(ran);
        CHECK(counted.allocations == 0);
        CHECK(counted.frees == 0);
        // The heap's top where the first block left it: nothing made, so no collection either, though two blocks
        // filled the queue whole.
        CHECK(first.heap > 0);
        CHECK(after.heap == first.heap);
        CHECK(sentFull == 256);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("a warmed block of the whole API allocates nothing, natively or in the JS heap",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    // The steady node: frames, transport, a control input and its changes, a param, messages, send and emit. Whole
    // numbers throughout, so it holds at 32 bits too, where a non-integer number is boxed (script/MqjsHost.hpp).
    const std::vector<PortSpec> ports = {{RP_PORT_CONTROL, false}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, false}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true},
                                         {RP_PORT_CONTROL, true}};
    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
        INFO(b.name);
        Host host;
        Made n(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.steady"), host, {}, ports, {50.0});
        REQUIRE(n.node);
        n.transport = rp_transport{48000.0, 120.0, 0.0, RP_TRANSPORT_PLAYING};
        auto fill = [&](std::uint32_t block) {
            clearQueue(n.in(1));
            n.control(0).count = 0;
            n.control(0).start = static_cast<double>(block % 8);
            for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < block % 5; ++k) {
                const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k), 1};
                pushMessage(n.in(1), k, note);
                pushControl(n.control(0), k * 10, static_cast<double>(k));
            }
        };
        fill(0);
        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
        const rp_script_heap_use first = n.heap(false);
        bool ran = true;
        rp::test::beginCountingAllocations(rp::test::countsCAllocations());
        for (std::uint32_t block = 1; block < 256; ++block) {
            fill(block);
            ran = ran && n.run() == RP_OK;
        }
        const auto counted = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
        const rp_script_heap_use after = n.heap(false);
        INFO(n.fault());
        CHECK(ran);
        CHECK(counted.allocations == 0);
        CHECK(counted.frees == 0);
        CHECK(after.heap == first.heap);
        // The last block (255: 0 messages, start 7): the summary, and the level as the stream summed.
        CHECK(n.sent(0) == std::vector<Sent>{{0, 0, {0, 1, 120, 50}}});
        REQUIRE(n.outputs[1].u.control->count == 1);
        CHECK(n.outputs[1].u.control->changes[0].value == 7.0);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("an array messages() handed out and JS emptied is grown again on a rooted slot, through collections",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    // The emptier sets its array's length to 0 every block, freeing its storage, so the host grows it again the next.
    // In the least heap it runs its blocks in, nearly every allocation collects, and the counts move from one of the
    // port's arrays to another (and every other block's input is SysEx, whose arrays are made for the block), so what
    // a collection frees lies below an array as well as above it, and the collection inside a grow moves the array.
    // Each block's output must be its input, message for message: with the grow handed a copy of the array rather than
    // its rooted slot, the engine writes the grown storage where the array was. The desktop's build runs it, in a pack
    // of the hog's bytecode whose heap the case sets, as the toolchain's runner does.
    static rp_mqjs_pack_source source = rp_script_hog;
    source.name = "hog-tight";
    const rp_package* package = rp::mqjs::exactPackage(source);
    INFO(rp::mqjs::packageRefusal());
    REQUIRE(package);
    const rp_node_type* type = typeOf(package, "rp.hog.emptier");
    REQUIRE(type);
    std::string wrong;  // a block whose output was not its input: the case fails, whatever the heap
    auto runs = [&](std::uint32_t heap, std::uint32_t blocks) {
        source.heap_bytes = heap;
        Host host;
        Made n(type, host, {}, kTransposePorts);
        REQUIRE(n.node);
        for (std::uint32_t block = 0; block < blocks; ++block) {
            clearQueue(n.in(0));
            std::vector<Sent> expected;
            const std::uint32_t count = block % 2 ? 1 + block * 7 % 32 : 1 + block * 37 % 256;
            for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < count; ++k) {
                std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes = {0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>((block + k) % 128),
                                                   static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k)};
                if (block % 2) {
                    bytes.assign(64, static_cast<std::uint8_t>((block + k) % 128));
                    bytes.front() = 0xf0;
                    bytes.back() = 0xf7;
                }
                push(n.in(0), k, bytes, k % 2);
                expected.push_back({k, k % 2, bytes});
            }
            if (n.run() != RP_OK) return false;  // the heap ran out: too small a heap for the search
            if (n.sent(0) != expected && wrong.empty())
                wrong = "heap " + std::to_string(heap) + ", block " + std::to_string(block) + ": " +
                        describe(n.sent(0));
        }
        return true;
    };
    // The least heap that runs 512 blocks (every count, both kinds), by halving, as the runner finds a pack's; then
    // long runs at it and above.
    std::uint32_t lo = rp::mqjs::kLeastContextBytes, hi = 81920;
    while (hi - lo > 8) {
        const std::uint32_t mid = (lo + (hi - lo) / 2) & ~7u;
        (runs(mid, 512) ? hi : lo) = mid;
    }
    for (const std::uint32_t margin : {0u, 64u, 512u, 4096u}) {
        INFO("margin " << margin);
        CHECK(runs(hi + margin, 4000));
    }
    INFO(wrong);
    CHECK(wrong.empty());
}

TEST_CASE("an object a pack kept past its block, read by the node that took its slot, throws and reads nothing",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
        INFO(b.name);
        Host host;
        {
            Made keeper(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.keeper"), host, {},
                        {{RP_PORT_CONTROL, false}, {RP_PORT_CONTROL, false}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, false},
                         {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}});
            REQUIRE(keeper.node);
            push(keeper.in(2), 3, {0x90, 60, 1});
            REQUIRE(pushControl(keeper.control(1), 5, 1.0));
            REQUIRE(keeper.run() == RP_OK);
        }
        // The keeper destroyed, its slot released; the reader, of one output, takes it, so the kept objects name its
        // slot, and ordinals past its one port: every read but data's throws the kept-object TypeError (a read in
        // any other slot would throw the not-running one, 4). data is the message's own value, read as it was.
        Made reader(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.reader"), host, {}, {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}});
        REQUIRE(reader.node);
        REQUIRE(reader.run() == RP_OK);
        INFO(reader.fault());
        CHECK(reader.sent(0) == std::vector<Sent>{{0, 0, {2, 1, 2, 2, 2}}});
    }
}

// ---- plans ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

namespace {

constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxFrames = 256;
constexpr std::size_t   kFrames = 9000;
constexpr std::size_t   kArenaBytes = 256 * 1024;
const std::vector<std::uint32_t> kSplit = {1, 31, 256, 3, 200, 77, 128};
const rp_transport               kTransport{48000.0, 120.0, 0.0, 0};

// A source's messages transposed by a script node into a digest, beside its audio straight in.
const char* kDocument = R"({"nodes":[
    {"id":"src","type":"rp.devtest.source","settings":{"seed":3}},
    {"id":"tp","type":"rp.devtest.script-transpose","settings":{"semitones":7}},
    {"id":"dg","type":"rp.devtest.digest"}],
  "wires":[
    {"from":"src.out","to":"dg.in"},
    {"from":"src.events","to":"tp.in"},
    {"from":"tp.out","to":"dg.events"}]})";

std::unique_ptr<NodeRegistry> desktopRegistry() {
    auto registry = std::make_unique<NodeRegistry>();
    for (const rp_package* p : {rp_devtest_plan_package(), rp_devtest_script_package()}) {
        std::string why;
        const bool added = registry->addPackage(p, &why);
        INFO(why);
        REQUIRE(added);
    }
    return registry;
}
const std::vector<const rp_package*>& deviceTypes() {
    static const std::vector<const rp_package*> types{rp_devtest_plan_package_device_mode(),
                                                      rp_devtest_script_package_device_mode()};
    return types;
}

void* acquireNoDevice(void*, const char*, const char*) { return nullptr; }
void  releaseNoDevice(void*, void*) {}
const rp_host_devices kDevices{nullptr, &acquireNoDevice, &releaseNoDevice};
const void*           deviceInterface(const rp_host*, const char* id) {
    return std::strcmp(id, RP_HOST_DEVICES_INTERFACE) == 0 ? &kDevices : nullptr;
}
const rp_host kDeviceHost{RP_ABI_VERSION, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, &ignoreLog, &deviceInterface};

ExportResult exported(std::size_t arena = kArenaBytes, const char* document = kDocument) {
    auto          registry = desktopRegistry();
    ExportOptions o;
    o.maxFrames = kMaxFrames;
    o.arenaBytes = arena;
    return exportPlan(document, *registry, deviceTypes(), o);
}

std::string described(const ExportResult& r) {
    std::string out;
    for (const auto& e : r.errors) out += e.code + " " + e.nodeId + ": " + e.message + "\n";
    return out;
}

struct Arena {
    std::vector<std::max_align_t> storage;
    explicit Arena(std::size_t bytes) : storage(bytes / sizeof(std::max_align_t) + 1) {}
    std::span<std::byte> span(std::size_t bytes) { return {reinterpret_cast<std::byte*>(storage.data()), bytes}; }
};

std::string refusal(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& blob, std::size_t bytes,
                    const std::vector<const rp_package*>& types) {
    Arena         arena(bytes);
    PlanLoadError err{};
    LoadedPlan*   plan = loadPlan(blob, arena.span(bytes), types, &kDeviceHost, &err);
    if (plan) {
        unloadPlan(plan);
        return "";
    }
    return std::string(err.code) + " " + err.node + ": " + err.message;
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("a plan with a script node, exported and loaded over the device-mode builds, renders what GraphHost renders",
          "[device-mode][script-pack][plan]") {
    // The desktop's render: GraphHost with the desktop's builds, its own package memory.
    rp_devtest_digest desktop{};
    std::uint32_t     desktopFaults = 0;
    {
        auto          registry = desktopRegistry();
        ResourceTable resources;
        GraphHost     host(*registry, resources, HostConfig{48000.0, kMaxFrames, Target::Desktop});
        const auto    result = host.setGraph(kDocument);
        std::string   errors;
        for (const auto& e : result.errors) errors += e.code + ": " + e.message + "\n";
        INFO(errors);
        REQUIRE(result.ok);
        std::size_t at = 0, block = 0;
        while (at < kFrames) {
            const auto n = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::min<std::size_t>(kSplit[block++ % kSplit.size()],
                                                                            kFrames - at));
            host.processBlock(n, kTransport);
            at += n;
        }
        rp_node* dg = host.node("dg");
        REQUIRE(dg);
        desktop = *static_cast<const rp_devtest_digest*>(dg->vt->get_interface(dg, kDigestInterface));
        desktopFaults = host.faultCount();
    }
    CHECK(desktopFaults == 0);
    CHECK(desktop.heard);

    const ExportResult r = exported();
    INFO(described(r));
    REQUIRE(r.ok());
    CHECK(r.size.packages == 1);
    CHECK(r.size.packageBytes == rp::mqjs::packageBytes(rp_script_devtest));

    // The loaded render, counting what the load, the blocks and the unload allocate (no Catch2 macro in the window).
    Arena                 arena(kArenaBytes);
    PlanLoadError         err{};
    rp_devtest_digest     loaded{};
    std::uint32_t         loadedFaults = ~0u;
    bool                  ok = false;
    std::size_t           packageCount = 0;
    rp::test::beginCountingAllocations(rp::test::countsCAllocations());
    LoadedPlan* plan = loadPlan(r.blob, arena.span(kArenaBytes), deviceTypes(), &kDeviceHost, &err);
    if (plan) {
        ok = true;
        packageCount = plan->packages.size();
        std::size_t at = 0, block = 0;
        while (at < kFrames) {
            const auto n = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::min<std::size_t>(kSplit[block++ % kSplit.size()],
                                                                            kFrames - at));
            runBlock(plan->view, n, kTransport);
            at += n;
        }
        if (LoadedNode* d = plan->find("dg"))
            loaded = *static_cast<const rp_devtest_digest*>(d->node->vt->get_interface(d->node, kDigestInterface));
        loadedFaults = plan->faults.load();
        unloadPlan(plan);
    }
    const auto counted = rp::test::endCountingAllocations();
    INFO(err.code << " " << err.node << ": " << err.message);
    REQUIRE(ok);
    CHECK(packageCount == 1);
    CHECK(loadedFaults == 0);
    CHECK(loaded.blocks == desktop.blocks);
    CHECK(loaded.hash == desktop.hash);
    CHECK(counted.allocations == 0);
    CHECK(counted.frees == 0);
}

TEST_CASE("the loader sizes a pack's memory with the plan, places it before the nodes, and refuses what cannot fit",
          "[device-mode][script-pack][plan]") {
    const ExportResult r = exported();
    INFO(described(r));
    REQUIRE(r.ok());
    PlanSize      size;
    PlanLoadError err{};
    REQUIRE(sizePlan(r.blob, deviceTypes(), 0, &size, &err));
    CHECK(size.packages == 1);
    CHECK(size.packageBytes == rp::mqjs::packageBytes(rp_script_devtest));
    CHECK(size.bytes >= size.structureBytes + size.packageBytes + size.instanceBytes);

    // Loaded, the pack's memory lies after the plan's structures and before the first node's instance.
    {
        Arena       arena(size.bytes);
        LoadedPlan* plan = loadPlan(r.blob, arena.span(size.bytes), deviceTypes(), &kDeviceHost, &err);
        INFO(err.message);
        REQUIRE(plan);
        REQUIRE(plan->packages.size() == 1);
        const LoadedPackage& pk = plan->packages[0];
        CHECK(pk.setUp);
        CHECK(pk.name() == "devtest");
        CHECK(pk.bytes == size.packageBytes);
        const auto* base = reinterpret_cast<const std::byte*>(arena.storage.data());
        CHECK(static_cast<const std::byte*>(pk.memory) >= base + size.structureBytes);
        for (const LoadedNode& n : plan->nodes)
            CHECK(static_cast<const std::byte*>(n.memory) >= static_cast<const std::byte*>(pk.memory) + pk.bytes);
        unloadPlan(plan);
        CHECK_FALSE(plan->packages[0].setUp);
    }

    // An arena that ends inside the pack's memory: refused, naming the pack and the overrun, before anything is made.
    const std::size_t short_ = size.structureBytes + size.packageBytes - 1;
    const std::string words = refusal(r.blob, short_, deviceTypes());
    INFO(words);
    CHECK(words.rfind("arena : the \"devtest\" pack's memory (" + std::to_string(size.packageBytes) +
                          " bytes) does not fit: the plan needs " + std::to_string(size.bytes) + " bytes, ",
                      0) == 0);
    CHECK(words.find(" past the " + std::to_string(short_) + "-byte arena") != std::string::npos);
    CHECK(rp_devtest_plan_live_device_mode() == 0);

    // The exporter refuses the same plan for the same arena, in the loader's words.
    const ExportResult tooSmall = exported(short_);
    REQUIRE_FALSE(tooSmall.ok());
    CHECK(tooSmall.errors[0].code == "arena");
    CHECK(tooSmall.errors[0].message.find("the \"devtest\" pack's memory") == 0);

    // A pack whose heap is under the least context the engine sets itself up in cannot be sized.
    static rp_mqjs_pack_source small = rp_script_devtest;
    small.heap_bytes = 1024;
    const rp_package* tiny = rp::mqjs::package(small);
    REQUIRE(tiny);
    const std::string under = refusal(r.blob, kArenaBytes, {rp_devtest_plan_package_device_mode(), tiny});
    CHECK(under == "package-memory : the \"devtest\" pack's memory cannot be sized: its heap is under the least "
                   "context the engine sets itself up in at this width, " +
                       std::to_string(rp::mqjs::kLeastContextBytes) + " bytes");

    // A pack that will not set up: refused at its setup, before any node is made, and nothing left alive.
    struct Refusing {
        static bool setup(const rp_package*, void*, rp_error* e) {
            std::snprintf(e->message, sizeof e->message, "%s", "not today");
            return false;
        }
    };
    const rp_package*       real = rp_devtest_script_package_device_mode();
    static rp_package_memory hooks;
    hooks = *real->memory;
    hooks.setup = &Refusing::setup;
    static rp_package refusing;
    refusing = *real;
    refusing.memory = &hooks;
    const std::string refused = refusal(r.blob, kArenaBytes, {rp_devtest_plan_package_device_mode(), &refusing});
    CHECK(refused == "package-setup : the \"devtest\" pack would not set up in its memory: not today");
    CHECK(rp_devtest_plan_live_device_mode() == 0);

    // A plan of C++ nodes alone has no package memory.
    const char* plain = R"({"nodes":[{"id":"src","type":"rp.devtest.source"},{"id":"dg","type":"rp.devtest.digest"}],
                           "wires":[{"from":"src.out","to":"dg.in"}]})";
    const ExportResult cpp = exported(kArenaBytes, plain);
    INFO(described(cpp));
    REQUIRE(cpp.ok());
    CHECK(cpp.size.packages == 0);
    CHECK(cpp.size.packageBytes == 0);
}

// ---- the engine's floor ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("the exporter refuses a script node whose first block faults on the device's build, and settings it would",
          "[device-mode][script-pack][plan]") {
    auto registry = std::make_unique<NodeRegistry>();
    for (const rp_package* p : {rp_devtest_plan_package(), rp_scripttest_script_package()}) {
        std::string why;
        REQUIRE(registry->addPackage(p, &why));
    }
    const std::vector<const rp_package*> types{rp_devtest_plan_package_device_mode(),
                                               rp_scripttest_script_package_device_mode()};
    ExportOptions o;
    o.maxFrames = kMaxFrames;
    o.arenaBytes = 1024 * 1024;
    // A create that throws plans (the desktop makes no instance) and loads; its first block, which the trial load runs,
    // faults it, and the export is refused naming it.
    const ExportResult throws = exportPlan(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"ct","type":"rp.scripttest.create-throws"}],"wires":[]})",
                                           *registry, types, o);
    INFO(described(throws));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(throws.ok());
    CHECK(throws.errors[0].code == "create-failed");
    CHECK(throws.errors[0].nodeId == "ct");
    CHECK(throws.errors[0].message.find(
              "its first block faulted on the device's build: create threw: TypeError: create would not") == 0);
    // A first block that runs on is held to the exporter's clock (the thread's CPU time at the desktop's deadline),
    // so it faults the node rather than hanging the export.
    const ExportResult spins =
        exportPlan(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sp","type":"rp.scripttest.spins"}],"wires":[]})", *registry, types, o);
    INFO(described(spins));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(spins.ok());
    CHECK(spins.errors[0].code == "create-failed");
    CHECK(spins.errors[0].message ==
          "its first block faulted on the device's build: process ran past its deadline of 500000 us");
    // Settings the device's decode would not read are refused where they are planned.
    const std::string longName = R"({"nodes":[{"id":"st","type":"rp.scripttest.settings","settings":{"extra":{")" +
                                 std::string(70, 'k') + R"(":1}}}],"wires":[]})";
    const ExportResult named = exportPlan(longName, *registry, types, o);
    INFO(described(named));
    REQUIRE_FALSE(named.ok());
    CHECK(named.errors[0].code == "settings-invalid");
    CHECK(named.errors[0].message.find("not ones a device reads") != std::string::npos);
    // And a node that runs is no fault of the export's.
    const ExportResult fine = exportPlan(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"st","type":"rp.scripttest.settings"}],"wires":[]})",
                                         *registry, types, o);
    INFO(described(fine));
    CHECK(fine.ok());
}

TEST_CASE("a script node across threads: made on the audio thread, swapped, rebuilt and released while blocks run",
          "[device-mode][script-pack][script-threads]") {
    // GraphHost with an audio thread running blocks while the control thread plans. The first document has devtest's
    // pack alone; the second adds scripttest's steady node, so its pack is set up (control thread) while blocks run.
    // Each document moves the devtest transpose's semitones (a settings swap, onSettings on the audio thread) and every
    // eighth renames it (a new instance made on the audio thread at its first block, the old one's slot released
    // through the ring, both pools in the pack's heap until the old plan is reclaimed: what the desktop's
    // kDesktopHeapFactor holds). The ThreadSanitizer build runs this case for the host's cross-thread protocol.
    NodeRegistry registry;
    for (const rp_package* p :
         {rp_devtest_plan_package(), rp_devtest_script_package(), rp_scripttest_script_package()}) {
        std::string why;
        INFO(why);
        REQUIRE(registry.addPackage(p, &why));
    }
    ResourceTable resources;
    GraphHost     host(registry, resources, HostConfig{48000.0, kMaxFrames, Target::Desktop});
    auto document = [](int k) {
        const std::string tp = "tp" + std::to_string(k / 8);
        const std::string semitones = std::to_string(k % 12);
        if (k == 0)
            return R"({"nodes":[
                {"id":"src","type":"rp.devtest.source","settings":{"seed":3}},
                {"id":")" + tp + R"(","type":"rp.devtest.script-transpose",
                 "settings":{"semitones":)" + semitones + R"(}},
                {"id":"dg","type":"rp.devtest.digest"}],
              "wires":[{"from":"src.events","to":")" + tp + R"(.in"},{"from":")" + tp + R"(.out","to":"dg.events"}]})";
        return R"({"nodes":[
            {"id":"src","type":"rp.devtest.source","settings":{"seed":3}},
            {"id":"st","type":"rp.scripttest.steady"},
            {"id":")" + tp + R"(","type":"rp.devtest.script-transpose","settings":{"semitones":)" + semitones + R"(}},
            {"id":"dg","type":"rp.devtest.digest"}],
          "wires":[{"from":"src.events","to":"st.ev"},{"from":"st.out","to":")" + tp + R"(.in"},
                   {"from":")" + tp + R"(.out","to":"dg.events"}]})";
    };
    REQUIRE(host.setGraph(document(0)).ok);
    std::atomic<bool> stop{false};
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> blocks{0};
    host.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    std::thread audio([&] {
        while (!stop.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
            host.processBlock(64, kTransport);
            blocks.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        }
    });
    auto settle = [&] {
        // Let the audio thread take each plan (and run the node) before the next.
        const std::uint32_t seen = blocks.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        while (blocks.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) < seen + 4) std::this_thread::yield();
    };
    settle();
    bool planned = true;
    for (int k = 1; k < 200 && planned; ++k) {
        planned = host.setGraph(document(k)).ok;
        settle();
    }
    stop.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    audio.join();
    host.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    CHECK(planned);
    CHECK(host.faultCount() == 0);
    rp_node* dg = host.node("dg");
    REQUIRE(dg);
    CHECK(static_cast<const rp_devtest_digest*>(dg->vt->get_interface(dg, kDigestInterface))->heard);
}

namespace {

// A GraphHost node's script fault, or null.
const char* faultOf(GraphHost& host, std::string_view id) {
    rp_node* n = host.node(id);
    if (!n) return nullptr;
    const auto* f = static_cast<const rp_script_fault*>(n->vt->get_interface(n, RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_INTERFACE));
    return f ? f->reason(n) : nullptr;
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("on the desktop, a pack whose heap ran out is set up again once its last node is gone",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    NodeRegistry registry;
    for (const rp_package* p : {rp_devtest_plan_package(), rp_hog_script_package()}) {
        std::string why;
        INFO(why);
        REQUIRE(registry.addPackage(p, &why));
    }
    ResourceTable resources;
    GraphHost     host(registry, resources, HostConfig{48000.0, kMaxFrames, Target::Desktop});
    REQUIRE(host.setGraph(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"hog","type":"rp.hog.hog","settings":{"grow":true}},
                                       {"id":"q","type":"rp.hog.quiet"}],"wires":[]})")
                .ok);
    int blocks = 0;
    while (blocks < 100000 && host.faultCount() < 2) {
        host.processBlock(64, kTransport);
        ++blocks;
    }
    REQUIRE(host.faultCount() == 2);
    const std::string dead = faultOf(host, "q") ? faultOf(host, "q") : "";
    CHECK(dead.find("the pack's heap of 163840 bytes ran out") == 0);
    // While a node of the dead pack is planned, a new one is as dead.
    REQUIRE(host.setGraph(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"hog","type":"rp.hog.hog","settings":{"grow":true}},
                                       {"id":"q","type":"rp.hog.quiet"},{"id":"q2","type":"rp.hog.quiet"}],
                             "wires":[]})")
                .ok);
    host.processBlock(64, kTransport);
    CHECK(faultOf(host, "q2") != nullptr);
    // A plan without them: once the old plans are reclaimed and the last node is destroyed, the pack is set up afresh,
    // and the next plan's node of it runs.
    REQUIRE(host.setGraph(R"({"nodes":[],"wires":[]})").ok);
    host.processBlock(64, kTransport);
    host.reclaim();
    REQUIRE(host.setGraph(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"q3","type":"rp.hog.quiet"}],"wires":[]})").ok);
    for (int k = 0; k < 16; ++k) host.processBlock(64, kTransport);
    CHECK(host.node("q3"));
    CHECK(faultOf(host, "q3") == nullptr);
    CHECK_FALSE(host.isFaulted("q3"));
}

TEST_CASE("on the desktop, with no clock of its host's, a script node's deadline is its thread's CPU time at 500 ms",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    NodeRegistry registry;
    for (const rp_package* p : {rp_devtest_plan_package(), rp_scripttest_script_package()}) {
        std::string why;
        INFO(why);
        REQUIRE(registry.addPackage(p, &why));
    }
    ResourceTable resources;
    GraphHost     host(registry, resources, HostConfig{48000.0, kMaxFrames, Target::Desktop});
    REQUIRE(host.setGraph(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sp","type":"rp.scripttest.spins"}],"wires":[]})").ok);
    const std::uint64_t start = cpuMicros(nullptr);
    host.processBlock(64, kTransport);
    const std::uint64_t spent = cpuMicros(nullptr) - start;
    CHECK(host.faultCount() == 1);
    const char* why = faultOf(host, "sp");
    REQUIRE(why);
    CHECK(std::string(why) == "process ran past its deadline of 500000 us");
    // The thread's CPU time, polled every 10000 instructions: at the deadline, and not much past it.
    CHECK(spent >= rp::mqjs::kDesktopDeadlineMicros);
    CHECK(spent < 4 * rp::mqjs::kDesktopDeadlineMicros);
}

TEST_CASE("the least context the host makes is one the engine sets itself up in without writing past it",
          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
    // A buffer of the least size, a guard after it: MicroQuickJS's setup of RetroPlug's standard library stays inside.
    constexpr std::size_t kGuard = 512;
    std::vector<std::uint64_t> memory((rp::mqjs::kLeastContextBytes + kGuard) / 8, 0xa5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5ull);
    JSContext* ctx = JS_NewContext(memory.data(), rp::mqjs::kLeastContextBytes, &rp_mqjs_stdlib);
    REQUIRE(ctx);
    JS_FreeContext(ctx);
    bool guarded = true;
    for (std::size_t i = rp::mqjs::kLeastContextBytes / 8; i < memory.size(); ++i)
        guarded = guarded && memory[i] == 0xa5a5a5a5a5a5a5a5ull;
    CHECK(guarded);
}

// ---- measured -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

TEST_CASE("a script node's cost a message, and its pack's heap use", "[.][script-bench]") {
    // The devtest transpose, each build, and rp.core.midi-filter (a C++ node of the same shape, passing everything), at
    // 16 and 256 messages a block (a queue's whole capacity). The heap is the same at any count: the port's pool is
    // made to its queue's 256 places at the first block, whose time (the instance made, the pools, the block) is given
    // too.
    constexpr std::uint32_t kBlocks = 16000;
    struct Subject {
        const char*         name;
        const rp_node_type* type;
        bool                script;
    };
    const std::vector<Subject> subjects = {
        {"desktop script", typeOf(rp_devtest_script_package(), "rp.devtest.script-transpose"), true},
        {"device script", typeOf(rp_devtest_script_package_device_mode(), "rp.devtest.script-transpose"), true},
        {"device C++ midi-filter", typeOf(rp_core_package_device_mode(), "rp.core.midi-filter"), false},
    };
    for (const std::uint32_t messages : {16u, 256u}) {
        for (const Subject& subject : subjects) {
            Host host;
            Made n(subject.type, host, subject.script ? msgpackOf(R"({"semitones":3})") : msgpackOf("{}"),
                   kTransposePorts);
            REQUIRE(n.node);
            auto fill = [&](std::uint32_t block) {
                clearQueue(n.in(0));
                for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < messages; ++k) {
                    const std::uint8_t note[3] = {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k % 2 ? 0x80 : 0x90),
                                                  static_cast<std::uint8_t>(40 + (block + k) % 40), 90};
                    pushMessage(n.in(0), k * 256 / messages, note);
                }
            };
            fill(0);
            const auto firstStart = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
            REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
            const double firstUs =
                std::chrono::duration<double, std::micro>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - firstStart).count();
            const rp_script_heap_use first = subject.script ? n.heap(true) : rp_script_heap_use{};
            for (std::uint32_t block = 1; block < 64; ++block) {
                fill(block);
                REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
            }
            const auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
            for (std::uint32_t block = 0; block < kBlocks; ++block) {
                fill(block);
                n.run();
            }
            const double ns =
                std::chrono::duration<double, std::nano>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start).count() /
                (double{kBlocks} * messages);
            const rp_script_heap_use warm = subject.script ? n.heap(true) : rp_script_heap_use{};
            std::printf("%s: %.0f ns a message (%u a block), first block %.0f us", subject.name, ns, messages, firstUs);
            if (subject.script)
                std::printf("; heap: context %zu, fixed %zu, live %zu after the first block, %zu after %u more",
                            warm.bytes, warm.fixed, first.heap, warm.heap, kBlocks + 63);
            std::printf("\n");
        }
    }
}
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to the day the prototype's
hashes were taken against, 4 November 2026 (the command spells the string out), as the gate's record does
(`/tmp/e4pro/gate-commands.txt`); nothing else may differ, and the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the
date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash compares only an image built from this worktree's path,
against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check, `/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same
Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1: an image built elsewhere (the `env
-i` runs' clones under `/tmp/e4-ci`, a scratch worktree) is judged by its sizes, never hashed.

````bash
The MicroQuickJS script host, and package memory in the SDK and the loader

A device script pack's nodes run on MicroQuickJS behind the node ABI, on the desktop as the box will run them
(docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md sections 4 and 5).

- graph-runtime's script/MqjsHost: one portable source built two ways. The device's build (no heap, no exceptions, no
  RTTI; retroplug-mqjs-host-device proves it in the ordinary build) registers a pack's types from the ids its build
  recorded, creates a node from the msgpack the blob carries and runs it in the pack's context; the desktop's adds the
  descriptor, layout_for, a settings swap and rp.sdk.settings-json/1 from a control context of its own, so exportPlan
  writes a script node's settings. A node's instance is made on the thread that runs blocks; a destroy queues its slot.
- RetroPlug's own standard library for the engine (script/rp_mqjs_stdlib.c over upstream's tables, its REPL's globals
  left out) with the block API's classes; every C function hands the call to the host through the context's opaque,
  so one table serves both builds in one binary. retroplug_mquickjs_stdlib() generates a library's tables at 64 and
  32 bits; retroplug_mquickjs_engine() builds the engine with them.
- The block API: messages(), send(), control(), emit(), frames and transport. Every object a block hands out is made at
  the node's first block, each input port's pool to its queue's whole capacity, and refilled after (an array per power
  of two that holds the count, grown on a rooted slot), so a pack's heap need is fixed by its plan and a warmed block
  allocates nothing, natively or in the JS heap (at 32 bits, a read of a non-integer number boxes it). A read through
  an object kept past its block is checked against the running node's ports, kept natively, and the running block, and
  throws. send() copies at the call.
- Faults: a throw, a deadline overrun (the engine's interrupt handler over the whole entry: the host's clock,
  rp.host.clock/1, at 10 ms on the box, or the thread's CPU time at 500 ms on the desktop, a reading of 0 timing
  nothing, started again once the ports' pools are made), a promise, "fault" or no process each fault the node
  (rp.script.fault/1 says why); a heap that runs out kills the pack's context and every node of the pack faults, no
  other pack's.
- The desktop's hosts give a pack's context twice its manifest's heap, since a re-plan holds a replaced instance
  beside its replacement; the box, the exporter's trial load and the toolchain's runner (exactPackage) give it
  exactly. A desktop pack whose heap ran out is set up afresh once its last node is destroyed.
- The desktop refuses settings the device's decode would not read (a key or a nesting past its limits), and the
  exporter's trial load runs one block, under a clock of its own, and refuses a plan whose script node faults there.
- The engine is compiled from script/rp_mqjs_engine.c, which includes mquickjs.c whole and reads its JSContext for
  rp.script.heap/1. The script interfaces are graph/rp_script.h in the SDK; graph/Text.hpp is the loader's and the
  host's one text builder, graph/ThreadClock.hpp the host's and the exporter's thread CPU clock.
- Each context runs a copy of the bytecode of its own: running bytecode writes into it (a string constant used as a
  property name is marked unique where it lies), so two contexts never share one.
- rp_package gains `memory` (rp_package_memory: a name, query, setup, teardown) and `ctx`; every C++ package leaves them
  null. A node finds its package's block through its host (rp.host.packages/1). The loader sizes each package the
  plan's types come from once, places it after the plan's structures and before the nodes, sets it up first and tears
  it down last, refusing a plan that cannot hold it naming the pack and the overrun; its error text is written out of
  line, so the loader is smaller than before. GraphHost and the exporter give theirs from graph/PackageMemory. A script
  pack's memory is its manifest's heap (the whole context) plus the host's state and the bytecode copy; a context
  under the engine's least (4096 bytes at 64 bits, 2560 at 32) is refused before the engine sees it.
- A package's script pack is a registration a product lists beside its native entries (retroplug_product, NO_SCRIPTS
  for the device check's), compiled again by retroplug_device_mode_objects; the export tool carries devtest's.
- The device-pack toolchain runs a pack's transcript and its heap check on retroplug-mqjs-run (the host over its own
  standard library), the heap check now creating and running a node of each type, and writes the bytecode as C for a
  binary to carry.
- Tests: ScriptPack.test.cpp in retroplug-device-mode-test, over devtest's pack and two of the test's own (scripttest,
  hog): registration, the block API on both builds, settings, hooks, each fault, a clock reading 0, the desktop's own
  deadline, a heap running out and a dead pack set up again, a full queue's first block sizing the heap and no later
  block allocating, an emptied array grown in a heap that collects at every allocation, a kept object refused, the
  exporter's refusals, GraphHost re-planning while an audio thread runs blocks ([script-threads], for the
  ThreadSanitizer build), and a plan with a script node exported and loaded over the device-mode builds rendering what
  GraphHost renders, the loader's package-memory sizing and refusals. test/graph/device-pack/guard-else.ts type-
  checks.
EOF
````

---

### Task 3: the bliptoaster pack and the box: the cart's MIDI policy as a TypeScript node

Design sections 4 to 6 and section 8's third commit. The `bliptoaster` pack (`packages/bliptoaster`, a script pack
alone, `heapBytes` 24576) holds one node, `rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy`: no settings, `idle: "skip"`, `in:
events.in()` and `out: events.out({ match: "in" })`; it drops polyphonic and channel aftertouch, system common and
real time and forwards everything else with its frame, flags and order. The box's plan becomes `rp.device.midi-in` ->
the policy -> `rp.n8.nes`, the arena 65536 bytes, `rp.device.midi-in` 64 messages, and the image carries the pack's
32-bit device runtime in flash, copies it into the pack's block in the arena at setup and runs it on the device's
MicroQuickJS, the engine at -Os. Around it: the engine wrapper (every external name renamed `rp_mqjs_*`, since every
desktop product now links the engine beside QuickJS; two upstream GC bugs and three swallowed exceptions fixed by
wrappers, guarded by a configure-time hash of the upstream text; `abort` wrapped, a `PRI*64` shim, the ARM unwinder
replaced by a trap); sizing at the target's width and the 3/2 heuristic; each pack bundled a second time as its device
runtime, which every node context runs; `idle: "skip"` and `forward()` on both hosts; the re-entry cap of 4 and the
deadline scaled by a block's messages; the box's stack guard. Every desktop product lists the pack, so the `[packages]`
golden gains its type at the end of each row.

Two reds come first, on Task 2's binaries as they are, the second with the golden placed. Then the engine wrapper,
the host, the SDK and the toolchain, the pack with its lockfile entry (checked by a frozen install), the box, and the

- [ ] **Step 3: The engine wrapper: the rename, the fixes and their guard, and the device's shims**

`rp_mqjs_names.h` renames the engine's 197 external names to `rp_mqjs_*`, force-included into the engine's sources
(desktop and device) and included by `rp_mqjs.h`: every desktop product now links mquickjs beside QuickJS, and 46
names clashed (`JS_Call`, `JS_NewContext`, `i32toa`, `js_dtoa`, ...). `cmake/mquickjs-names.cmake` is a post-build
check that the library defines no other external name (toolchain `nm` on Linux, Xcode's on macOS, never run; none on
MSVC). `rp_mqjs_engine.c` carries the fixes as wrappers, compiling upstream's definition under another name and
routing every call (first argument spelt `ctx`) to ours: `JS_MakeUniqueString` collects before the name table grows,
so a collection can no longer land inside the growth and corrupt it; `rp_mqjs_keep_bytecode_names` marks a loaded
bytecode's strings kept after relocation, so the weak table no longer drops them; `js_string_concat_subst` and
`string_buffer_puts` make the engine's StringBuffer sticky, so `String.prototype.replace` and the buffer's appends
return an exception they swallowed; `hasOwnProperty` makes its key first and returns on a throw;
`rp_mqjs_new_array_buffer`, `_uint8_array` and `_uint8_view` build typed arrays in the engine with no `JS_Call`
(lengths past `JS_SHORTINT_MAX` refused); and `rp_mqjs_limit_reentries` starts a context's `JS_Call` count at 8 - 4.
**`cmake/mquickjs.cmake` hashes the text of each upstream span these rest on** (`JS_MakeUniqueString`, the sweep of
`unique_strings`, replace and its substitution, the StringBuffer and its appends, `js_object_hasOwnProperty`,
`js_typed_array_constructor`; CR stripped) and counts `js_call_rec_count`'s mentions (exactly 4), failing the
configure with words that name `rp_mqjs_engine.c` on any change. `rp_mqjs_device.c` wraps `abort` to the SDK's `panic`
(newlib's reaches `_malloc_r`), `cmake/mquickjs-device/rp_mqjs_inttypes.h` is the forced include giving the `PRI*64`
macros this toolchain's freestanding `<stdint.h>` lacks, and `cmake/device-image/no-unwind.c`, linked into every
`rp_device_executable`, is a strong `__aeabi_unwind_cpp_pr0` that panics, in place of the ARM unwinder newlib's
`setjmp.o` pulls in through `.ARM.exidx`. graph-runtime's CMake defines the engine (at -Os) and the host for a device
build given `RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR`, the 32-bit tables (`retroplug-mqjs-tables-32`), and the engine built with
`DEBUG_GC` (a collection at every allocation, `retroplug-mqjs-engine-gc`) under a second runner,
`retroplug-mqjs-run-gc`, which the `[debug-gc]` cases hold to the ordinary runner's digests.

Create `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/script/rp_mqjs_names.h`:

````cpp
/* rp_mqjs_names.h - MicroQuickJS's external names, made RetroPlug's: every function and object the engine's library
 * defines with external linkage (mquickjs.c, dtoa.c, libm.c and cutils.c), renamed rp_mqjs_<name> by the preprocessor.
 * A binary that carries a device script pack's registration (every desktop product) carries QuickJS as well (the
 * desktop's script host and UI, deps/dpf.js's txiki), and the two engines define the same names: JS_NewContext,
 * JS_Call, JS_GetPropertyStr and some forty more, and the number-printing helpers of their shared cutils (i32toa,
 * js_dtoa). The vendored sources are compiled as they stand, with this header first (-include, cmake/mquickjs.cmake's
 * retroplug_mquickjs_engine and graph-runtime's device engine), and rp_mqjs.h, which every RetroPlug source that
 * calls the engine includes, includes it before mquickjs.h, so declarations, definitions and calls all take the new
 * names and nothing else changes. A name the engine gains with an upstream bump and this list lacks is caught at the
 * desktop build, which holds the library to defining no external name outside rp_mqjs_ (cmake/mquickjs-names.cmake). */
#ifndef RP_MQJS_NAMES_H
#define RP_MQJS_NAMES_H
````

Create `cmake/mquickjs-names.cmake`:

````cmake
# Holds MicroQuickJS's library to its renamed external names (graph-runtime's script/rp_mqjs_names.h): every symbol
# the library defines with external linkage must be one of RetroPlug's, rp_mqjs_<name>, since a desktop binary links
# the engine beside QuickJS, which defines many of upstream's own names. A name an upstream bump adds and the header
# does not rename fails the build here, naming it, rather than at the link of every product.
#
#   cmake -DNM=<nm> -DLIBRARY=<archive> -P cmake/mquickjs-names.cmake
execute_process(COMMAND "${NM}" -g --defined-only "${LIBRARY}" OUTPUT_VARIABLE _out RESULT_VARIABLE _rc ERROR_QUIET)
if(NOT _rc EQUAL 0)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "mquickjs-names: ${NM} could not read ${LIBRARY}")
endif()
string(REPLACE "\n" ";" _lines "${_out}")
set(_stray "")
foreach(_line IN LISTS _lines)
    # "<address> <type> <name>": a defined name of external linkage (Mach-O's names lead with an underscore).
    if(_line MATCHES "^[0-9A-Fa-f]+ [A-Za-z] _?([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)$")
        if(NOT CMAKE_MATCH_1 MATCHES "^rp_mqjs_")
            list(APPEND _stray "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
        endif()
    endif()
endforeach()
if(_stray)
    list(REMOVE_DUPLICATES _stray)
    list(JOIN _stray " " _stray)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "mquickjs-names: ${LIBRARY} defines names that are not RetroPlug's (rename each in "
                        "packages/graph-runtime/native/src/script/rp_mqjs_names.h): ${_stray}")
endif()
````

Create `packages/graph-runtime/native/src/script/rp_mqjs_device.c`:

````cpp
/* What a device image needs of MicroQuickJS's C runtime beyond the engine (graph-runtime's device engine:
 * packages/graph-runtime/native/CMakeLists.txt), in a Pico SDK image under the link trap
 * (cmake/device-image.cmake).
 *
 * abort. The engine calls it on a state it cannot go on from (a corrupt bytecode, an opcode it does not know). newlib's
 * abort raises SIGABRT through its signal table, which it sets up on the heap (_init_signal_r, _malloc_r), so linking
 * it would put the heap in the image and the trap refuses it; the engine library wraps the symbol instead
 * (--wrap=abort), and every call in the image, the engine's and any other's, reaches this: the SDK's panic, which
 * prints its message on the console and stops. Standalone, the box's watchdog then restarts it; with a debugger
 * attached it stays stopped (panic ends at a breakpoint, and the box's watchdog is paused on debug, box.cpp) until
 * someone resumes or resets it. This ties the device engine to the Pico SDK's panic, the one SDK every image that
 * links it (the box, the device check) builds on; a device on another SDK gives its own. setjmp and longjmp (the
 * engine's parser, which JSON.parse and the Function constructor reach) link as newlib has them: neither reaches the
 * heap. */
extern void panic(const char* fmt, ...) __attribute__((noreturn));

void __wrap_abort(void) { panic("MicroQuickJS: abort"); }
````

````cpp
/* What a device build of MicroQuickJS (deps/mquickjs) is compiled with first (-include, graph-runtime's device engine:
 * packages/graph-runtime/native/CMakeLists.txt): the 64-bit printf conversions mquickjs.c names (PRIu64, in a debug
 * dump). arm-none-eabi GCC's <stdint.h> is its freestanding one, which newlib's <inttypes.h> does not recognise, so
 * newlib defines none of the 64-bit ones there; the vendored source is compiled as it stands, and this supplies them
 * as newlib's own would for that target (int64_t is long long). */
#ifndef RP_MQJS_INTTYPES_H
#define RP_MQJS_INTTYPES_H

#define PRId64 "lld"
#endif
#ifndef PRIu64
#define PRIu64 "llu"
#endif
#ifndef PRIx64
#define PRIx64 "llx"
#endif
#ifndef PRIo64
#define PRIo64 "llo"
#endif

#endif /* RP_MQJS_INTTYPES_H */
````

Create `cmake/device-image/no-unwind.c`:

````cpp
/* What every RP2350 image links in place of libgcc's ARM unwinder (cmake/device-image.cmake's rp_device_executable).
 *
 * newlib's setjmp.o, which MicroQuickJS's engine links (its exceptions are setjmp and longjmp), carries .ARM.exidx
 * entries whose personality routine is __aeabi_unwind_cpp_pr0, and that one reference pulls libgcc's whole unwinder
 * into the image (unwind-arm.o, libunwind.o and pr-support.o, about 4 KB, which the box runs from RAM). Nothing in an
 * image unwinds: it builds with -fno-exceptions, and the link trap refuses every way to throw. So the routine is
 * defined here, strong, as a trap of its own: a call to it stops the image (the SDK's panic, which prints and halts).
 * Were something to need the real unwinder, it would pull unwind-arm.o, which defines the routine again, and the link
 * would fail on the two definitions, loudly. It is not one of the trap's wrapped symbols (device-image.cmake's list):
 * those are calls the image must not make, and this one only an index entry names, which no code here ever follows. */
#include "pico.h"

void __aeabi_unwind_cpp_pr0(void) { panic("__aeabi_unwind_cpp_pr0: nothing in this image unwinds"); }
````

````diff
+ * is included whole and unpatched, and what follows it is RetroPlug's (rp_mqjs.h declares it).
+ *
+ * One change of behaviour is RetroPlug's too, made here rather than in the vendored file: how a string is made a
+ * property name (JS_MakeUniqueString). The engine keeps the names made at run time in a sorted table its collector
+ * treats as weak, dropping each whose string is not marked, and a collection that runs inside the table's own growth
+ * (the allocation in JS_MakeUniqueString's resize) drops entries under the insertion: the resize copies the entries
+ * the table had before the collection and the insertion lands at the place it found before it, so the table comes back
+ * with stale words in it, which the next lookup reads as strings (a crash, or a name that resolves to another's slot).
+ * It takes a dead name in the table and a collection at that one allocation, which a tight heap makes likely (the
+ * toolchain's least-heap search met it). RetroPlug's version, rp_mqjs_make_unique_string below, collects first when the
+ * insertion has to grow the table and finds its place after, so the growth itself never meets a dead entry. Every call
+ * to JS_MakeUniqueString in mquickjs.c passes `ctx` first, which is what the two macros below tell the definition
+ * (whose first parameter is `JSContext *ctx`) from the calls by: the definition is compiled under another name and
+ * left unused, and every call reaches RetroPlug's. A bump of deps/mquickjs that adds a call spelt otherwise, or
+ * renames the function, fails to compile here rather than quietly reaching the upstream body.
+ *
+ * Three exceptions the engine loses are RetroPlug's to keep, by the same trick where it can be:
+ * - String.prototype.replace with a function: js_string_replace ignores js_string_concat_subst's failure, so an
+ *   exception the replacement function throws (a node's error, the heap running out, the engine refusing a C
+ *   re-entry) is dropped and replace returns the string it had built. The engine's own convention is a sticky
+ *   StringBuffer (a failed append sets its value to JS_EXCEPTION, which string_buffer_pop returns), which
+ *   concat_subst's function path forgets: every call reaches rp_mqjs_concat_subst, which calls no function once the
+ *   buffer has failed (replaceAll's later matches) and marks the buffer failed when the upstream body fails, so both
+ *   of replace's paths end in string_buffer_pop returning the exception, pending as it was thrown.
+ * - string_buffer_puts loses an out-of-memory the same way (its JS_NewString fails and the buffer stays good):

+static JSValue rp_mqjs_make_unique_string(JSContext* ctx, JSValue val) {
+    JSString* p;
+    int a, is_numeric, i;
+    JSValueArray* arr;
+    const JSValueArray* arr1;
+    JSValue val1, new_tab;
+    JSGCRef val_ref;
+
+    (void)rp_mqjs_upstream_make_unique_string;
+    if (!JS_IsPtr(val)) return val;
+    p = JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(val);
+    if (p->mtag != JS_MTAG_STRING || p->is_unique) return val;
+
+    /* Found in the ROM tables (the standard library's, a loaded bytecode's) or in the table of names made so far. */
+    for (i = 0; i < ctx->n_rom_atom_tables; i++) {
+        arr1 = ctx->rom_atom_tables[i];
+        if (arr1) {
+            val1 = find_atom(ctx, &a, arr1, arr1->size, val);
+            if (!JS_IsNull(val1)) return val1;
+        }
+    }
+    arr = JS_IsNull(ctx->unique_strings) ? NULL : JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(ctx->unique_strings);
+    val1 = find_atom(ctx, &a, arr, ctx->unique_strings_len, val);
+    if (!JS_IsNull(val1)) return val1;
+
+    JS_PUSH_VALUE(ctx, val);
+    is_numeric = js_is_numeric_string(ctx, val);
+    JS_POP_VALUE(ctx, val);
+    if (is_numeric < 0) return JS_EXCEPTION;
+
+    /* Not found: inserted. When the table is full its growth allocates, and a collection there would drop the names
+     * that died under the insertion; so collect first, which drops them now, and the growth's own collection, if it
+     * comes, finds every entry alive. The place is found after, in the table as the collection left it. The sweep
+     * shrinks the table to its live length after every collection, so the first new name after any collection finds
+     * it full: that name pays one more full collection. A node that makes names at event rate (a message's own
+     * property name) pays nothing measurable; one that makes a new name every block pays a collection a block. */
+    if (JS_IsNull(ctx->unique_strings) ||
+        ((JSValueArray*)JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(ctx->unique_strings))->size <= ctx->unique_strings_len) {
+        JS_PUSH_VALUE(ctx, val);
+        JS_GC(ctx);
+        JS_POP_VALUE(ctx, val);
+    }
+    arr = JS_IsNull(ctx->unique_strings) ? NULL : JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(ctx->unique_strings);
+    find_atom(ctx, &a, arr, ctx->unique_strings_len, val);
+
+    JS_PUSH_VALUE(ctx, val);
+    new_tab = js_resize_value_array(ctx, ctx->unique_strings, ctx->unique_strings_len + 1);
+    JS_POP_VALUE(ctx, val);
+    if (JS_IsException(new_tab)) return JS_EXCEPTION;
+    ctx->unique_strings = new_tab;
+    arr = JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(ctx->unique_strings);
+    memmove(&arr->arr[a + 1], &arr->arr[a], sizeof(arr->arr[0]) * (ctx->unique_strings_len - a));
+    arr->arr[a] = val;
+    p = JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(val);
+    p->is_unique = TRUE;
+    p->is_numeric = is_numeric;
+    ctx->unique_strings_len++;
+    return val;
+}
+
 void rp_mqjs_memory_of(JSContext* ctx, rp_mqjs_memory* out) {
     out->fixed = (size_t)(ctx->heap_base - (uint8_t*)ctx);
     out->heap = (size_t)(ctx->heap_free - ctx->heap_base);
     out->stack = (size_t)(ctx->stack_top - (uint8_t*)ctx->sp);
     out->free_bytes = (size_t)((uint8_t*)ctx->sp - ctx->heap_free);

+
+void rp_mqjs_keep_bytecode_names(uint8_t* bytecode, uint32_t size) {
+    uint8_t* ptr = bytecode + sizeof(JSBytecodeHeader);
+    uint8_t* end = bytecode + size;
+    while (ptr < end) {
+        JSMemBlockHeader* mb = (JSMemBlockHeader*)ptr;
+        if (mb->mtag == JS_MTAG_STRING) mb->gc_mark = 1;
+        ptr += get_mblock_size(ptr);
+    }
+}
+
+/* The host's reads and writes of its own arrays and byte views, in place: what a warmed block runs a message through
+ * (rp_mqjs.h says why each exists). None allocates, so none collects. */
+
+JSValue rp_mqjs_array_get(JSContext* ctx, JSValue v, uint32_t i) {
+    if (JS_IsPtr(v)) {
+        JSObject* p = JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(v);
+        if (p->mtag == JS_MTAG_OBJECT && p->class_id == JS_CLASS_ARRAY && i < p->u.array.len) {
+            const JSValueArray* tab = JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(p->u.array.tab);
+            return tab->arr[i];
+        }
+    }
+    return JS_GetPropertyUint32(ctx, v, i);
+}
+
+int rp_mqjs_array_put(JSContext* ctx, JSValue v, uint32_t i, JSValue item) {
+    if (JS_IsPtr(v)) {
+        JSObject* p = JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(v);
+        if (p->mtag == JS_MTAG_OBJECT && p->class_id == JS_CLASS_ARRAY && i < p->u.array.len) {
+            JSValueArray* tab = JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(p->u.array.tab);
+            tab->arr[i] = item;
+            return 0;
+        }
+    }
+    return JS_IsException(JS_SetPropertyUint32(ctx, v, i, item)) ? -1 : 0;
+}
+
+uint8_t* rp_mqjs_bytes(JSContext* ctx, JSValue v, uint32_t* length) {
+    (void)ctx;
+    if (!JS_IsPtr(v)) return NULL;
+    JSObject* p = JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(v);
+    if (p->mtag != JS_MTAG_OBJECT || (p->class_id != JS_CLASS_UINT8_ARRAY && p->class_id != JS_CLASS_UINT8C_ARRAY))
+        return NULL;

+int rp_mqjs_is_fixed(JSContext* ctx, JSValue v) { return JS_IsPtr(v) && JS_IS_ROM_PTR(ctx, JS_VALUE_TO_PTR(v)); }
+
+/* The three wrappers the header comment describes. */
+
+static int rp_mqjs_concat_subst(JSContext* ctx, void* buffer, JSValue* str, JSValue* rep, uint32_t pos,
+                                uint32_t end_of_match, JSValue* capture_buf, uint32_t captures_len, JSValue* needle) {

+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+static int rp_mqjs_buffer_puts(JSContext* ctx, void* buffer, const char* str) {
+    StringBuffer* b = buffer;
+    if (rp_mqjs_upstream_buffer_puts(ctx, b, str) < 0) {
+        b->buffer_ref.val = JS_EXCEPTION;
+        return -1;
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
+
+JSValue rp_mqjs_js_object_hasOwnProperty(JSContext* ctx, JSValue* this_val, int argc, JSValue* argv) {
+    if (JS_IsObject(ctx, *this_val)) {

+        if (JS_IsException(key)) return JS_EXCEPTION;
+        argv[0] = key;
+    }
+    return rp_mqjs_upstream_object_hasOwnProperty(ctx, this_val, argc, argv);

+void rp_mqjs_limit_reentries(JSContext* ctx, int calls) {
+    if (calls < 1) calls = 1;
+    if (calls > JS_MAX_CALL_RECURSE) calls = JS_MAX_CALL_RECURSE;
+    ctx->js_call_rec_count = JS_MAX_CALL_RECURSE - calls;
+}

+/* The host's buffers and views, made by the engine's own constructors (rp_mqjs.h): with no JS_Call, so at any depth
+ * of the C re-entries, and with no global looked up by name. The typed array's constructor reads its arguments before
+ * it allocates, and roots the buffer it keeps across its allocation, so arguments in a C array are safe: given as short
+ * integers, which make nothing (a number past JS_SHORTINT_MAX, 2^30 - 1, would be a boxed float, made on the heap,
+ * which could move the buffer held in the array before the constructor reads it). A length or an offset past that is
+ * refused; the host's are a queue's, of 4096 bytes and 2^20 messages at most. */
+
+JSValue rp_mqjs_new_array_buffer(JSContext* ctx, uint32_t bytes) { return js_array_buffer_alloc(ctx, bytes); }
+
+JSValue rp_mqjs_new_uint8_array(JSContext* ctx, uint32_t length) {
+    if (length > JS_SHORTINT_MAX) return JS_ThrowRangeError(ctx, "invalid length");
+    JSValue arg = JS_NewShortInt((int32_t)length);
+    return js_typed_array_constructor(ctx, NULL, 1 | FRAME_CF_CTOR, &arg, JS_CLASS_UINT8_ARRAY);
+}
+
+JSValue rp_mqjs_new_uint8_view(JSContext* ctx, JSValue buffer, uint32_t offset, uint32_t length) {
+    if (offset > JS_SHORTINT_MAX || length > JS_SHORTINT_MAX) return JS_ThrowRangeError(ctx, "invalid length");
+    JSValue args[3] = {buffer, JS_NewShortInt((int32_t)offset), JS_NewShortInt((int32_t)length)};
+    return js_typed_array_constructor(ctx, NULL, 3 | FRAME_CF_CTOR, args, JS_CLASS_UINT8_ARRAY);
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The host: the target's width, the device runtime, `idle`, `forward`, the cap and the deadline**

`rp_node.h`'s `rp_package_memory` gains `query_target`, and the exporter sizes a pack's memory at the target's width
(`sizePlan(..., targetPointerBytes)`, `blob::kTargetPointerBytes` = 4) while nodes and structures keep E3's 64-bit
upper bound, so `<symbol>ArenaEstimate` stays an upper bound on the box's figure; its trial load runs at its own
width. `rp_device_midi_in.h`: `RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES` is 64 (the bytes stay 4096). `MqjsHost`: `kDeviceHalves` (a
64-bit device build gives 3/2 of `heapBytes`, a 32-bit one exactly), `desktopContextBytes()` (at least 1 MiB, four
times `heapBytes` past it), `kBoxStateBytes` (448, which a 32-bit build reserves under a `static_assert`) and
`boxPackageBytes()`; `rp_mqjs_pack.h`'s source carries the device runtime as `bytecode` and the whole pack as
`control_bytecode` (64-bit only), with `box_bytecode_size` and the bytecode's placement (`.flashdata` on a device, so
`copy_to_ram` leaves it in flash; setup copies and relocates it). The warm path reads the host's arrays in place,
finds a port a bytecode constant names by its value and skips a ready port's pool; `forward(port, message)` reads a
handed-out message natively, and `sendData` reads its data through a slot the collector updates; `idle: "skip"`
returns before the context on a block that brings nothing, never on a block of another `rp_process`; a node's context
is capped at `RP_MQJS_MAX_REENTRIES` (4) re-entries after its load; and on a host's clock a block's entry gets
`kHostClockMessageMicros` (250 us) more for each message on its events and bytes inputs. The QuickJS host
(`ScriptHost`) honours `idle` and `forward` too. The runner (`mqjs-run/main.cpp`) takes the runtime with `--control
<whole>`, fills inputs at the device MIDI input's capacity (64 / 4096) in a five-block cycle (64 notes, 64 SysEx of 64
bytes, two sweeps of every first byte, an empty block), prints `digest=`, and gains `--least no` and `--deadline-us`;
`PackageMemory` allocates the desktop's large contexts with `calloc`.

- [ ] **Step 5: The SDK and the toolchain: the device runtime bundle, `idle` and `forward`**

`defineNode.ts`: under `RP_DEVICE_RUNTIME` a definition keeps `{id, ports, create, layout, idle}` (the trimmed SDK;
`parseSettings` and `descriptor` throw), `orderedLayout` shared with `buildLayout` (it keeps `exclusive`), `idle:
"skip"` refused with an audio port or with nothing to wake it, and the Block type gains `forward`. The toolchain
bundles the entry a second time as the device runtime (`minifySyntax`), lowers and scans it, compiles it at 64 bits
and with `-m32` (`<name>.device.js` kept for a fault's line), runs both bundles through the same blocks on the runner
and refuses a pack whose output digests or default layouts differ, prints the 3/2 check ("the check would pass X"),
and writes `pack64.c` (both bundles) and `pack32.c` (the runtime), each run in a work dir of its own and its outputs
written by rename. `cmake/packages.cmake`'s `_retroplug_device_script_targets` registers a pack in a device build from
the desktop build's `pack32.c` when `RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR` is set (without it a device build takes native entries
alone, so the device check builds unchanged). The exporter's list gains `bliptoaster`, and
`retroplug-export-plan-current` also builds the packs' 32-bit sources and the 32-bit tables, what a device image takes
from the desktop build. devtest's `heapBytes` is 57344, the desktop tests' figure behind 256-place queues (its
manifest's description says so).

- [ ] **Step 6: The `bliptoaster` pack**

`packages/bliptoaster/package.json` (`@retroplug/bliptoaster`): `"script": { "entry": "ts/index.ts", "device": true,
"heapBytes": 24576 }` and no native member. `ts/index.ts` defines the policy: its test inlined in the loop over
`b.messages("in")`, each kept message passed on with `b.forward("out", m)`. The root `CMakeLists.txt` adds
`retroplug_package(bliptoaster)` and appends it to `RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES`, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` gains the member's
importer: its diff is applied as it stands, never regenerated, and checked by a frozen install. The retroplug
`tsconfig.json` type-checks `../bliptoaster/ts`.

Create `packages/bliptoaster/package.json`:

````json
{
  "name": "@retroplug/bliptoaster",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "description": "The BlipToaster cart's MIDI policy as a device script pack: rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy, which passes the box's MIDI on to the cart less what the ROM's FIFO is not fed.",
  "retroplug": {
    "script": { "entry": "ts/index.ts", "device": true, "heapBytes": 24576 }
  }
}
````

Create `packages/bliptoaster/ts/index.ts`:

````ts
// The bliptoaster script pack (packages/bliptoaster/package.json's retroplug.script,
// docs/modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md section 6): the BlipToaster cart's MIDI policy, a device pack the box's
// built-in plan runs between its MIDI input and the cart (pico/n8-host/plan.json), and the desktop products list so it
// can be auditioned there. The device-pack toolchain (packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs) compiles it to
// MicroQuickJS bytecode, at 64 bits for the desktop's host and at 32 for the box's.
import { defineNode, events } from "../../retroplug/src/graph/defineNode";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../retroplug/src/script/register";

// What BlipToaster's FIFO is not fed: polyphonic and channel aftertouch (high-rate streams a controller floods and no
// ROM here reads), the system common messages but a SysEx (F1 to F6) and the real-time ones (F8 to FF), which the
// bridge never forwarded. Every other message passes as it came, its frame, flags and bytes, in order: a SysEx (F0,
// or a lone F7), and a message of no kind (one whose first byte is a data byte, or an empty one), as
// rp.core.midi-filter passes them. A status is read from the message's first byte alone, with no running status
// carried across messages, which is rp.core.midi-filter's reading too: this node drops exactly what that filter drops
// with `drop: ["polyAftertouch", "channelAftertouch", "systemCommon", "realtime"]`, message for message. The test is
// written out in the loop rather than called, as a call is a frame of the interpreter's for every message.

// The policy has no settings. Its output is sized as its input's queue (capacity.match), so a stream it passes whole
// is never one it drops. Each message's first byte is read once, and what passes goes on through forward, which the
// host makes (its frame, flags and bytes as they came, copied at the call), so a warmed block allocates nothing for a
// message of up to three bytes, at either width. It keeps nothing between blocks and sends only what a block brought
// it, so the host skips it on a block with no message (idle: "skip"), the box's every pass between two.
export const midiPolicyNode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy",
  name: "BlipToaster MIDI policy",
  category: "bliptoaster",
  idle: "skip",
  ports: { in: events.in(), out: events.out({ match: "in" }) },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const messages = b.messages("in");
      const count = messages.length;
      for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const m = messages[i];
        // The first byte; undefined for an empty message, which then matches no kind below and passes.
        const status = m.data[0];
        const high = status & 0xf0;
        if (high === 0xa0 || high === 0xd0 || (status > 0xf0 && status < 0xf7) || status >= 0xf8) continue;
        b.forward("out", m);
      }
    },
  }),
});

registerScriptNodes([midiPolicyNode]);
````

- [ ] **Step 7: The box runs the policy**

`pico/host`: `DeviceHost` offers `rp.host.clock/1` (`time_us_64`, the box's 10 ms and 250 us a message); `BuiltInPlan`
prints the pack line (`[host] pack bliptoaster, <bytes> bytes`), times the load and the first block and prints the
heap line after it (`[host] pack bliptoaster: heap <X> of 24576 bytes in use after the first block; the load took <us>
us and the first block <us> us`), and prints a script fault's words on a second `[host]` line, cut to 159 bytes;
`MidiStaging` asserts the 64 messages. `pico/n8-host`: `plan.json` is `rp.device.midi-in` ->
`rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy` -> `rp.n8.nes`; `plan.cmake` gives the packages `core device-io n8 bliptoaster` and the
arena 65536; `CMakeLists.txt` derives `RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR` from `RP_EXPORT_PLAN_TOOL`, adds the pack, sets
`RP_MQJS_MAX_PACKS=1 RP_MQJS_MAX_TYPES=1` and `PICO_USE_STACK_GUARDS=1` (core 0's `MSPLIM`, so an overrun is a
HardFault the watchdog restarts rather than a write into SCRATCH_X), and says what the image takes; `BoxCartLink`
keeps its 512 messages (after a reconnect `rp.n8.nes` pays owed note-offs first); `main.cpp` offers the clock;
`loop.sh`'s staleness guard also covers the script packs' TypeScript, the SDK's, the toolchain and the engine.
`[stats]` and every line a gate script matches are unchanged, `filtered` included: the policy's drops are the
filter's.
