````cpp
namespace {

using namespace rp::graph;

constexpr const char* kDrop = R"({"drop":["polyAftertouch","channelAftertouch","systemCommon","realtime"]})";
constexpr std::uint32_t kCapacity = RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES;
constexpr std::uint32_t kBytes = RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES;

std::string readFile(const std::string& path) {
    std::ifstream in(path, std::ios::binary);
    return std::string((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
}

const rp_node_type* typeOf(const rp_package* p, std::string_view id) {
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < p->node_type_count; ++i)
        if (id == p->node_types[i]->id) return p->node_types[i];
    return nullptr;
}

void ignoreLog(void*, int, const char*) {}

// What a script node is made under: its pack's memory (rp.host.packages/1), nothing else. Declared before the nodes.
struct Host {
    PackageMemory packages;
    rp_host       host{RP_ABI_VERSION, this, nullptr, nullptr, &ignoreLog, &Host::interfaceOf};
    static const void* interfaceOf(const rp_host* h, const char* id) {
        auto* self = static_cast<Host*>(h->ctx);
        return std::strcmp(id, RP_HOST_PACKAGES_INTERFACE) == 0 ? self->packages.service() : nullptr;
    }
};

struct Message {
    std::uint32_t             frame = 0;
    std::uint32_t             flags = 0;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes;
    bool operator==(const Message&) const = default;
};

// One events-in, events-out node made by hand from msgpack settings, its queues at the box's capacity (or another),
// run a block at a time as an executor runs it.
struct Node {
    const rp_node_type*           type = nullptr;
    std::vector<std::max_align_t> memory;
    rp_node*                      node = nullptr;
    std::vector<rp_message>       inItems, outItems;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t>     inBytes = std::vector<std::uint8_t>(kBytes), outBytes = inBytes;
    rp_queue                      in{}, out{};
    rp_port_view                  views[2]{};
    rp_transport                  transport{48000.0, 120.0, 0.0, 0};
    rp_process                    step{};

    Node(const rp_node_type* t, const rp_host* host, const char* json, std::uint32_t capacity = kCapacity)
        : type(t), inItems(capacity), outItems(capacity) {
        in = rp_queue{inItems.data(), 0, capacity, inBytes.data(), 0, kBytes, 0};
        out = rp_queue{outItems.data(), 0, capacity, outBytes.data(), 0, kBytes, 0};
        REQUIRE(type);
        const auto settings = settingsToMsgpack(json);
        REQUIRE(settings);
        const rp_settings s{reinterpret_cast<const char*>(settings->data()), settings->size(), RP_SETTINGS_MSGPACK};
        rp_memory_req req{};
        rp_error      err{};
        REQUIRE(type->query_memory(type, &s, &req, &err));
        memory.resize(req.size / sizeof(std::max_align_t) + 1);
        node = type->create(type, host, memory.data(), &s, &err);
        INFO(err.message);
        REQUIRE(node);
        REQUIRE(node->vt->activate(node, 48000.0, 256, &err));
        views[0].kind = RP_PORT_EVENTS;
        views[0].u.queue = &in;
        views[1].kind = RP_PORT_EVENTS;
        views[1].u.queue = &out;
        const std::uint8_t connected = 1;
        node->vt->ports_changed(node, &connected, 1);
    }
    ~Node() { type->destroy(node); }
    Node(const Node&) = delete;
    Node& operator=(const Node&) = delete;

    // One block over `messages`, its output.
    std::vector<Message> run(const std::vector<Message>& messages) {
        clearQueue(in);
        clearQueue(out);
        for (const Message& m : messages) REQUIRE(pushMessage(in, m.frame, m.bytes, m.flags));
        step = rp_process{256, &transport, &views[0], 1, &views[1], 1, nullptr, 0};  // the same step every block
        REQUIRE(node->vt->process(node, &step) == RP_OK);
        std::vector<Message> got;
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < out.count; ++i) {
            const auto data = messageData(out, out.items[i]);
            got.push_back({out.items[i].frame, out.items[i].flags, {data.begin(), data.end()}});
        }
        return got;
    }
};

// What a parser makes of a first byte: a channel message is three bytes (two for a program change and channel
// pressure), a SysEx five (F0 .. F7), F1 and F3 two, F2 three, a lone F7 and the rest of system common and real time
// one; a data byte leads a three-byte message of no kind.
std::vector<std::uint8_t> messageFor(std::uint8_t first, std::uint8_t a, std::uint8_t b) {
    if (first < 0x80) return {first, a, b};
    if (first < 0xF0) {
        if ((first & 0xF0) == 0xC0 || (first & 0xF0) == 0xD0) return {first, a};
        return {first, a, b};
    }
    if (first == 0xF0) return {0xF0, 0x7D, a, b, 0xF7};
    if (first == 0xF1 || first == 0xF3) return {first, a};
    if (first == 0xF2) return {first, a, b};
    return {first};
}

// The stream: every first byte once, and an empty message, in blocks of the queue's capacity, frames rising with a tie
// every fourth and the flags moving; then `seeded` blocks of first bytes drawn at random.
std::vector<std::vector<Message>> stream(std::uint32_t seeded) {
    std::vector<Message> all;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < 256; ++i)
        all.push_back({0, i % 3 == 0 ? 0u : i, messageFor(static_cast<std::uint8_t>(i), i & 0x7f, (i * 7) & 0x7f)});
    all.insert(all.begin() + 100, Message{0, 5, {}});
    std::vector<std::vector<Message>> blocks;
    for (std::size_t at = 0; at < all.size(); at += kCapacity) {
        std::vector<Message> block(all.begin() + at, all.begin() + std::min<std::size_t>(at + kCapacity, all.size()));
        for (std::size_t k = 0; k < block.size(); ++k) block[k].frame = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(k - k / 4);
        blocks.push_back(std::move(block));
    }
    std::uint32_t state = 0x2545F491u;
    auto next = [&] {
        state ^= state << 13;
        state ^= state >> 17;
        state ^= state << 5;
        return state;
    };
    for (std::uint32_t b = 0; b < seeded; ++b) {
        std::vector<Message> block;
        std::uint32_t        frame = 0;
        for (std::uint32_t k = next() % (kCapacity + 1); k > 0 && frame < 256; --k, frame += next() % 3) {
            const auto first = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(next());
            block.push_back({frame, next() % 4, messageFor(first, next() & 0x7f, next() & 0x7f)});
        }
        blocks.push_back(std::move(block));
    }
    return blocks;
}

}  // namespace

TEST_CASE("rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy drops what rp.core.midi-filter drops with BlipToaster's list, message for "
          "message",
          "[device-mode][script-pack][bliptoaster]") {
    struct Pair {
        const char*       name;
        const rp_package* policy;
        const rp_package* filter;
    };
    const Pair pairs[] = {{"desktop", rp_bliptoaster_script_package(), rp_core_package()},
                          {"device", rp_bliptoaster_script_package_device_mode(), rp_core_package_device_mode()}};
    const auto blocks = stream(400);
    std::vector<std::vector<Message>> heard[2];
    for (std::size_t p = 0; p < 2; ++p) {
        INFO(pairs[p].name);
        REQUIRE(pairs[p].policy);
        Host host;
        Node policy(typeOf(pairs[p].policy, "rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy"), &host.host, "{}");
        Node filter(typeOf(pairs[p].filter, "rp.core.midi-filter"), &host.host, kDrop);
        std::size_t passed = 0, dropped = 0;
        for (std::size_t b = 0; b < blocks.size(); ++b) {
            INFO("block " << b);
            const auto mine = policy.run(blocks[b]);
            const auto theirs = filter.run(blocks[b]);
            REQUIRE(mine == theirs);
            heard[p].push_back(mine);
            passed += mine.size();
            dropped += blocks[b].size() - mine.size();
        }
        // The first blocks hold every first byte once: what goes is 0xA0 to 0xAF, 0xD0 to 0xDF, 0xF1 to 0xF6 and 0xF8
        // to 0xFF, 46 of the 257 (the empty message among those that stay).
        std::size_t firstDropped = 0;
        for (std::size_t b = 0; b * kCapacity < 257; ++b) {
            const auto mine = policy.run(blocks[b]);
            firstDropped += blocks[b].size() - mine.size();
        }
        CHECK(firstDropped == 16 + 16 + 6 + 8);
        CHECK(passed > dropped);
        CHECK(dropped > 0);
    }
    // Both builds of the policy heard the same.
    CHECK(heard[0] == heard[1]);
}

TEST_CASE("rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy's descriptor is its golden", "[device-mode][script-pack][bliptoaster]") {
    const rp_package* pack = rp_bliptoaster_script_package();
    REQUIRE(pack);
    CHECK(std::string(pack->manifest_json) == R"({"id":"rp.bliptoaster.script","version":"1.0.0"})");
    REQUIRE(pack->node_type_count == 1);
    const rp_node_type* type = pack->node_types[0];
    CHECK(std::string(type->id) == "rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy");
    const std::string json = type->descriptor(type);
    const std::string path =
        std::string(RP_DEVICE_MODE_GOLDEN_DIR) + "/rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy.descriptor.json";
    if (std::getenv("RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE")) std::ofstream(path) << json << "\n";
    CHECK(json + "\n" == readFile(path));
    // The same port layout as the filter's, which it stands in for on the box: events in, an output that matches it.
    CHECK(json.find(R"("ports":[{"id":"in","dir":"in","kind":"events"},{"id":"out","dir":"out","kind":"events",)"
                    R"("capacity":{"match":"in"}}],"params":[])") != std::string::npos);
}

TEST_CASE("the bliptoaster pack's heap holds its policy behind the box's input, full every block",
          "[device-mode][script-pack][bliptoaster]") {
    for (const rp_package* pack : {rp_bliptoaster_script_package(), rp_bliptoaster_script_package_device_mode()}) {
        INFO((pack == rp_bliptoaster_script_package() ? "desktop" : "device"));
        Host host;
        Node policy(typeOf(pack, "rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy"), &host.host, "{}");
        rp_script_heap_use use{};
        for (std::uint32_t b = 0; b < 64; ++b) {
            std::vector<Message> block;
            if (b % 2 == 0) {
                for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < kCapacity; ++k)
                    block.push_back({k * 256 / kCapacity, 0, {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k % 2 ? 0x80 : 0x90),
                                                             static_cast<std::uint8_t>(48 + (b + k) % 24), 100}});
            } else {
                for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < kBytes / 64; ++k) {
                    std::vector<std::uint8_t> sysex(64, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k & 0x7f));
                    sysex.front() = 0xF0;
                    sysex.back() = 0xF7;
                    block.push_back({k * 4, 0, sysex});
                }
            }
            CHECK(policy.run(block).size() == block.size());
        }
        const auto* heap =
            static_cast<const rp_script_heap*>(policy.node->vt->get_interface(policy.node, RP_SCRIPT_HEAP_INTERFACE));
        REQUIRE(heap);
        REQUIRE(heap->use(policy.node, true, &use));
        const std::uint32_t declared = rp_script_bliptoaster.heap_bytes;
        INFO("bliptoaster's heap at 64 bits after 64 full blocks: " << use.fixed + use.heap << " live of "
                                                                    << use.bytes << " (declared " << declared
                                                                    << ", the box's)");
        // The device's build gives the context the toolchain check's 3/2 of the box's figure (kDeviceHalves), and
        // what the policy holds after full blocks fits it; the desktop's gives it far more (desktopContextBytes()).
        const std::size_t checked = std::size_t{declared} * rp::mqjs::kDeviceHalves / 2;
        CHECK(use.bytes >= checked);
        CHECK(use.fixed + use.heap < checked);
    }
}

TEST_CASE("on the desktop, the policy behind a 256-place source runs through re-plans that hold two of it",
          "[device-mode][script-pack][bliptoaster]") {
    // Re-plans on a GraphHost, the policy behind rp.devtest.source's events (the planner's default 256 places): a new
    // id each time, so a new instance, made at its first block. This thread stands in for the audio thread (the host
    // owned by it), so a replaced plan is handed back at the block that adopts the next and kept until reclaim(),
    // after the round's blocks: the old instance and its pools stay in the pack's heap beside the new one's for those
    // blocks, as on a desktop host whose control thread reclaims later.
    NodeRegistry registry;
    for (const rp_package* p : {rp_devtest_plan_package(), rp_bliptoaster_script_package()}) {
        std::string why;
        INFO(why);
        REQUIRE(registry.addPackage(p, &why));
    }
    ResourceTable resources;
    GraphHost     graph(registry, resources, HostConfig{48000.0, 256, Target::Desktop});
    const rp_transport transport{48000.0, 120.0, 0.0, 0};
    graph.setAudioThreadOwns(true);
    std::size_t reclaimed = 0;
    for (int round = 0; round < 8; ++round) {
        const std::string id = "policy" + std::to_string(round);
        REQUIRE(graph.setGraph(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"src","type":"rp.devtest.source"},{"id":")" + id +
                               R"(","type":"rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy"}],"wires":[{"from":"src.events","to":")" + id +
                               R"(.in"}]})")
                    .ok);
        for (int b = 0; b < 4; ++b) graph.processBlock(256, transport);
        reclaimed += graph.reclaim();
    }
    graph.setAudioThreadOwns(false);
    CHECK(reclaimed >= 7);  // each replaced plan was held to the round's end
    CHECK(graph.faultCount() == 0);

    // The same two instances by hand, in one host's pack memory, behind full 256-place queues of notes and of SysEx:
    // more than a context sized for the box's 64 places would hold, at the desktop's factors.
    Host host;
    Node first(typeOf(rp_bliptoaster_script_package(), "rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy"), &host.host, "{}", 256);
    Node second(typeOf(rp_bliptoaster_script_package(), "rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy"), &host.host, "{}", 256);
    std::size_t most = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t b = 0; b < 16; ++b) {
        std::vector<Message> block;
        if (b % 2 == 0) {
            for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < 256; ++k)
                block.push_back({k, 0, {0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(48 + (b + k) % 24), 100}});
        } else {
            for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < kBytes / 16; ++k) {
                std::vector<std::uint8_t> sysex(16, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k & 0x7f));
                sysex.front() = 0xF0;
                sysex.back() = 0xF7;
                block.push_back({k, 0, sysex});
            }
        }
        CHECK(first.run(block).size() == block.size());
        CHECK(second.run(block).size() == block.size());
        const auto* heap =
            static_cast<const rp_script_heap*>(first.node->vt->get_interface(first.node, RP_SCRIPT_HEAP_INTERFACE));
        rp_script_heap_use use{};
        REQUIRE(heap);
        REQUIRE(heap->use(first.node, true, &use));
        most = std::max(most, use.fixed + use.heap);
    }
    INFO("the pack's heap held at most " << most << " bytes, of "
                                          << rp::mqjs::desktopContextBytes(rp_script_bliptoaster));
    CHECK(most > std::size_t{rp_script_bliptoaster.heap_bytes} * rp::mqjs::kWidthFactor * rp::mqjs::kDesktopHeapFactor);
}
````

````ts
// A device pack whose node does one thing in the full bundle and another in the device's runtime of the pack (the
// box's bundle, built with RP_DEVICE_RUNTIME: graph/defineNode.ts): the device-pack toolchain runs both through the
// same blocks and must refuse it, saying the two outputs differ (test/graph/device-pack.test.ts).
import { defineNode, events } from "../../../src/graph/defineNode";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "../../../src/script/register";

declare const RP_DEVICE_RUNTIME: boolean | undefined;

export const differs = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.device.differs",
  ports: { out: events.out() },
  create: () => {
    const note = new Uint8Array([0x90, typeof RP_DEVICE_RUNTIME === "undefined" ? 60 : 61, 100]);
    return {
      process(b) {
        b.send("out", 0, note);
      },
    };
  },
});

registerScriptNodes([differs]);
````

````ts
    out: events.out({ messages: typeof RP_DEVICE_RUNTIME === "undefined" ? 64 : 32 }),

});

registerScriptNodes([layoutDiffers]);
````

````diff
+TEST_CASE("a node the host skips when idle runs only on a block that brings it something, and forward sends a message "
+          "as send would",
+          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
+    // in, level; out, made, calls; the param p.
+    const std::vector<PortSpec> ports = {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, false}, {RP_PORT_CONTROL, false}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true},
+                                         {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true},  {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}};
+    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
+        INFO(b.name);
+        Host host;
+        Made n(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.skipper"), host, {}, ports, {0.0});
+        REQUIRE(n.node);
+        // What a block's call said its count was, or 0 when it was not called.
+        auto calls = [&]() -> int {
+            const std::vector<Sent> sent = n.sent(2);
+            return sent.empty() ? 0 : sent[0].bytes.at(0);
+        };
+        // Its first block runs, though it brings nothing; then such a block is not run at all.
+        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+        CHECK(calls() == 1);
+        for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
+            REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+            CHECK(calls() == 0);
+        }
+        // A message runs it. Each goes on as it came, but for the velocity the node wrote into a note-on's data before
+        // forwarding it; and an object the node made goes on as send would send its fields.
+        push(n.in(0), 5, {0x90, 60, 100}, 1);
+        push(n.in(0), 9, {0xF8});
+        push(n.in(0), 9, {});
+        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+        CHECK(calls() == 2);
+        CHECK(n.sent(0) == std::vector<Sent>{{5, 1, {0x90, 60, 1}}, {9, 0, {0xF8}}, {9, 0, {}}});
+        CHECK(n.sent(1) == std::vector<Sent>{{6, 1, {0x90}}, {10, 1, {0xF8}}, {10, 1, {0}}});
+        clearQueue(n.in(0));
+        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+        CHECK(calls() == 0);
+        // A change on a control input runs it, and one on a param.
+        REQUIRE(pushControl(n.control(1), 10, 0.5));
+        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+        CHECK(calls() == 3);
+        n.control(1).count = 0;
+        REQUIRE(pushControl(*n.params[0], 0, 0.25));
+        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+        CHECK(calls() == 4);
+        n.params[0]->count = 0;
+        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+        CHECK(calls() == 0);
+        // A re-activation's hook waits for its next call, which an idle block then makes.
+        rp_error err{};
+        REQUIRE(n.node->vt->activate(n.node, 44100.0, 256, &err));
+        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+        CHECK(calls() == 5);
+        REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+        CHECK(calls() == 0);
+        // A new plan's step (another rp_process) whose level starts elsewhere with no change, as a rewired or
+        // disconnected input does: its first block there runs, and reads the start; the next is skipped again.
+        n.control(1).start = 0.4;
+        REQUIRE(n.run(256, 1) == RP_OK);
+        REQUIRE(n.sent(2).size() == 1);
+        CHECK(n.sent(2)[0].bytes == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{6, 40});
+        REQUIRE(n.run(256, 1) == RP_OK);
+        CHECK(calls() == 0);
+        // On the desktop, a settings swap (the same layout, so the instance is kept) waits for the next call, which an
+        // idle block then makes.
+        if (b.name == std::string("desktop")) {
+            const rp_settings none{nullptr, 0, RP_SETTINGS_JSON};
+            void*             prepared = nullptr;
+            void*             old = nullptr;
+            REQUIRE(n.node->vt->prepare_settings(n.node, &none, &prepared, &err) == RP_PREPARE_SWAP);
+            n.node->vt->commit_settings(n.node, prepared, &old);
+            n.node->vt->release_settings(n.node, old);
+            REQUIRE(n.run(256, 1) == RP_OK);
+            CHECK(calls() == 7);
+            REQUIRE(n.run(256, 1) == RP_OK);
+            CHECK(calls() == 0);
+        }
+        CHECK(n.fault().empty());
+    }
+}

+TEST_CASE("by a host's clock, a block's deadline grows by kHostClockMessageMicros for each message it hands the node",
+          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
+    // The host's clock, once the node is made, a millisecond on at each reading: the entry's start and its restart once
+    // the ports are ready are its first two, so a node held to L microseconds faults at the reading past L + 2 ms, the
+    // (L / 1000 + 3)th. Before, the thread's CPU time, as the cases' hosts give it.
+    struct Ticks {
+        bool          live = false;
+        std::uint32_t calls = 0;
+        static std::uint64_t read(void* c) {
+            auto& t = *static_cast<Ticks*>(c);
+            if (!t.live) return cpuMicros(nullptr);
+            return std::uint64_t{++t.calls} * 1000;
+        }
+    };
+    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
+        // None, then 40 on the events input and one on the bytes input: each counts.
+        for (const std::uint32_t events : {0u, 40u}) {
+            const std::uint32_t messages = events ? events + 1 : 0;
+            INFO(b.name << ", " << messages << " messages");
+            Ticks clock;
+            Host  host(20000);
+            host.clock.ctx = &clock;
+            host.clock.micros = &Ticks::read;
+            Made n(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.spins-in"), host, {},
+                   {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, false}, {RP_PORT_BYTES, false}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}});
+            REQUIRE(n.node);
+            for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < events; ++k) {
+                const std::uint8_t note[3] = {0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k), 100};
+                REQUIRE(pushMessage(n.in(0), k, note));
+            }
+            if (events) {
+                const std::uint8_t raw[2] = {0xF8, 0xFA};
+                REQUIRE(pushMessage(n.in(1), 0, raw));
+            }
+            const std::uint32_t limit = 20000 + messages * rp::mqjs::kHostClockMessageMicros;
+            clock.live = true;
+            CHECK(n.run() == RP_FAULT);
+            CHECK(n.faultKind() == RP_SCRIPT_FAULT_DEADLINE);
+            CHECK(n.fault() == "process ran past its deadline of " + std::to_string(limit) + " us");
+            // The interrupt held the node to the lengthened deadline, not the fixed one: it read the clock until then.
+            CHECK(clock.calls == limit / 1000 + 3);
+        }
+    }
+}

+TEST_CASE("a node reads and forwards its messages, SysEx among them, from the deepest call into JavaScript a context "
+          "allows on the C stack",
+          "[device-mode][script-pack]") {
+    for (const Build& b : builds()) {
+        INFO(b.name);
+        Host host;
+        Made n(typeOf(b.scripttest, "rp.scripttest.deep"), host, {},
+               {{RP_PORT_EVENTS, false}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}, {RP_PORT_EVENTS, true}});
+        REQUIRE(n.node);
+        std::vector<Sent> sent;
+        for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < 6; ++k) {
+            std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes = {0x90, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(60 + k), 100};
+            if (k % 2) {  // a SysEx past the three bytes a place keeps a view of: its array is made in the refill
+                bytes.assign(64, static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k));
+                bytes.front() = 0xF0;
+                bytes.back() = 0xF7;
+            }
+            REQUIRE(pushMessage(n.in(0), k * 10, bytes, k % 3 == 0 ? 1u : 0u));
+            sent.push_back({k * 10, k % 3 == 0 ? 1u : 0u, bytes});
+        }
+        for (int block = 0; block < 2; ++block) {
+            REQUIRE(n.run() == RP_OK);
+            INFO(n.fault());
+            CHECK(n.sent(0) == sent);
+            REQUIRE(n.sent(1).size() == 1);
+            // The host's own call into process is the first of the calls on the C stack, each forEach one more.
+            CHECK(n.sent(1)[0].bytes == std::vector<std::uint8_t>{static_cast<std::uint8_t>(rp::mqjs::kMaxReentries)});
+        }
+        CHECK(n.fault().empty());
+    }
+}

+// ---- the engine's two fixes (script/rp_mqjs_engine.c, cmake/mquickjs.cmake's header) --------------------------------
+
+TEST_CASE("a loaded pack's names stay the engine's after a collection: its definitions are found from C",
+          "[device-mode][script-pack][debug-gc]") {
+    // The pack's bytecode loaded as the host loads it, into a context of its own: relocated, its strings kept
+    // (rp_mqjs_keep_bytecode_names), run. Its definitions are under a name of the bytecode's own,
+    // `__rp_scriptNodes`, which the code used as a property name and so made unique where it lies; a collection then
+    // runs, and a lookup from C makes the same name again. Without the strings kept, the collection drops the
+    // bytecode's string from the engine's weak table of names, the lookup makes a second string of that text, and
+    // finds nothing.
+    const rp_mqjs_pack_source& source = rp_script_devtest;
+    std::vector<std::uint64_t> memory((std::size_t{1} << 20) / sizeof(std::uint64_t));
+    std::vector<std::uint64_t> code(source.bytecode_size / sizeof(std::uint64_t) + 1);
+    std::memcpy(code.data(), source.bytecode, source.bytecode_size);
+    auto* bytes = reinterpret_cast<std::uint8_t*>(code.data());
+    JSContext* ctx = JS_NewContext(memory.data(), memory.size() * sizeof(std::uint64_t), &rp_mqjs_stdlib);
+    REQUIRE(ctx);
+    REQUIRE(JS_RelocateBytecode(ctx, bytes, source.bytecode_size) == 0);
+    rp_mqjs_keep_bytecode_names(bytes, source.bytecode_size);
+    const JSValue main = JS_LoadBytecode(ctx, bytes);
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(JS_IsException(main));
+    REQUIRE_FALSE(JS_IsException(JS_Run(ctx, main)));
+    JS_GC(ctx);
+    const JSValue defs = JS_GetPropertyStr(ctx, JS_GetGlobalObject(ctx), "__rp_scriptNodes");
+    CHECK(JS_IsArray(ctx, defs));
+    JS_FreeContext(ctx);
+}
+
+namespace {
+
+// A runner's line for one pack (retroplug-mqjs-run pack: its nodes from the device's runtime, registered from the whole
+// pack), or the run's exit status when it failed.
+std::string runnerLine(const std::string& runner, const std::string& dir, const rp_mqjs_pack_source& source,
+                       std::uint32_t heapBytes, std::uint32_t blocks) {
+    std::string types;
+    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < source.type_count; ++i) types += (i ? "," : "") + std::string(source.type_ids[i]);
+    const std::string name = source.name;
+    const std::string out = dir + "/." + name + ".runner-" + std::to_string(heapBytes) + ".txt";
+    std::string command = "\"" + runner + "\" pack \"" + dir + "/" + name + ".device64.bin\" --control \"" + dir + "/" +
+                          name + ".mqjs64.bin\" --name " + name + " --heap-bytes " + std::to_string(heapBytes) +
+                          " --types " + types + " --blocks " + std::to_string(blocks) +
+                          " --least no --deadline-us 3000000 > \"" + out + "\" 2>&1";
+#ifdef _WIN32
+    command = "\"" + command + "\"";  // cmd /c drops a command line's outer quotes when it starts with one
+#endif
+    const int status = std::system(command.c_str());
+    std::ifstream in(out, std::ios::binary);
+    const std::string text((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
+    std::remove(out.c_str());
+    if (status != 0) return "exit " + std::to_string(status) + ": " + text;
+    const std::size_t at = text.find("ok least=");
+    return at == std::string::npos ? text : text.substr(at);
+}
+
+std::string digestOf(const std::string& line) {
+    const std::size_t at = line.find("digest=");
+    return at == std::string::npos ? line : line.substr(at);
+}
+
+}  // namespace
+
+TEST_CASE("the pack check runs the same in the engine's DEBUG_GC build, a collection at every allocation",
+          "[device-mode][script-pack][debug-gc]") {
+    // retroplug-mqjs-run-gc is the toolchain's runner over the engine built with DEBUG_GC (graph-runtime's CMakeLists):
+    // every allocation collects first, and every collection moves what it keeps. Each pack's check, its nodes run from
+    // the device's runtime over the runner's whole stimulus, must digest to what the ordinary runner's does (the
+    // declared heap's run alone: the debug build's runs are slow). The debug build keeps a block of up to half the
+    // context aside to move the heap's addresses, so it runs at twice the declared heap. A bytecode string dropped from
+    // the weak table of names (the second fix, reverted) fails here at registration, and scripttest's sends node (data
+    // that is no Uint8Array, whose every read can collect) holds the host to reading its data through a slot the
+    // collector updates: a copy of the value, held across those reads, sends what the collector moved away.
+    // Each pack's run: the runner's 16 blocks, scripttest's one cycle of five (a block of each kind, its sends node's
+    // among them), as its many nodes make the debug build's run long. Both runners give a call 3 s by the wall
+    // clock, so a slow build's node (a sanitizer's, under DEBUG_GC) meets the deadline only where an ordinary one does.
+    struct Pack {
+        const rp_mqjs_pack_source* source;
+        std::string                dir;
+        std::uint32_t              blocks;
+    };
+    const std::string build = RP_BUILD_DIR;
+    for (const Pack& p : {Pack{&rp_script_bliptoaster, build + "/packages/bliptoaster/script", 16},
+                          Pack{&rp_script_devtest, build + "/packages/devtest/script", 16},
+                          Pack{&rp_script_hog, build + "/device-mode/script-packs/hog", 16},
+                          Pack{&rp_script_scripttest, build + "/device-mode/script-packs/scripttest", 5}}) {
+        INFO(p.source->name);
+        const std::string plain = runnerLine(RP_MQJS_RUN, p.dir, *p.source, p.source->heap_bytes, p.blocks);
+        const std::string gc = runnerLine(RP_MQJS_RUN_GC, p.dir, *p.source, 2 * p.source->heap_bytes, p.blocks);
+        INFO(plain);
+        INFO(gc);
+        REQUIRE(plain.starts_with("ok least=none"));
+        REQUIRE(gc.starts_with("ok least=none"));
+        CHECK(digestOf(gc) == digestOf(plain));
+    }
+}

+// Skipped when idle, so it sends on `calls` each call how many process calls it has had and its level input's start (in

+// goes on through forward, twice: on `out` as the block handed it out, a note-on's velocity written to 1 in its data

+// frame later and flagged.
+export const skipperNode = defineNode({

+  params: { p: param.float({ name: "P", min: 0, max: 1, default: 0 }) },
+  create: () => {

+    return {

+        calls++;

+        const messages = b.messages("in");

+          b.forward("out", m);

+    };

+// Calls forEach from inside forEach's callback until the engine refuses the next call into JavaScript (the host's
+// limit on a context's C re-entries), reads its block's messages and forwards them from the deepest callback (so the
+// host's refill, a SysEx's array among it, runs there), then sends how deep that was on `depth`. A throw from below the
+// deepest call, or from the work done there, goes on up and faults the node.
+export const deepNode = defineNode({

+  create: () => {

+    let block: Block | null = null;
+    let depth = 0;
+    let reached = 0;
+    let done = false;
+    const down = (): void => {
+      const at = ++depth;

+        reached = 0;
+        done = false;
+        down();
+        block = null;
+        b.send("depth", 0, [reached]);
+      },
+    };
+  },
+});

+TEST_CASE("a script node the host skips when idle runs only on a block that brings it something, and forward sends a "
+          "message as send would",
+          "[script]") {
+    ScriptRig rig(kSkipper);
+    // Two constants, one into the skipper's level and the other into a probe's control; `swapped` crosses them.
+    auto plan = [&](bool swapped) {
+        return doc(node("feed", "rp.test.feed") + "," + node("s", "rp.toy.skipper") + "," +
+                       node("out", "rp.test.probe") + "," + node("made", "rp.test.probe") + "," +
+                       node("calls", "rp.test.probe") + "," + node("k", "rp.core.constant", "", R"({"value":0.5})") +
+                       "," + node("k2", "rp.core.constant", "", R"({"value":0.8})"),
+                   wire("feed.midi", "s.in") + "," + wire("s.out", "out.events") + "," +
+                       wire("s.made", "made.events") + "," + wire("s.calls", "calls.events") + "," +
+                       wire(swapped ? "k2.out" : "k.out", "s.level") + "," +
+                       wire(swapped ? "k.out" : "k2.out", "made.control"));
+    };
+    const auto r = rig.set(plan(false));
+    INFO(ScriptRig::codes(r));
+    REQUIRE(r.ok);
+    auto& feed = rig.node<Feed>("feed");
+    const auto& out = rig.node<Probe>("out");
+    const auto& made = rig.node<Probe>("made");
+    const auto& calls = rig.node<Probe>("calls");
+    auto count = [&]() -> int { return calls.events.empty() ? 0 : calls.events[0].data.at(0); };
+    // Its first block runs, though it brings nothing; then such a block is not run at all.
+    rig.run();
+    CHECK(count() == 1);
+    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
+        rig.run();
+        CHECK(count() == 0);
+    }
+    feed.next[Feed::Midi] = {{5, bytes({0x90, 60, 100}), 1}, {9, bytes({0xf8})}, {9, {}}};
+    rig.run();
+    CHECK(count() == 2);
+    REQUIRE(out.events.size() == 3);
+    CHECK(out.events[0].frame == 5);
+    CHECK(out.events[0].flags == 1);
+    CHECK(out.events[0].data == bytes({0x90, 60, 1}));
+    CHECK(out.events[1].data == bytes({0xf8}));
+    CHECK(out.events[2].data.empty());
+    REQUIRE(made.events.size() == 3);
+    CHECK(made.events[0].frame == 6);
+    CHECK(made.events[0].flags == 1);
+    CHECK(made.events[0].data == bytes({0x90}));
+    CHECK(made.events[2].frame == 10);
+    CHECK(made.events[2].data == bytes({0}));
+    rig.run();
+    CHECK(count() == 0);
+    // A param's change runs it, and a change on its control input.
+    REQUIRE(rig.host->setParam("s", "p", 0.5));
+    rig.run();
+    CHECK(count() == 3);
+    rig.run();
+    CHECK(count() == 0);
+    REQUIRE(rig.host->setParam("k", "value", 0.25, 10));
+    rig.run();
+    CHECK(count() == 4);
+    CHECK(calls.events[0].data.at(1) == 50);  // the change is at frame 10: the start is the last block's end
+    rig.run();
+    CHECK(count() == 0);
+    // A re-plan that keeps it and rewires its level to the other constant, which brings no change: its first block in
+    // the new plan runs, and reads the new start.
+    const auto again = rig.set(plan(true));
+    INFO(ScriptRig::codes(again));
+    REQUIRE(again.ok);
+    rig.run();
+    CHECK(count() == 5);
+    CHECK(calls.events[0].data.at(1) == 80);
+    rig.run();
+    CHECK(count() == 0);
+    CHECK(rig.scripts.throwCount() == 0);
+}
````

**The hash guard refuses a changed upstream span.** One word of a comment inside `JS_MakeUniqueString` changes, so the
span's text, and with it its hash, is not what the fixes were written against; the configure stops naming the
wrapper's file and printing the new text's hash, then the change is reversed and the configure passes again. CMake
wraps a message's lines, so the command folds the output's whitespace.

````patch
diff --git a/deps/mquickjs/mquickjs.c b/deps/mquickjs/mquickjs.c
--- a/deps/mquickjs/mquickjs.c
+++ b/deps/mquickjs/mquickjs.c
@@ -2052,7 +2052,7 @@
     if (is_numeric < 0)
         return JS_EXCEPTION;
     
-    /* not found: add it in the table */
+    /* not found: add it to the table */
     JS_PUSH_VALUE(ctx, val);
     new_tab = js_resize_value_array(ctx, ctx->unique_strings,
                                  ctx->unique_strings_len + 1);
````

A variant that recompiles the firmware prints the SDK's `CFG_TUSB_OS redefined` warnings (`tusb_config.h` defines it and the SDK passes it on the command line); they are older than E4.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to the day the prototype's
hashes were taken against, 4 November 2026 (the command spells the string out), as the gate's record does
(`/tmp/e4pro/gate-commands.txt`); nothing else may differ, and the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the
date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash compares only an image built from this worktree's path,
against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check, `/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same
Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1: an image built elsewhere (the `env
-i` runs' clones under `/tmp/e4-ci`, a scratch worktree) is judged by its sizes, never hashed.

````bash
The bliptoaster pack and the box: the cart's MIDI policy as a TypeScript node

packages/bliptoaster is a device script pack with one node, rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy: no settings, events in and an
output that matches it, dropping poly and channel aftertouch, system common and real time and passing the rest as it
came, through forward. A twin test holds it to rp.core.midi-filter with the same list, message for message, on both
builds of each; its descriptor is a golden. Every desktop product lists it, last, so the products' registration rows
gain its type.

The block API gains forward(port, message), send of a message's frame, data and flags in one native call, on both script
hosts, and a definition may say idle: "skip": process does nothing on a block that brings no message and no control or
param change, so the host does not call it there, past its first block in each plan (a new plan sets each control
input's start afresh) and while no hook waits. defineNode refuses the flag on a layout with an audio port or with
nothing a block can bring it. The policy takes both.

The box's plan is rp.device.midi-in -> rp.bliptoaster.midi-policy -> rp.n8.nes (box-plan.hex re-recorded). The box
registers the pack at boot from the 32-bit source the desktop build's toolchain wrote (the build the exporter comes
from), on the device's MicroQuickJS host and engine (-Os, the 32-bit tables of the same standard library, a PRI shim,
abort wrapped to the Pico SDK's panic; setjmp and longjmp link as they are), one pack of one type. The bytecode stays in
flash (.flashdata) and setup copies it into the pack's memory in the arena, where it is relocated against the image's
own standard library. The host offers rp.host.clock/1 (10 ms a call, 250 us more for each message a block hands the
node). The arena is 64 KiB; the boot console says the pack's bytes, and after the first block its heap in use and how
long the load and that block took; a script node's fault is printed with its words.

A pack is bundled twice: whole, and as the device's runtime (RP_DEVICE_RUNTIME: defineNode keeps a definition's id,
create, layout and idle flag). Every node context on every host runs the runtime (the box's bytecode at 32 bits, the
desktop's at 64), and only the desktop's control context runs the whole pack (registration, descriptors, settings). The
toolchain lays every type out from both bundles on the engine and holds the layouts equal, and runs both bundles' nodes
through the same blocks (notes, full SysEx, and sweeps of every first byte) and holds their output equal.

heapBytes is the box's 32-bit context, which only the box measures (its boot line, the device check). A 64-bit device
build (the exporter's trial load, the device-mode tests) gives the toolchain check's 3/2 of it (kDeviceHalves), a
heuristic set under every 64/32 ratio measured. The desktop's hosts give a pack at least 1 MiB (allocated zeroed by
calloc), as its queues are the planner's 256 places and a re-plan holds two instances; a test re-plans the policy behind
a 256-place source. The exporter sizes a pack's memory at the target's width (rp_package_memory's query_target,
sizePlan's targetPointerBytes). devtest's heapBytes is 57344, the desktop tests' figure (its manifest says so).

rp.device.midi-in carries 64 messages a block (4 KB still), so the policy's pools hold 64 places; the box's staging and
UART ring follow it, and the cart link keeps 512 messages.

The engine's external names are renamed rp_mqjs_ (rp_mqjs_names.h, a check that the library defines no other), as a
product links it beside QuickJS. rp_mqjs_engine.c makes JS_MakeUniqueString collect before the growth that would drop
dead names under an insertion (a heap corruption in tight heaps), and marks a loaded bytecode's strings kept, so a name
made from one is not dropped while it stays marked unique. retroplug-mqjs-run-gc (the runner over a DEBUG_GC engine)
and a direct case hold the second, and hold send and forward to reading data that is no Uint8Array through a slot the
collector updates. A warmed block reads the host's arrays and message bytes in place, finds a port named by a bytecode
constant by value and skips a ready port's pool with no JS.

Three exceptions the engine drops are kept, by wrappers in rp_mqjs_engine.c: one a String.prototype.replace function
throws (js_string_replace ignores js_string_concat_subst's failure: every call reaches a wrapper that marks the
StringBuffer failed, as the engine's own appends do, and calls no function after), an out-of-memory in
string_buffer_puts (the same), and one a hasOwnProperty key's toString throws (our hasOwnProperty makes the key first).
The host holds every call into a node's context after its load (create, hooks and blocks) to 4 nested calls into
JavaScript on the C stack (RP_MQJS_MAX_REENTRIES, rp_mqjs_limit_reentries; the engine allows 8): at about 290 bytes a
level on the RP2350 the deepest chain then fits the box's 4 KB stack with room for its interrupts (2360 bytes measured,
with a malformed JSON text parsed at the last level, where 8 levels took 3320). The load, the desktop's control
context and the toolchain's script run keep the engine's 8, as the SDK's definitions nest deeper. The host makes a
block's arrays and views with the engine's own constructors, with no call into JavaScript and no global looked up, so
messages() works at the last level. cmake/mquickjs.cmake records every fix and hashes the upstream text each rests on
at configure: JS_MakeUniqueString, the sweep of unique_strings, replace and its substitution, the StringBuffer and its
appends, hasOwnProperty and the typed array's constructor, and it counts js_call_rec_count's mentions, which the cap
rests on.

The box's image runs with PICO_USE_STACK_GUARDS (core 0's MSPLIM): an overrun is a HardFault, after which the watchdog
restarts the box, rather than a silent write into SCRATCH_X. Every device image links cmake/device-image/no-unwind.c, a
strong __aeabi_unwind_cpp_pr0 that panics, in place of libgcc's ARM unwinder, which newlib's setjmp.o (the engine's
exceptions) pulled in through its unwind index for nothing: about 4 KB of the box's RAM (3840 bytes in its PIO build).

The scripttest pack gains four types: replace-throws and has-own-throws (each must fault "process threw: ..."),
spins-in (the deadline grows 250 us for each message on its events and bytes inputs, held by a scripted clock) and deep
(it reads and forwards its messages, SysEx among them, at the cap's depth, and sends the depth); the device-mode
objects' tables hold 32 types (RP_MQJS_MAX_TYPES).
EOF
````

### Task 4: rp-device-check with a script pack: a script plan, a bench and the stack in two phases

Design section 7 and section 8's fourth commit. `rp-device-check` carries the devtest script pack (its
`script-transpose` and a new `script-nest`) on the device's MicroQuickJS host, at a heap of the image's own (40960,
`RP_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES_devtest`), checks its two types with the C++ ones (22 types), and runs three new things after
E3's checks: a **bench** of the transpose (a first block, then 16 rounds of an empty block, 64 notes and 64 SysEx of 64
bytes, timed by the M33's cycle counter beside the XIP cache's counters), the **script plan**
(`script-plan.json`: `rp.device.midi-in` -> `script-transpose` -> `script-nest` -> `rp.devtest.digest`, exported at the
image's arena, rate and block and fed the runner's five-block stimulus through the device MIDI input), judged by its
digest against the desktop's exactly, with the pack's report; and the **stack in two phases**, the script plan's load
and its blocks each measured on a fresh paint and judged against the 4 KB stack with 512 bytes kept for interrupts. The
nest node nests `replace` callbacks to the re-entry cap, reads and forwards its messages there and parses JSON at the
deepest level, so the measure covers the deepest chain a node may build. The script plan runs last, so a stack overrun
there leaves every other line printed.

A red comes first, on Task 3's binary as it is. Then the nest node, the build (the heap variable, the plans, the
case generator, the size table), the check and the host's one accessor, and the tests, whose blob golden is a new file.

- [ ] **Step 2: `rp.devtest.script-nest`**

devtest's pack gains `rp.devtest.script-nest`, a pass-through with a `deep` setting (default false). With `deep` it
calls `"x".replace("x", down)` from inside the callback until the engine refuses the next re-entry (the cap of 4),
reads its messages with `messages()` at the deepest level and forwards every one but the real-time ones from there,
parses `"{"` as JSON so the measure covers the parser and a syntax error's backtrace, and faults unless it reached
exactly the cap: `replace`'s C frames between two calls are the largest on the M33 (about 288 bytes a level). The
manifest's description says the script pack's `heapBytes` (57344) is the desktop tests' figure and that an image
registering it behind a 64-place queue should give it about 40960 of its own (the toolchain's 3/2 check passes it,
with the nest, at 39792).

````diff
   },

+// How deep a node's calls into JavaScript may go on the C stack: the host's cap on a node's context
+// (graph-runtime's script/rp_mqjs.h, RP_MQJS_MAX_REENTRIES), the host's own call into process the first of them.
+const kReentries = 4;
+
+// A pass-through that, with `deep` set, does its block's work as deep in MicroQuickJS's C re-entries as the host lets
+// it. A native function that calls back into JavaScript enters the interpreter again through a nested JS_Call, on the C
+// stack, and the engine refuses a call past kReentries with an InternalError. String.prototype.replace with a function
+// is the native whose C frames between two calls are the largest (js_string_replace and js_string_concat_subst: 200
+// bytes on the RP2350 at -Os, where Array.prototype.forEach's js_array_every takes 64). Each block the node calls
+// replace from inside replace's callback until the engine refuses, and at the deepest level reads its messages (the
+// host's refill, a SysEx's array among it), forwards them and parses a malformed JSON text, whose parser and syntax
+// error are the deepest C chain a call there can make: what the device check measures its stack under
+// (packages/graph-runtime/device-check's script plan sets `deep`). The deepest is the level whose replace never
+// entered its callback; a throw from below it, or from the work there, goes on up, so the node faults. It faults too if
+// the host let it nest less or more deeply than kReentries. With `deep` set it passes on every message but the
+// real-time ones (F8 to FF), so a run that hears the deep path is told from one that does not; with `deep` off, the
+// default (the device check's run of each type, the toolchain's run), it passes every message on from process itself.
+export const scriptNestNode = defineNode({
+  id: "rp.devtest.script-nest",
+  name: "Script nest (devtest)",
+  category: "test",
+  settings: s.object({ deep: s.bool(false) }),
+  ports: { in: events.in(), out: events.out({ match: "in" }) },
+  create: ({ settings }) => {
+    const deep = settings.deep;
+    let block: Block | null = null;
+    let depth = 0;
+    let reached = 0;
+    let done = false;
+    const work = (b: Block): void => {
+      const messages = b.messages("in");
+      for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i++) if (messages[i].data[0] < 0xf8) b.forward("out", messages[i]);
+      try {
+        JSON.parse("{");
+      } catch (e) {
+        // The syntax error is the point: its parser and its error's backtrace run on the deepest chain.
+      }
+    };
+    const down = (): string => {
+      const at = ++depth;
+      if (at > reached) reached = at;
+      try {
+        "x".replace("x", down);
+      } catch (e) {
+        if (done || reached !== at) throw e;
+      }
+      if (!done && reached === at) {
+        done = true;
+        work(block as Block);
+      }
+      depth--;
+      return "";
+    };
+    return {
+      process(b) {
+        if (!deep) {
+          const shallow = b.messages("in");
+          for (let i = 0; i < shallow.length; i++) b.forward("out", shallow[i]);
+          return;
+        }
+        block = b;
+        depth = 0;
+        reached = 0;
+        done = false;
+        down();
+        block = null;
+        if (reached !== kReentries) throw new Error(`nested ${reached} deep, where the host allows ${kReentries}`);
+      },
+    };
+  },
+});
+
+registerScriptNodes([scriptTransposeNode, scriptNestNode]);
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The build: the image's own heap, the script plan, the cases and the size table**

`cmake/packages.cmake`: `RP_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES_<package>` gives a device image's registration a copy of the pack's
source with that heap (a whole number from 4096 to 524288, filled at the call with no static constructor), and is
refused in words wherever it would size nothing: a package with no script pack (`RP_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES_<package> is
set, but the package has no script pack (its manifest's retroplug.script) for it to size`), and a build that registers
none, a desktop build or a device build without `RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR`; `retroplug_product`'s `NO_SCRIPTS` is gone,
its one user being the case generator. The check's `CMakeLists.txt` derives `RP_DESKTOP_BUILD_DIR` from
`RP_EXPORT_PLAN_TOOL`, as the box does, sets devtest's heap from `RP_DEVICE_CHECK_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES`
(`packages.cmake`, 40960), and exports both plans in one loop (`DeviceCheckPlan.hpp`, `DeviceCheckScriptPlan.hpp`);
`plan.cmake` holds `script-plan.json` (the transpose at `semitones` 7, the nest at `deep: true`, the digest on events
only). The case generator sets each package's memory up in memory of its own, so a script type can be created, and
writes a script type's events and bytes ports at the device MIDI input's 64 / 4096. `tools/build-device-check.sh`'s
size table gains the owners "devtest: the script pack", "graph-runtime: MicroQuickJS" and "graph-runtime: the script
host".

Create `packages/graph-runtime/device-check/script-plan.json`:

````json
{"nodes":[
    {"id":"in","type":"rp.device.midi-in"},
    {"id":"tp","type":"rp.devtest.script-transpose","settings":{"semitones":7}},
    {"id":"nest","type":"rp.devtest.script-nest","settings":{"deep":true}},
    {"id":"dg","type":"rp.devtest.digest"}],
  "wires":[
    {"from":"in.midi","to":"tp.in"},
    {"from":"tp.out","to":"nest.in"},
    {"from":"nest.out","to":"dg.events"}]}
````

Expected: nothing: the range is this block's diff and it applies cleanly. Run the same range without `--check` to apply it, which keeps trailing whitespace in context lines exactly as the prototype has it.

- [ ] **Step 4: The check: the bench, the script plan, the pack's report and the stack's two phases**

`DeviceCheck.{hpp,cpp}`: the check's host answers `rp.host.packages/1` (`openPackage()` / `closePackage()`),
`rp.host.clock/1` (`offerClock()`; the image offers `time_us_64`, so the box's deadline applies) and
`rp.device.midi-in/1`, which hands out the stimulus for the block `runPlan` staged: the runner's five-block cycle at
the queue's capacity (64 notes; 64 SysEx of 64 bytes; two sweeps of 63; a block of none), without empty messages or
flags, which midi-in carries neither of. `run()` sets a script type's package memory up first (`Step::Package`,
appended), takes an out-param form and names a script fault's words in a Process failure. `PlanCase` gains the
stimulus, an exact digest to expect, the context and the cycle counter, and an `afterLoad` hook; `PlanResult` gains
the messages, the load's and the first block's cycles and up to two pack reports; `PlanStep::Heap` is appended.
`benchScript()` binds the transpose into a one-step plan with its memory in the arena and times the rounds. `main.cpp`
runs each check in a small never-inlined function and prints in another (so the deepest chain runs on a base close to
the box's), starts the DWT cycle counter, and runs, in order, the types, the N8 protocol, the plan, the bench, then
the script plan on a repainted stack (its load's high-water mark read and the stack repainted in `afterLoad`), then
the overall stack line; a stack phase that leaves under 512 bytes blinks 39, the script plan's steps 30 + the step and
the bench's 40 + the step. `MqjsHost` gains `stateBytes()` for the pack line.

````diff
+std::uint32_t messageOf(std::uint8_t first, std::uint8_t* out) {
+    out[0] = first;

+// The type's package's memory (a script pack's context), placed in the arena and set up, which the host offers its

+struct PackageScope {

+    Step take(Arena& a, const rp_package& package, rp_error* err) {

+    }

+std::uint32_t stimulusCount(std::uint32_t block) {
+    switch (block % kStimulusCycle) {
+        case 0: return RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES;
+        case 1: return RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES / 64;
+        case 4: return 0;
+        default: return RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES - 1;
+    }
+}
+
+std::uint32_t stimulusMessage(std::uint32_t block, std::uint32_t k, std::uint32_t frames, std::uint8_t* out,
+                              std::uint32_t* frame) {
+    switch (block % kStimulusCycle) {
+        case 0:
+            *frame = k * frames / RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES;
+            out[0] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(k % 2 ? 0x80 : 0x90);
+            out[1] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(48 + (block + k) % 24);
+            out[2] = 100;
+            return 3;
+        case 1:
+            *frame = k * frames * 64 / RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES;
+            std::memset(out, 0, 64);
+            out[0] = 0xF0;
+            out[1] = 0x7D;
+            out[63] = 0xF7;
+            return 64;
+        default: {
+            const std::uint32_t sweep = block / kStimulusCycle * 2 + (block % kStimulusCycle - 2);
+            *frame = (k + 1) / 2 * (frames / 32);
+            return messageOf(static_cast<std::uint8_t>((sweep * (RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES - 1) + k) % 256), out);
+        }
+    }
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The tests: the check's script steps on the desktop, and the script plan's blob golden**

`DeviceCheck.test.cpp` registers the pack as the image does, through a copy of its source at the image's heap
(`DeviceModeEntries.hpp` declares `rp_devmode::mqjs`'s pieces and scripttest's registrations), and its eight new
`[device-mode][device-check][script-pack]` cases hold: the registration at the image's heap (types, memory at this
width and the box's, the cases' queues); a script type whose memory does not fit and a 4096 heap refused at setup; the
script plan (allocating nothing, 4 nodes, 40 blocks, 2032 messages, 0 drops, its digest pinned to `0xc7248a64d500e6d8`
on every host, the context 3/2 x 40960, the arena equal to the estimate at this width); its golden; its failure steps,
each with its words (a wrong context, a wrong digest, a heap running out, no stimulus); the bench (allocating nothing,
13 blocks, 512 messages, all passed) and its failure steps; and a spinning node faulting by a clock the host offers (1
ms a reading) with the deadline's words. The "carries every device entry" case accepts a script pack's entry,
`tests.cmake` lists script entries with their sources, gives the device-mode objects `RP_MQJS_MAX_PACKS=16` and
exports the script plan with the image's arguments, and `ScriptPack.test.cpp` pins devtest's two types.
**`golden/device-check-script-plan.hex` is a new file, not a re-recording**: the script plan's 864-byte blob as hex,
recorded once by the prototype (`RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE=1` is what records it, and no step here sets it), placed from its
text and held to its blob hash; `plan-blob.hex`, `box-plan.hex` and `device-check-plan.hex` are unchanged.

````diff
+// A script pack as the image registers it (the device check's CMakeLists.txt): its source with the image's own heap,
+// RP_DEVICE_CHECK_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES, in place of its manifest's, on the device-mode build of the host. The copy lives
+// as long as the binary, as the host keys a pack on its source's address. `heapBytes` gives another figure.
+const rp_package* imageScriptPackage(const rp_mqjs_pack_source& source,
+                                     std::uint32_t heapBytes = RP_DEVICE_CHECK_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES) {
+    static std::deque<rp_mqjs_pack_source> copies;
+    const rp_mqjs_pack_source*             copy = nullptr;
+    for (const rp_mqjs_pack_source& c : copies)
+        if (c.bytecode == source.bytecode && c.heap_bytes == heapBytes) copy = &c;
+    if (!copy) {
+        copies.push_back(source);
+        copies.back().heap_bytes = heapBytes;
+        copy = &copies.back();
+    }
+    const rp_package* p = rp_devmode::mqjs::package(*copy);
+    INFO(rp_devmode::mqjs::packageRefusal());
+    REQUIRE(p);
+    return p;
+}

+// The source of the image's script pack (its one), as its manifest built it.
+const rp_mqjs_pack_source& imageScriptSource() {
+    for (const CheckedEntry& e : checkedEntries())
+        if (e.script) return *e.script;
+    FAIL("the device check's cases name no script pack");
+    throw;
+}
+
+// The image's script pack, on the device-mode build, at the image's heap or `heapBytes`.
+const rp_package* imageScriptPack(std::uint32_t heapBytes = RP_DEVICE_CHECK_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES) {
+    return imageScriptPackage(imageScriptSource(), heapBytes);
+}

+constexpr std::size_t kImageContextBytes =
+    std::size_t{RP_DEVICE_CHECK_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES} * rp::mqjs::kDeviceHalves / 2;

+// ---- the script pack ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

+namespace {
+
+using rp::device_check::BenchResult;
+using rp::device_check::BenchStep;
+
+const std::vector<std::uint8_t> kScriptPlanBlob(std::begin(kDeviceCheckScriptPlan), std::end(kDeviceCheckScriptPlan));
+
+// The export's estimate for the script plan at this width. The exporter sizes a pack's memory at the box's width from
+// its manifest's heap (boxPackageBytes; MqjsHost.hpp), and the image's own is what its registration gives: so on the
+// image the estimate holds the pack's memory with the room between the two heaps, and here the pack's memory at this
+// width stands in for the box's (as BoxHost.test.cpp's arena does for the box's plan).
+std::size_t scriptPlanEstimate() {
+    const rp_package* pack = imageScriptPack();
+    rp_memory_req     req{};
+    rp_error          err{};
+    REQUIRE(pack->memory->query(pack, &req, &err));
+    return kDeviceCheckScriptPlanArenaEstimate - rp::mqjs::boxPackageBytes(imageScriptSource()) + req.size;
+}
+
+// The image's script plan case (main.cpp's kScriptPlan) over `blob`, its context held to this width's figure for the
+// image's heap, its arena to the export's estimate at this width, untimed (the desktop has no cycle counter the check
+// reads).
+PlanCase scriptPlanCase(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& blob = kScriptPlanBlob) {
+    PlanCase c;
+    c.blob = blob.data();
+    c.blobSize = blob.size();
+    c.arenaEstimate = scriptPlanEstimate();
+    c.frames = rp::device_check::kScriptPlanFrames;
+    c.splits = rp::device_check::kScriptPlanSplits;
+    c.splitCount = std::size(rp::device_check::kScriptPlanSplits);
+    c.digest = rp::device_check::kScriptPlanDigest;
+    c.stimulus = true;
+    c.expectDigest = true;
+    c.want = rp::device_check::kScriptPlanWant;
+    c.contextBytes = kImageContextBytes;
+    return c;
+}
+
+// `packages` with the image's script pack replaced by `pack`.
+std::vector<const rp_package*> withScriptPack(const rp_package* pack) {
+    std::vector<const rp_package*> packages = devicePackages();
+    for (const rp_package*& p : packages)
+        if (p->memory) p = pack;
+    return packages;
+}
+
+// The messages the stimulus hands a run of `blocks` blocks.
+std::uint32_t stimulusMessages(std::uint32_t blocks) {
+    std::uint32_t n = 0;
+    for (std::uint32_t b = 0; b < blocks; ++b) n += rp::device_check::stimulusCount(b);
+    return n;
+}
+
+struct BenchRun {
+    BenchResult result{};
+    int         allocations = -1;
+};
+
+// benchScript as the image runs it, untimed, in an arena of `arenaBytes` made before counting starts.
+BenchRun runBench(const std::vector<const rp_package*>& packages, const std::vector<TypeCase>& cases = kAllCases,
+                  std::size_t arenaBytes = rp::device_check::kArenaBytes, std::uint32_t rounds = 4) {
+    BenchRun                      r;
+    std::vector<std::max_align_t> arena(arenaBytes / sizeof(std::max_align_t) + 1);
+    rp::test::beginCountingAllocations(rp::test::countsCAllocations());
+    rp::device_check::benchScript(packages.data(), packages.size(), cases.data(), cases.size(), arena.data(),
+                                  arenaBytes, rounds, nullptr, &r.result);
+    r.allocations = rp::test::endCountingAllocations().allocations;
+    return r;
+}
+

+TEST_CASE("the device check registers the devtest script pack with the image's heap, and checks its types with the "
+          "rest",
+          "[device-mode][device-check][script-pack]") {
+    const rp_package* pack = imageScriptPack();
+    REQUIRE(pack->memory);
+    CHECK(std::string(pack->memory->name) == "devtest");
+    CHECK(idsOf(pack) == std::vector<std::string>{"rp.devtest.script-transpose", "rp.devtest.script-nest"});
+    rp_memory_req req{};
+    rp_error      err{};
+    REQUIRE(pack->memory->query(pack, &req, &err));
+    // Its memory is the host's state, the bytecode's copy and a context of the image's figure at this width.
+    CHECK(req.size > kImageContextBytes);
+    CHECK(req.size < kImageContextBytes + 64 * 1024);
+    // At the box's width, the image's figure exactly beside the state and the 32-bit bytecode.
+    REQUIRE(pack->memory->query_target);
+    rp_memory_req box{};
+    REQUIRE(pack->memory->query_target(pack, 4, &box, &err));
+    CHECK(box.size > RP_DEVICE_CHECK_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES);
+    CHECK(box.size < std::size_t{RP_DEVICE_CHECK_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES} + 32 * 1024);
+
+    // Its cases: a script type's message queues are the device MIDI input's, whatever the planner's default.
+    std::size_t scriptCases = 0;
+    for (const TypeCase& c : kAllCases) {
+        if (std::string(c.id).rfind("rp.devtest.script-", 0) != 0) continue;
+        ++scriptCases;
+        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < c.portCount; ++i) {
+            INFO(c.id << " port " << i);
+            CHECK(c.ports[i].messages == RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_MESSAGES);
+            CHECK(c.ports[i].bytes == RP_DEVICE_MIDI_IN_BYTES);
+        }
+    }
+    CHECK(scriptCases == 2);
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("the device check stops at a script type whose package memory does not fit, and names it",
+          "[device-mode][device-check][script-pack]") {
+    std::vector<TypeCase> cases;
+    for (const TypeCase& c : kAllCases)
+        if (std::string(c.id).rfind("rp.devtest.script-", 0) == 0) cases.push_back(c);
+    REQUIRE(cases.size() == 2);
+    const Result fits = runCheck({imageScriptPack()}, cases);
+    INFO(fits.error.message);
+    CHECK(fits.step == Step::Ok);
+    CHECK(fits.types == 2);
+    // The pack's memory takes the most of any type's run: the context and the bytecode's copy, beside its nodes.
+    CHECK(fits.arenaBytes > kImageContextBytes);
+
+    const Result r = runCheck({imageScriptPack()}, cases, 16 * 1024);
+    CHECK(r.step == Step::Package);
+    CHECK(std::string(r.id) == "rp.devtest.script-transpose");
+    CHECK(std::string(r.error.message) == "the package's memory does not fit the arena");
+
+    // A context too small for the pack's runtime to define its nodes in: its setup refuses, in its words.
+    const Result small = runCheck({imageScriptPack(4096)}, cases);
+    CHECK(small.step == Step::Package);
+    CHECK(std::string(small.error.message).find("devtest") != std::string::npos);
+}

+TEST_CASE("the device check's script plan runs the stimulus through two script nodes behind the device MIDI input, "
+          "to the digest the image holds it to, in the image's arena, allocating nothing",
+          "[device-mode][device-check][script-pack]") {
+    REQUIRE(rp_devtest_plan_live_device_mode() == 0);
+    const PlanRun run = runPlanCase(scriptPlanCase(), devicePackages());
+    const PlanResult& r = run.result;
+    INFO(describe(r) << "; the digest 0x" << std::hex << r.digest << std::dec);
+    REQUIRE(r.step == PlanStep::Ok);
+    CHECK(run.allocations == 0);
+    CHECK(run.frees == 0);
+    CHECK(run.alive == 0);
+    CHECK(r.nodes == 4);
+    CHECK(r.frames == rp::device_check::kScriptPlanFrames);
+    CHECK(r.blocks == 40);
+    CHECK(r.messages == stimulusMessages(40));
+    CHECK(r.drops == 0);
+    CHECK(r.digestBlocks == r.blocks);
+    CHECK(r.heard);
+    // Its digest is of messages alone, integers the script nodes made, so it is the same on every host: the figure the
+    // image holds the RP2350's run to (DeviceCheck.hpp), pinned everywhere.
+    CHECK(r.digest == rp::device_check::kScriptPlanWant);
+    // Its one pack, at the image's heap, with what the run left in it.
+    INFO("the pack: " << r.packs[0].inUseBytes << " of " << r.packs[0].contextBytes << " bytes in use at this width, "
+                      << r.packs[0].memoryBytes << " placed; " << r.arenaBytes << " arena bytes");
+    REQUIRE(r.packCount == 1);
+    CHECK(std::string(r.packs[0].name) == "devtest");
+    CHECK(r.packs[0].contextBytes == kImageContextBytes);
+    CHECK(r.packs[0].memoryBytes > r.packs[0].contextBytes);
+    CHECK(r.packs[0].fixedBytes > 0);
+    CHECK(r.packs[0].inUseBytes > r.packs[0].fixedBytes);
+    CHECK(r.packs[0].inUseBytes < r.packs[0].contextBytes);
+    // The estimate at this width is this width's layout exactly, as the main plan's is; the image's 32-bit layout,
+    // with a pack's memory under the manifest's heap's, is under the export's own figure.
+    CHECK(r.arenaBytes == scriptPlanEstimate());
+    CHECK(rp::mqjs::boxPackageBytes(imageScriptSource()) > std::size_t{RP_DEVICE_CHECK_SCRIPT_HEAP_BYTES});
+}

+TEST_CASE("the device check's script plan is its golden's bytes, as the image's build exports and embeds it",
+          "[device-mode][device-check][script-pack]") {
+    std::string hex;
+    char        digits[3];
+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kScriptPlanBlob.size(); ++i) {
+        std::snprintf(digits, sizeof digits, "%02x", kScriptPlanBlob[i]);
+        hex += digits;
+        hex += (i % 32 == 31 || i + 1 == kScriptPlanBlob.size()) ? '\n' : ' ';
+    }
+    const std::filesystem::path golden =
+        std::filesystem::path(RP_DEVICE_MODE_GOLDEN_DIR) / "device-check-script-plan.hex";
+    if (const char* update = std::getenv("RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE"); update && std::string(update) == "1") {
+        std::ofstream(golden, std::ios::binary) << hex;
+        WARN("recorded " << golden.string());
+    }
+    std::ifstream     in(golden, std::ios::binary);
+    const std::string want((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
+    CHECK(want == hex);
+}

+TEST_CASE("the device check's script plan check stops at the step that fails, and says why",
+          "[device-mode][device-check][script-pack]") {
+    REQUIRE(rp_devtest_plan_live_device_mode() == 0);
+
+    SECTION("a pack whose context is not the image's figure") {
+        PlanCase c = scriptPlanCase();
+        c.contextBytes = kImageContextBytes + 8;
+        const PlanRun run = runPlanCase(c, devicePackages());
+        CHECK(run.result.step == PlanStep::Heap);
+        CHECK(std::string(run.result.error.node) == "-");
+        CHECK(std::string(run.result.error.message) ==
+              "a script pack's context is not the size the case says its image declares");
+        CHECK(run.result.packCount == 1);
+        CHECK(run.alive == 0);
+    }
+    SECTION("a digest that is not the desktop's") {
+        PlanCase c = scriptPlanCase();
+        c.want = rp::device_check::kScriptPlanWant ^ 1;
+        const PlanRun run = runPlanCase(c, devicePackages());
+        CHECK(run.result.step == PlanStep::Result);
+        CHECK(std::string(run.result.error.node) == "dg");
+        CHECK(std::string(run.result.error.message) == "the digest is not the one the case expects");
+        CHECK(run.alive == 0);
+    }
+    SECTION("a pack whose heap runs out: the script node's fault, in its words") {
+        const PlanRun run = runPlanCase(scriptPlanCase(), withScriptPack(imageScriptPack(12288)));
+        INFO(describe(run.result));
+        CHECK(run.result.step == PlanStep::Process);
+        CHECK(run.result.blocks == 1);
+        const std::string message = run.result.error.message;
+        CHECK(message.rfind("the block faulted the node: ", 0) == 0);
+        CHECK(message.find("heap") != std::string::npos);
+        CHECK(run.alive == 0);
+        CHECK(run.allocations == 0);
+    }
+    SECTION("a plan without the stimulus: the digest hears nothing") {
+        PlanCase c = scriptPlanCase();
+        c.stimulus = false;
+        const PlanRun run = runPlanCase(c, devicePackages());
+        CHECK(run.result.step == PlanStep::Result);
+        CHECK(run.result.messages == 0);
+        CHECK(std::string(run.result.error.message) == "the digest heard nothing but silence");
+    }
+}

+    CHECK(r.contextBytes == kImageContextBytes);
+    CHECK(r.inUseBytes > 0);
+    CHECK(r.inUseBytes < r.contextBytes);
+    // Untimed here: the desktop passes no counter.
+    CHECK(r.firstCycles == 0);
+    CHECK(r.noteCycles == 0);
+}

+TEST_CASE("the device check's host gives a script node the clock the image offers, by which a node past its deadline "
+          "faults, in its words",
+          "[device-mode][device-check][script-pack]") {
+    // rp.scripttest.spins, which never returns, in a plan of its own; its pack at a heap the image's arena holds.
+    const rp_package*       pack = imageScriptPackage(rp_script_scripttest, 65536);
+    rp::graph::NodeRegistry registry;
+    std::string             why;
+    REQUIRE(registry.addPackage(rp_scripttest_script_package(), &why));
+    std::vector<const rp_package*> types = devicePackages();
+    types.push_back(pack);
+    rp::graph::ExportOptions o;
+    o.sampleRate = 48000.0;
+    o.maxFrames = 256;
+    o.arenaBytes = rp::device_check::kArenaBytes;
+    o.trialLoad = false;  // the exporter's own deadline would fault it first
+    const auto exported =
+        rp::graph::exportPlan(R"({"nodes":[{"id":"sp","type":"rp.scripttest.spins"}],"wires":[]})", registry, types, o);
+    REQUIRE(exported.ok());
+
+    // A clock a millisecond further on at each reading, as the engine polls it while the node spins: the image's
+    // (time_us_64) by the host's figure, kHostClockDeadlineMicros, as a block that hands the node no message has it.
+    struct Ticks {
+        static std::uint64_t read(void* ctx) { return *static_cast<std::uint64_t*>(ctx) += 1000; }
+    };
+    std::uint64_t       now = 0;
+    const rp_host_clock clock{&now, &Ticks::read, 0};
+    // Offered for this case alone: taken back as it ends, however it ends, so no later case meets a clock of this
+    // frame's.
+    struct Offered {
+        explicit Offered(const rp_host_clock* c) { rp::device_check::offerClock(c); }
+        ~Offered() { rp::device_check::offerClock(nullptr); }
+    } offered(&clock);
+    PlanCase c;
+    c.blob = exported.blob.data();
+    c.blobSize = exported.blob.size();
+    c.frames = 256;
+    const PlanRun run = runPlanCase(c, types);
+    INFO(describe(run.result));
+    CHECK(run.result.step == PlanStep::Process);
+    CHECK(std::string(run.result.error.node) == "sp");
+    CHECK(std::string(run.result.error.message) ==
+          "the block faulted the node: process ran past its deadline of " +
+              std::to_string(rp::mqjs::kHostClockDeadlineMicros) + " us");
+    CHECK(run.result.blocks == 1);
+    CHECK(run.allocations == 0);
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to the day the prototype's
hashes were taken against, 4 November 2026 (the command spells the string out), as the gate's record does
(`/tmp/e4pro/gate-commands.txt`); nothing else may differ, and the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the
date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash compares only an image built from this worktree's path,
against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check, `/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same
Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and `arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1: an image built elsewhere (the `env
-i` runs' clones under `/tmp/e4-ci`, a scratch worktree) is judged by its sizes, never hashed.

````diff
-**Registration.** A pack's bytecode, run once, defines its nodes with `defineNode`. The host makes one `rp_node_type`
````
